Since pains are remedies for souls and bodies, they are a form of perfection for living beings, especially for the human species. Indeed, its Originator and Creator made it ill only to heal it, tested it only to grant it well-being, and caused it to die only to bring it to life. He, glorified is He, drives animals and humans through the stages of their perfection, stage after stage, until their final perfection, by means that are unavoidable, and their perfection depends upon those means. The existence of a necessitated thing without its necessary consequence is impossible, just as the existence of a created being without need, poverty, deficiency, and the consequences of these is impossible, and the consequences of those consequences as well. But most souls are ignorant of God, His wisdom, His knowledge, and His perfection, so they posit things that are impossible and conceive them mentally, supposing them to be more perfect than the actual existing world. Yet despite this, He may show mercy to them because of their ignorance, weakness, and deficiency. If they acknowledge this and acknowledge to Him His perfection and praiseworthiness, and act according to the requirements of these two acknowledgments, their share of mercy will be greater. God, glorified is He, opened creation with praise and concluded the affair of this world with praise, so He said: ﴿All praise is due to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾, and He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said: "All praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds."﴾

He sent down His Book with praise, legislated His religion with praise, and made obligatory its reward and punishment with praise. His praise is among the necessary consequences of His essence, for it is impossible for Him to be other than praiseworthy. Praise is the cause of creation and its goal: He made it obligatory, and creation came into being for praise. So His praise is as vast as His knowledge and mercy encompass, and our Lord has encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge. He did not bring anything into existence, decree it, or legislate it except with His praise and for His praise. Everything He created and legislated includes praiseworthy ends, and their necessary consequences and the consequences of those consequences are unavoidable. For this reason His praise has filled His heavens and His earth, what is between them, and whatever else of things He has created and will create after this creation. His praise fills all of that.

His praise, exalted is He, is of several kinds: praise for His lordship, praise for His sole possession of it, praise for His divinity and His uniqueness in it, praise for His blessing, praise for His favor, praise for His wisdom, praise for His justice in His creation, praise for His independence from having a child, a partner, or an ally out of humiliation, and praise for His perfection, which is not fitting for anyone else. He is praiseworthy in every state, at every moment and breath, for everything He does, everything He legislates, for every attribute He has, for everything from which He is exempt, and for everything in existence, good and evil, pleasure and pain, well-being and trial. Just as the entire dominion belongs to Him, all power belongs to Him, all might belongs to Him, all knowledge belongs to Him, all beauty belongs to Him, all praise belongs to Him, as in the transmitted supplication: "O God, to You belongs all praise, to You belongs all dominion, in Your hand is all good, to You all affairs return, and You are worthy to be praised."

The world was not made prosperous except by His praise, nor was Paradise, nor was Hell, to such an extent that its inhabitants praise Him, as al-Hasan said: "The people of the Fire will enter the Fire, and their hearts will still praise Him for what they find of proof and no way out."

(Benefit)

From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light. And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the taghut; they bring them out of light into darkness.﴾

He made "light," which is His path, singular, and made "darknesses," which are the path of Satan, plural.

Whoever understands this understands the secret of using the singular for light and the plural for darknesses in His saying: ﴿All praise is due to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾, although there is a subtler secret than this, which is known to one who knows the source of light, whence it flows, from what it arises, and that its origin is entirely one. As for darknesses, they are many, multiplied by the multiplicity of the veils that produce them, and they are very numerous: each veil has its own darkness. Darknesses do not return to the Guiding Light, exalted is His majesty, in any respect, neither in attribute, essence, name, nor act; they return only to His created effects, glorified is He. So He is the One who makes darknesses, and their effects are many and multiplied. Light, by contrast, returns to His name and attribute, exalted is His majesty, "exalted above having anything like Him, and He is the Light of the heavens and the earth."

Ibn Mas'ud said: "With your Lord there is no night or day; the light of the heavens and the earth is from the light of His Face." Narrated by al-Darimi from him.

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dharr: I said, "O Messenger of God, did you see your Lord?" He said: "Light; how could I see Him?"

The point is that the path to God, exalted is He, is one, for He is the manifest Truth, and Truth is one, its return is to one.

As for falsehood and error, they are not confined; rather, everything other than Him is false, and every path to falsehood is false. Falsehood is multiple, and its paths are multiple.

As for what occurs in the words of some scholars, that the paths to God are many and diverse, which God made so according to the diversity and variance of readiness, out of His mercy and grace, this is correct and does not contradict what we have mentioned about the unity of the path.

The clarification of this: the path is one, comprising everything that pleases God, and what pleases Him is many and diverse. All that pleases Him is one path, while His pleasures are multiple and diverse according to times, places, persons, and states, and all of them are paths to His good pleasure. These which God has made for His mercy and wisdom are very many and varied, because the readiness and receptivity of His servants differ. Had He made them one kind, given the differences of minds and intellects and the strength or weakness of readiness, only one person after another would have walked them. But because readiness differs, the paths have become diverse, so that each person journeys to his Lord by a path that suits his readiness, strength, and acceptance.

From here the diversity of the Sharia and its variation is known, even though all of them return to one religion; indeed, the variety of one Sharia is known together with the unity of the Worshipped One and His religion. From this is the well-known hadith: "The prophets are sons of one father (ʿallāt); their religion is one."

"Awlad al-ʿallat" means that the father is one while the mothers are many. So the religion of the prophets is likened to the one father, and their laws to the many mothers, for although they are many, all of them return to one father.

Once this is known, some people make the path of knowledge and teaching the chief of their work and the way they consider their journey to God, having devoted their time seeking the face of God. They remain devoted to the path of knowledge and teaching until they reach God through that path and an особый opening is granted them therein, or they die on the path of their seeking, and it is hoped that they will attain their goal after death.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to God and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has fallen upon God﴾ [al-Nisa': 100].

It has been related of a large group whom death overtook while they were eagerly seeking the Qur'an that they were seen after their death and informed that they were completing their pursuit and learning in the barzakh, for a servant dies upon what he lived upon.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾. It is known that they did not make these equal to Him, glorified is He, in creating, providing, causing death and life, dominion, or power; they made them equal to Him only in love, in worshipping, in submission to them and abasement before them. This is the extreme of ignorance and injustice. How can dust be equated with the Lord of lords? How can slaves be equated with the Owner of necks? How can the poor in essence, the weak in essence, the incapable in essence, the needy in essence, whose own essence holds nothing but non-existence, be equated with the Self-Sufficient in essence, the Capable in essence, whose independence, power, dominion, existence, beneficence, knowledge, mercy, and absolute complete perfection are necessary consequences of His essence?

What injustice is more hideous than this? What judgment is more grossly unjust than this? In that He equalized with His creation One who has no equal, as He said: ﴿All praise is due to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾.

The polytheist equalized with Him Him who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light, with one who possesses not even an atom's weight for himself or for others in the heavens or on earth. What a justice that contains the greatest and most hideous injustice!

It is said: His saying "yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord" means they set up others as equals to Him in worship, which is love and exaltation. This is the more correct of the two views.

It is also said: the bāʾ (in bi-rabbihim) means "from" ('an), and the meaning is: those who disbelieve turn away from their Lord, swerving from His worship to the worship of another. This is not strong, for the Arabs do not say "adaltu bi-kadhā" meaning "I turned away from it." This usage appears only with the verb "to ask," as in "sa'altu bi-kadhā," meaning "about it"; as if they included in it the sense of "I cared for it and was concerned with it," and similar.

(Section)

His saying: ﴿yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ means they liken Him to others and equate Him with others in divinity and worship. Every innovation and corrupt doctrine in the religions of the messengers has its root in faulty analogy. The Jahmiyya denied the attributes and actions of the Lord, His elevation above His creation, His istiwa' over His Throne, His speech and His speaking to His servants, and His being seen in the Hereafter, only through faulty analogy. The Qadariyya denied the all-encompassing scope of His power and will, and placed in His dominion what He does not will, and claimed that He wills what does not come to be, only through faulty analogy. The Rafida went astray, showed enmity toward the best of creation, declared the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ unbelievers, and reviled them, only through faulty analogy. The zindiqs and the materialists denied the resurrection of bodies, the splitting of the heavens, the folding up of this world, and held that the world is eternal, only through faulty analogy. Whatever corruption has befallen the affairs of the world and whatever ruin has come upon it, came only through faulty analogy. The first sin by which God was disobeyed was faulty analogy, and it was what brought upon Adam and his descendants what it brought from the one who held this analogy. So the root of all the evil of this world and the Hereafter comes from this faulty analogy. This wisdom is understood only by one who has insight into what is obligatory and what actually is, and who has understanding of the Sharia and of divine decree.

(Another Section)

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿All praise is due to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾.

That is, they ascribe others as equal to Him, thus attributing to His creation a equal and a likeness.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He means they made equal to Me, from My creation, stones and idols, after acknowledging My blessing and My lordship.

Al-Zajjaj said: God, glorified is He, informed that He is the Creator of what is mentioned in this verse, and that its Creator has nothing like Him, and informed that the disbelievers make equals to Him. "Adl" means equalization; one says "adala al-shay' bi al-shay'" when he makes one thing equal to another. The meaning of "yaʿdilūna bihi" is that they associate others with Him.

Mujahid said, quoting al-Ahmar: It is said "'adala al-kafir bi-rabbihi 'adlan wa 'udulan" when he equates others with his Lord and worships them.

Al-Kisa'i said: "'adaltu al-shay' bi al-shay'" means "a'diluhu 'udulan," when I make it equal to it.

Similarly His saying about these likeners, that they will say in the Fire to their gods: ﴿By God, we were indeed in clear error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 97-98].

They confessed that they were in the greatest and clearest error, for they made equals and likenesses to God from His creation, equating them with Him in worship and exaltation.

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know anyone equal to Him?﴾ [Maryam: 65].

Ibn 'Abbas said: "A likeness and an equal, one who is comparable to Him."

That is a denial, of creatures being like the Creator and equal to Him in such a way as to deserve worship and exaltation. He did not say, glorified is He, "Do you know Him to be a namesake, or a likeness to another," for no one has said this. Rather, the polytheistic likeners made some created things similar to Him, comparable, equal, and peers, and so this likening and equalizing was rejected.

Likewise His saying: ﴿They worship besides God that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens and earth, nor are they able. So do not strike for God examples﴾ [al-Nahl: 73-74].

He forbade them to strike for Him examples drawn from His creation, and He did not forbid them to strike Him as an example for His creation, for no one has said this, nor did they do it. For God, exalted, is greater and mightier and more magnificent than anything in the natural disposition of all people. But the polytheistic likeners exaggerate regarding those they venerate, so they liken them to the Creator, whereas God, exalted is He, is too great in the hearts of all creatures to have anyone else made a principle alongside Him, and then they liken Him, glorified is He, to something else.

And consider how the heavens are mentioned in plural form in His words, "And He is Allah in the heavens and in the earth; He knows your secret and your open declaration" (﴿وَهُوَ اللَّهُ في السَّماواتِ وفي الأرْضِ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكم وجَهْرَكُمْ﴾).

For it has come in the plural here for an evident wisdom, namely that the adverbial phrase ("in the heavens and in the earth") is connected to what is contained in His name, blessed and exalted, of the meaning of divinity (ulūhiyyah). The meaning is: He is the God (al-Ilah), He is the one worshipped (al-Ma'bud) in each one of the heavens, and in each one of this kind He is the one who is worshipped (al-Ma'lūh). Mentioning the plural here is more eloquent and better than limiting it to the singular generic term. When this meaning escaped the understanding of some of the Mutasannin (those who anthropomorphize, al-Mutasannah), he explained the verse in a way that does not befit it, saying: "The complete pause is on 'the heavens', then he begins with His words, 'And in the earth He knows...'" He thereby erred in understanding the verse, whereas its meaning is what I have told you, and this is the view of the verifying scholars of tafsir (muhaqqiqī ahl al-tafsir).

The polytheists said, out of obstinacy in their disbelief: ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him?﴾ They meant: an angel that we can see and witness, who would testify to him and confirm him. Otherwise, the angel was already descending upon him with revelation from God. God answered this and explained the wisdom behind not sending down an angel in the form they had proposed. If He had sent down an angel as they proposed, and they still did not believe or confirm him, they would be hastened to punishment, as God's custom continued with the disbelievers regarding the signs they demanded: when those signs came to them and they did not believe in them. So He said: ﴿And had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved.﴾ Then God, glory be to Him, explained that if He had sent down an angel as they proposed, their aim would still not have been achieved. If He sent him in his own form, they would not be able to receive from him, since humans cannot address an angel or be in direct contact with him. The Prophet (ﷺ), though he was the strongest of creation, when the angel descended upon him, would be overwhelmed by it, seized by distress, and sweat would pour from him on a cold day. And if He made him in the form of a man, confusion would arise for them: is he a man or an angel? So God said: ﴿And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man and We would have confused them about that which they confuse [themselves with].﴾ In that case, they would say, upon seeing the angel in human form: "This is a human, not an angel." This is the meaning of the verse.

[Section: The error of the wayfarers regarding the natural and the legal distinction]

Section: As for the error of those among the people of spiritual wayfaring (sulūk) and will (irādah) who erred in this matter, they supposed that witnessing the cosmic reality (shuhūd al-ḥaqīqah al-kawniyyah) and annihilation (fanā') in the oneness of lordship (tawḥīd al-rubūbiyyah) are among the stations of the knowers, indeed the most sublime of their stations. So they journeyed, hastening toward the flash of this witnessing and traveling along the valleys of annihilation in it. What urged them on this journey and made them eager for it was what they witnessed of the state of the people of the natural distinction (al-farq al-ṭab'ī). They disdained keeping company with them on the path and regarded separation from them as an obligatory individual duty. When the legal distinction (al-farq al-shar'ī) appeared on their path, and there came upon them from it the greatest of spiritual inspirations, it divided their collectedness, split the unity of their resolve, and stood between them and the essence of unification (al-jam'), which is the final stage of their journey. Thus their paths diverged in the face of this great inspiration.

Among them is the one who plunged into it without turning to it, saying: "Occupation with the litanies (awrād) instead of the essence of the One sought is a cutting off from the goal. The purpose of the litanies is collectedness upon the Other. So what is the point of being occupied with the means instead of the aim, after arriving at it and returning from its presence to the stations of the journey toward it?" Some of them may recite:

*He is asked for litanies who is heedless,*
*so how of a heart whose every moment is a litany?*

When one of them is forced to make a distinction because of an inspiration of command, he says: "The distinction should be present on the tongue, while the unification is witnessed in the heart."

Then among these people is the one who drops the commands and prohibitions altogether, and regards their observance as a matter of preserving the order of the Law, the welfare of the public, and the beginnings of the journey. These are what urge the heedless to exert themselves in the journey. But when he advances in the journey, he dispenses with them through his nearness and collectedness.

Among them is the one who does not consider their dropping (of the commands and prohibitions) to apply except to those who have witnessed the cosmic reality and attained the station of annihilation in it. Whoever has this as his witnessing, the command and prohibition fall away from him according to them.

Some of them also say: "The witnessing of the will (shuhūd al-irādah) drops the command." And in this station they say: "The knower does not regard any ugly deed as ugly, nor any good deed as good."

One of them says: "The knower does not forbid any wrong, because of his insight into God's secret in predestination."

And they say: "Performing worship is a station of confusion (talbīs)," and they argue with His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We would have confused them about that which they confuse [themselves with]﴾ [al-An'am: 9].

This is among the worst of ignorance. For this falls within the answer of the particle *law* (if/had), by which the antecedent (al-muqaddam), which is the implying element (al-malzūm), is negated because its consequent (al-lāzim) is negated, namely the answer and the following clause. So the negation of making the Messenger an angel, as they proposed, is due to the negation of confusion from God upon them. The disbelievers had said: ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him?﴾ [al-An'am: 8], meaning: that we may see him and witness him. Otherwise, the angel had never ceased coming to him from God with His command and prohibition. They proposed the descent of an angel whom they could witness. So God, glory be to Him, informed them of the wisdom for which He did not make an angel His messenger to them, nor send down an angel they could see. He said: ﴿And had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved﴾ [al-An'am: 8], meaning: punishment would have become due and the affair would have been completed, and they would not be given respite if they persisted in denial.

This is parallel to His words in Surat al-Ḥijr: ﴿And they say: "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed, indeed you are a madman. Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are of the truthful?"﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 6]. God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth, and they would not then be given respite﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 8]. Here "the truth" means punishment. Then He said: ﴿And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾ [al-An'am: 9], meaning: if We had sent down to them an angel, We would have made him in the form of a human, since they cannot receive from the angel in the form he is in. In that case, confusion would fall upon them from Us, because they would not know whether he is a man or an angel. And if We had made him a man, We would have confused them and made what they sought appear similar to something else.

As for His words, *mā yalbisūn* (that which they confuse [themselves with]), there are two opinions:

The first: it is a recompense for them for their confusing their weak followers. The meaning is that they cast doubt upon their weak followers and mixed truth with falsehood for them, so doubt was cast upon them, and the angel was confused with the man for them.

The second: We would confuse for them what they had confused for themselves. They mixed things up for themselves and did not believe in the Messenger from among them, after recognizing his truthfulness, and they sought an angelic messenger whom they could witness. This is their confusion of themselves. So if We answered what they proposed, they would not believe even then, and We would confuse them with their own confusion of themselves.

And what connection does this have with the confusion that this group mentions, namely attaching existent things, rewards, and punishments to causes; attaching knowledge to intermediaries, judgments to proofs, rulings and their causes, retribution to crimes, and rewards to acts of obedience? These are pure wisdom and its requirement. The effect of His name, the Wise, in creation and command arises only through causes, and likewise this world and the Hereafter, and likewise reward and punishment. So making causes established as a means of confusion is among the greatest falsehoods, in law and in decree.

**(A Subtle Point)**

Al-Mubarrad reported from Abu Kamil, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Raja' ibn Amr al-Nakha'i, who said: In Kufa there was a youth of handsome face, intensely devoted to worship and striving. He lodged in the neighbourhood of a people from al-Nakha', and he looked upon a beautiful girl among them, and he fell in love with her, and love for her overcame his reason, and what he suffered befell the girl as well. He sent someone to ask for her hand from her father, but her father informed him that she had already been promised to a cousin of hers. When the pain of passion grew severe upon the two of them, the girl sent word to him: "I have been told of the intensity of your love for me, and my trial with you has grown severe. If you wish, I will visit you, or if you wish, I will arrange for you to come to my house."

He said to the messenger: "Neither of these two qualities," and [recited]: ﴿Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾

"I fear a Fire whose blaze will not subside and whose flame will not be extinguished." When the messenger conveyed his words to her, she said: "And he, despite this, fears God! By God, no one is more worthy of this than another, and the servants are all equal in it." Then she withdrew from the world, cast its ties behind her back, and began to worship, while she melted and wasted away from love for the youth and longing for him, until she died of it. The youth would come to her grave and weep there and pray for her. One day sleep overcame him at her grave, and he saw her in his dream in the finest of forms. He said: "How are you, and what have you encountered after me?"

She said:

"Excellent is love, O my hope, your love,
a love that leads to goodness and beneficence."

He said: "Upon that, to what have you come?"

She said:

"To bliss and a life that has no end,
in the Garden of Eternity, a kingdom that is not perishable."

He said to her: "Remember me there, for I shall not forget you."

She said: "And I, by God, shall not forget you either. I have asked my Lord and yours to gather us together, so help me in that by striving."

He said to her: "When shall I see you?"

She said: "You will soon come to us, and you will see us." The youth did not live after the vision more than seven nights, until he died, may God have mercy on him.

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Harun al-Rashid fell in love with one of his slave-girls and wished to have her, but she said: "Your father has touched me." So he became infatuated with her and composed about her:

"I see water, and I have a fierce thirst,
but there is no path to reach it.

Is it not enough for you that you possess me,
and that people are to me like slaves?

And that if you were to cut off my hand and my foot,
I would say, out of contentment: 'You have done well, so increase it.'"

He asked Abu Yusuf about this, and he said: "Does everything a slave-girl says get believed?"

Ibn al-Mubarak said: I do not know which of the three I should marvel at most: Harun al-Rashid for desiring her, or her for turning away from him, or Abu Yusuf for permitting him to approach her.

Some devout women had been desired by a wealthy man; she was beautiful, and she was proposed for, but she refused. The man heard that she intended to perform Hajj, so he bought three hundred camels and proclaimed: "Whoever wishes to perform Hajj, let him hire from so-and-so." The woman hired from him. When they were on part of the journey, he came to her and said: "Either you marry me yourself, or otherwise." She said: "Woe to you, fear God!" He said: "It is nothing but what you hear. By God, I am not a camel-driver, and I did not come out except for your sake." When she feared for herself, she said: "Woe to you, look, is there among the men an eye that has not slept?" He said: "No, they have all slept." She said: "Has the eye of the Lord of the worlds slept?" Then she let out a gasp and fell dead, and the man fell unconscious. When he recovered he said: "Woe to me! I have killed a soul and did not attain my desire."

**(Chapter: Restraint from Sin Arises from Many Causes)**

The first: the servant's knowledge of its ugliness, baseness, and vileness, and that God forbade and prohibited it only to safeguard and protect him from lowly and base things, just as a compassionate parent protects his child from what harms him. This cause moves the intelligent person to abandon it even if no threat of punishment were attached to it.

The second cause: shame before God, glorified is He. For when the servant knows that He sees him, that He stands over him, and that he is in His sight and hearing, and he is a living, modest person, he feels shame before his Lord about exposing himself to His displeasure.

The third cause: observing His blessings upon you and His kindness toward you, for sins inevitably remove blessings.

No servant commits a sin except that a blessing from God is removed from him in proportion to that sin. If he repents and returns, the blessing returns to him or its equivalent; if he persists, it does not return. Sins never cease removing blessings from him until all blessings are stripped away. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11].

The greatest blessing is faith, and the sins of fornication, theft, drinking wine, and plundering remove and strip it away.

One of the early generation said: "I committed a sin and was deprived of the night prayer for a year." Another said: "I committed a sin and was deprived of understanding the Qur'an." Concerning such a matter it has been said:

"If you are in a blessing, guard it,
for sins remove blessings."

In sum, sins are the fire of blessings, consuming them as fire consumes firewood; we seek refuge with God from the loss of His blessing and the transformation of His well-being.

The fourth cause: fear of God and dread of His punishment.

This is established only through affirming His promise and His threat, and believing in Him, His Book, and His Messenger. This cause grows stronger with knowledge and certainty and weakens as they weaken. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear God﴾ [Fatir: 28]. One of the early generation said: "Fear of God is sufficient as knowledge, and being deceived by God is sufficient as ignorance."

The fifth cause: love of God, glorified is He, which is the strongest of the causes for restraint from disobeying Him and from His sins.

For the lover is obedient to the one he loves, and whenever the authority of love grows stronger in the heart, its demand for obedience and abandonment of disobedience becomes stronger. Disobedience and transgression arise only from weakness of love and its authority. There is a difference between one who is restrained from disobeying his master by fear of his whip and punishment, and one who is restrained by his love for his master. Concerning this, Umar said: "Excellent is the servant Suhayb; had he not feared God, he would not have disobeyed Him."

That is, if he did not fear God, he would still have in his heart such love for God and such reverence for Him that it would prevent him from disobeying Him.

The sincere lover has a watcher from the beloved over him, guarding his heart and limbs, and the sign of sincere love is the constant witnessing of this watcher.

Here is a subtle point that must be noted: bare love does not produce this effect unless it is joined with reverence and glorification of the beloved. When it is joined with reverence and glorification, it produces this shame and obedience. Otherwise, love devoid of them produces only a kind of familiarity, expansiveness, remembrance, and longing. For this reason its effect and its requirement are left behind; the servant searches his heart and finds in it some kind of love for God, yet it does not move him to abandon His disobedience. The reason is that it is stripped of reverence and glorification. Nothing populates the heart like love joined with reverence and glorification of God, and that is among the finest, or the finest, of God's gifts to His servant, and that is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills.

The sixth cause: the nobility, purity, excellence, dignity, and zeal of the soul, which refuses to choose the things that lower it, diminish its rank, belittle it, and place it on a level with the base.

The seventh cause: strong knowledge of the evil consequence of sin, the ugliness of its effect, and the harm arising from it: the blackening of the face, the darkness and constriction of the heart, its grief and pain, its confinement, the severity of its anxiety and agitation, the scattering of its unity, weakness in resisting its enemy, its being stripped of its adornment, bewilderment in its affair, the abandonment by its protector and helper, the enemy's dominion over it, the hiding of the knowledge it was prepared for, the forgetting or weakening of what it had attained, and its sickness which, if it becomes firmly established, is death without doubt. For sins kill hearts. Among them is its humiliation after honour; among them is that it becomes a captive in the hands of its enemies after having been a sovereign who disposes freely, whom its enemies feared; among them is that its influence is diminished so that it has no authority over its subjects nor beyond them, so its subjects do not obey it when it commands them, and it has no effect on others; among them is the loss of its security and its replacement by fear, for the most fearful of people is the one most wicked in conduct; among them is the loss of intimacy and its replacement by desolation, and the more it does wrong the more desolate it becomes; among them is the loss of contentment and its replacement by wrath; among them is the loss of tranquillity in God, of peace with Him and refuge with Him, and its replacement by rejection and distance from Him; among them is its falling into the well of regrets, so it is never free of constant regret: whenever it attains a pleasure, its soul strives toward its like if it has not satisfied its want from it, or toward something else if it has satisfied its want from it; and what it is unable to attain of that is manifold more than what it is able to attain; and the more its striving intensifies and it recognizes its incapacity, the more its regret and grief intensify.

Alas, what a fire by which the heart is tormented in this abode before the Fire of God, which is kindled and rises over the hearts! Among them is its poverty after wealth, for it was wealthy with the capital of faith which it trades with, gaining many profits; when its capital is taken, it becomes poor and destitute. Then either it strives to acquire another capital through sincere repentance, earnestness, and diligence, or else it has lost a great profit through what it squandered of its capital. Among them is the diminishing of its provision, for the servant is deprived of provision through a sin he commits. Among them is the weakness of its body.

Among them is the loss of the awe and sweetness that obedience had clothed it with, so it is replaced by humiliation and contempt.

Among them is the arising of hatred and aversion toward him in the hearts of people.

Among them is the loss of the most precious and most excellent thing to him, which is time that has no substitute and never returns.

Among them is his enemy's greed for him and his success over him, for when he sees him submissive and responsive to what he commands, his greed intensifies, he entertains the notion of conquering him, and makes him part of his party, until he becomes his friend rather than the friend of his true Master. Among them is the sealing and rust upon his heart, for when the servant sins, a black spot is made upon his heart; if he repents of it, his heart is polished; if he commits another sin, another spot is made upon it, and it continues until it covers his heart, and that is the rust. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Nay, but what they have been earning has become a rust upon their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14].

Among them is that he is deprived of the sweetness of obedience; when he performs it, he does not find its effect in his heart in sweetness, strength, increase of faith, understanding, and desire for the Hereafter, for obedience yields these fruits without doubt.

Among them is that it prevents his heart from departing from the world and alighting in the courtyard of the Resurrection, for the heart remains scattered and wasted until it departs from the world and alights in the Hereafter. When it alights there, the delegations of success and divine care come to it from every direction, and it gathers its scattered parts, prepares its equipment, and readies its provision for the Day of its return. As long as it has not departed toward the Hereafter and attended it, weariness, toil, dispersion, laziness, and idleness are inevitably its companions.

Among them is the aversion of God, His angels, and His servants from him, for when the servant turns away from obedience to God and occupies himself with His disobedience, God turns away from him, and His angels and servants turn away from him, just as when he turns toward God, God turns toward him and turns the hearts of His creatures toward him.

Among them is that one sin calls for another sin, then the two strengthen one another and call for a third, then the three gather and call for a fourth, and so on, until his sins overwhelm him and his wrongdoing encompasses him.

One of the early generation said: "Among the reward of a good deed is a good deed after it, and among the punishment of an evil deed is an evil deed after it." Among them is his knowledge of the loss of what is dearer to him and better for him than it, of its kind and of other kinds, for God does not combine for His servant the pleasure of forbidden things in this world and the pleasure of what is in the Hereafter.

As God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire: "You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 20]. The believer does not squander his good things in this world; rather, he must leave some of his good things for the Hereafter.

As for the disbeliever, he does not believe in the Hereafter, so he is greedy to take all his portions and good things in this world. Among them is his knowledge that his deeds are his provision and his means to the abode of his permanence: if he takes provision from disobedience to God, that provision brings him to the abode of the disobedient and the criminals; if he takes provision from obedience to Him, he arrives at the abode of the people of His obedience and His friendship. Among them is his knowledge that his deed is his guardian in his grave, his companion therein, his intercessor with his Lord, and his advocate and defender; if He wills, He makes it for him, and if He wills, He makes it against him. Among them is his knowledge that righteous deeds lift the servant up, sustain him, and ascend with him to God, so in proportion to the strength of his attachment to them will be his ascent along with their ascent; and deeds of immorality drag him down, pull him toward the abyss, and draw him to the lowest of the low, and in proportion to the strength of his attachment to them will be his descent with them and his fall to where they settle him. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]. And God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾ [al-A'raf: 40]. Thus, since the gates of heaven were not opened for their deeds but were closed against them, they will not be opened for their souls at departure but will be closed against them.

As for the people of faith and righteous deeds, since the gates of heaven were open to their deeds until they reached God, glorified is He, they were opened for their souls until they reached Him, exalted is He, and stood before Him; He had mercy on them and ordered that their names be written in ʿIlliyyin. Among them is his departure from the fortress of God, in which no loss befalls the one who enters it; by his disobedience he goes out of it to where he becomes plunder for thieves and highwaymen.

So what is to be supposed of one who leaves an impregnable fortress where no calamity reaches him, for a desolate ruin which is the refuge of thieves and highwaymen? Will they leave anything of his property with him?

Among them is that by disobedience he has exposed himself to the erasure of blessing in every matter of his worldly and otherworldly affairs, for obedience brings the servant the blessings of everything, while disobedience erases every blessing.

In sum, the evil effects of disobedience are more than the servant can comprehend in knowledge, and the good effects of obedience are more than he can comprehend in knowledge; the good of this world and the next in its entirety lies in obedience to God, and the evil of this world and the next in its entirety lies in disobedience to Him. In some reports, God, the Exalted, says: "Who is it that obeyed Me and was made wretched by his obedience to Me? And who is it that disobeyed Me and was made happy by his disobedience?"

The eighth cause: shortness of hope, and his knowledge of the swiftness of his departure, and that he is like a traveller who has entered a village while intending to leave it, or like a rider who rested in the shade of a tree and then moved on and left it. Because he knows how brief his stay is and how swift his departure will be, he is eager to abandon what burdens him and harms him without benefiting him, and eager to depart with the best of what is in his presence. Nothing is more beneficial to the servant than shortness of hope, and nothing more harmful than procrastination and long hope.

The ninth cause: avoiding excess in his food, drink, clothing, sleep, and social mixing, for the strength of the drive toward sin arises only from these surpluses, for they seek an outlet; if lawful outlets are restricted for them, they overstep to the unlawful. Among the things most harmful to the servant is idleness and emptiness, for the soul does not sit idle; if he does not occupy it with what benefits it, it will occupy him with what harms it, without doubt.

The tenth cause, which comprehends all these causes: the firmness of the tree of faith in the heart. The servant's restraint from sins is in proportion to the strength of his faith; the stronger his faith, the more complete his restraint, and when faith weakens, restraint weakens. For whoever has faith penetrating his heart, with the awareness of God's standing over him and His seeing him, His prohibition of what He has forbidden him, His hatred of it, and His abhorrence of its doer, and faith in reward and punishment, Paradise and Hell, will refrain from failing to act in accordance with the requirement of this knowledge.

Whoever thinks that he can abstain from transgressions and sins without firm and established faith has erred. When the lamp of faith grows strong in the heart, and its sides are all illuminated by it, and its light shines in its corners, that light spreads to the limbs and radiates to them, so they swiftly respond to the call of faith and submit to it, obedient, subdued, neither reluctant nor averse, but rejoicing in its summons whenever it calls them, as a man rejoices at the call of a beloved benefactor to a place of honour.

So he is, at every time, awaiting its call and preparing to meet it.

﴿And God singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the Owner of tremendous bounty﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 25:

As for the veils (al-akinna), they appear in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts veils, lest they understand it﴾. It is the plural of kinan, like inan and a'inna, and its root meaning is concealment and covering. It is said: kannahu, akannahu, and kinan, with one meaning; yet there is a difference between them. Akannahu means he concealed it and hid it, as in His saying: ﴿Or you concealed it within yourselves﴾. Kannahu means he guarded it and preserved it, as in His saying: ﴿As though they were eggs, well-guarded﴾. The two share the meaning of covering and shielding. Al-kinan is what conceals a thing and shields it, and it is like a sheath. They acknowledged this against themselves when they said: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you there is a barrier﴾. So they mentioned the covering of the heart, which is the veils (al-akinna); the covering of the ear, which is deafness (al-waqr); and the covering of the eye, which is the barrier (al-hijab). The meaning is: we do not understand your speech, we do not hear it, and we do not see you. The meaning is that we, in refusing to accept from you, are in the position of one who does not understand what you say and does not see you.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Our hearts are in coverings like the quiver that holds the arrows."

Mujahid said: "Like the case of the arrows."

Muqatil said: "There is a covering over them, so we do not understand what you say."

(Benefit)

These veils and deafness are intense hatred, aversion, and turning away, by which they are unable to hear or to reason. The reality is that this arises from the veils and deafness; it is their necessary consequence and effect. Whoever explains the veils and deafness by it has explained them by their necessary consequence and effect. In every case, that aversion, turning away, and hatred are among their actions, and they are created by God, glory be to Him, just as the tenderness and mercy and the inclination of hearts toward His House are among their actions, and God is the one who makes them. He is the Maker of essences, their attributes, their actions, their wills, and their beliefs. All of that is made and created by Him, even though the servant is the doer of it by his own choice and will.

If it is said: does all this contradict His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God did not appoint any bahira, sa'iba, wasila, or ham﴾? The bahira and the sa'iba became such only by the making of the people. He, exalted is He, informed that this was not by His making. It is said: by God's praise, there is no contradiction whatsoever among the texts of the Book. The "making" here is legislative and commanding, not existential and decreed. The making in the Book of God is divided into these two kinds, just as command, permission, decree, prescription, and prohibition are divided into them, as will be explained, God willing. So He, exalted is He, negated from the bahira and the sa'iba His religious, legislative making; that is, He did not legislate that or command it. But those who disbelieved fabricated lies against Him and made that a religion for Him without knowledge.

Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim), on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 27–28:

Most of the exegetes have circled around the meaning of this verse, and they have not offered anything that heals.

So review their statements and you will find that they neither cure the sick nor quench the thirst.

The meaning of the verse is more sublime and greater than what they have explained it by. They did not perceive the purpose of the turn introduced by "bal" (rather), nor the matter that became apparent to them, which they had been concealing. They thought that what had become apparent to them was the punishment. When they did not find this to fit with His words ﴿what they had been concealing before﴾, they supposed an omitted modifier (mudaf), namely that the predicate of "what they had been concealing before" is [the punishment], and another problem arose for them, to which they have no answer.

It is this: the people did not conceal their shirk (associating partners with God) and their disbelief; rather, they displayed it, called to it, and fought for it. When they realized that this objection applied to them, they said: the people, at some stations and places of the Resurrection, concealed their shirk and denied it, and said: ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾. Then, when they stood before the Fire, there became apparent to them the recompense for that which they had concealed.

Al-Wahidi said: "And this is the view of the exegetes."

But the proponents of this view have accomplished nothing. For the context, the turn introduced by "bal", the report about them that if they were returned they would revert to what they had been forbidden, and their saying ﴿By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ do not fit with what they have mentioned. So reflect on this.

A group, including al-Zajjaj, said: "bal" [here] is for the following of what the leaders had concealed from them regarding the matter of the Resurrection.

This explanation requires further explanation, and there is in it an evident far-fetchedness.

Better than this is what al-Mubarrad understood from the verse. He said: It is as if their disbelief had not been manifest to them, since its harm was hidden from them.

The meaning of his words is: because the harm of its consequence and its calamity were hidden from them, it was as though it was hidden from them, its reality not having become apparent to them. When they witnessed the punishment, its reality and its evil became apparent to them.

He said: This is like what you say to someone to whom you had spoken about a matter before: "Now there has become apparent to you what I had told you." Yet it was already apparent to him before this.

It is not easy to describe their disbelief and shirk, which they proclaimed at the heads of witnesses and called to, every present and absent person, as something they had been concealing because its consequence was hidden from them. Nor is it said of one who displays injustice and corruption, kills souls, and strives in the land with corruption, that he concealed that because he was ignorant of its evil consequence and it was hidden from him.

So the meaning of the verse, and God knows best what He intended by His speech, is this: when these polytheists stood before the Fire, witnessed it, and knew that they would enter it, they wished that they might be returned to the world and believe in God and His signs, and not return to denying His messengers. God, glorified is He, informed that the matter is not as they wish, that faith is not in their natures or dispositions, but their disposition is disbelief, polytheism and denial, and that if they were returned they would be, after being returned, as they were before. He also informed that they are liars in their claim that if they were returned they would believe and affirm.

When the purpose and intent of the verse are established, the meaning of the turn with "bal" becomes clear, and the meaning of what had become apparent to them, what they had been concealing, and what prompted their saying ﴿O would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord﴾ becomes clear. The people knew that in the world they were upon falsehood, and that the messengers had told the truth regarding what they conveyed from God. They were certain of this and verified it, but they concealed it and did not display it among themselves; rather, they enjoined one another to keep it hidden. So what moved them to wish for return and belief was not the knowledge of something they had not known regarding the truthfulness of the messengers, for they knew that and concealed it. What became apparent to them on the Day of Resurrection was what they had been harboring within themselves: their knowledge that they were upon falsehood and that the messengers were upon the truth. They witnessed this directly, after they had been hiding and concealing it. Had they been returned, their souls would not have permitted them to believe, and they would have reverted to disbelief and denial. They did not wish for faith because they knew on that day that it was the truth and that shirk was falsehood; rather, they wished for it when they witnessed the punishment, which they had no capacity to bear.

This is like one who used to conceal his love for a person and his companionship with him, while knowing that his love was false and that rectitude lay in turning away from it. It is said to him: if his guardian discovers you, he will punish you. He knows this yet persists in obstinacy and says: rather, his love and companionship are the right course. Then, when his guardian seized him to punish him for this and he was certain of the punishment, he wished to be spared the punishment and that he would never meet him again. Yet in his heart there remained such love and eagerness for the companionship that it would move him to return after witnessing the punishment, indeed after the punishment had touched him and worn him down. Then there became apparent to him at the moment of punishment what he had been concealing: his knowledge of his error and the rightness of what he had been forbidden from. Had he been returned, he would have reverted to what he had been forbidden.

Consider how the turn introduced by "bal" corresponds to this meaning, which is the negation of their saying: "If we were returned, we would believe and affirm." Because what has now become apparent to us is that what the messengers said is the truth, is not the case. Rather, you used to know this and recognize it, and you used to conceal it, so nothing new appeared to you that would make you knowing of it and thus excusable. Rather, what appeared to you was what had already been known, and you used to enjoin one another to hide and conceal it. And God knows best.

Because what has now become apparent to us is that what the messengers said is the truth, is not the case. Rather, you used to know this and recognize it, and you used to conceal it, so nothing new appeared to you that would make you knowing of it and thus excusable. Rather, what appeared to you was what had already been known, and you used to enjoin one another to hide and conceal it. And God knows best.

[Chapter: Ten things that are lost and of no benefit]

Knowledge that is not acted upon; and deeds without sincerity (ikhlas) or following the Prophetic model (iqtida').

Wealth that is not spent from, so its possessor does not enjoy it in this world, nor sends it ahead of him to the Hereafter.

A heart empty of the love of Allah, longing for Him, and intimacy with Him.

A body idle from obeying Him and serving Him.

Love that is not bound by seeking the pleasure of the beloved and complying with his commands.

Time that is wasted, neither making up for what has passed, nor seizing the opportunity for righteousness and drawing near (to Allah).

Thought that wanders over what brings no benefit.

Service to someone whose service does not bring you closer to Allah, nor returns to you any improvement in your worldly affairs.

Had He sent it down according to their demands, they would have been hastened with punishment if they did not believe. Then He mentioned what indicates His complete power by creating these great communities whose number none but He can count. Whoever is able to create these communities with the difference of their kinds, types, attributes, and forms, how could He be unable to send down a sign? Then He informed about His complete power and knowledge, that these communities He has counted, recorded, and decreed their provisions, their terms, and their conditions in a Book in which nothing has been neglected. Then He causes them to die, then gathers them to Himself. "And those who denied Our signs are deaf and dumb, in darknesses," away from sight and reflection which would lead them to knowledge of His lordship, His oneness, and the truthfulness of His messengers. Then He informed that signs do not by themselves establish guidance, even if He sent them down according to human demands; rather, the whole matter belongs to Him: whoever He wills, He lets go astray, and whoever He wills, He places on a straight path. This second opinion is the more apparent of the two, and Allah knows best.

(Section)

Some of the early generation said: "These hearts are wandering. Some of them roam around the Throne, and some of them roam around the latrine (al-hush)."

The Transformation of the Heart (Maskh al-Qalb)

Among them is the transformation of the heart, so it is transformed as an image is transformed, and the heart becomes like the heart of the animal that resembles it in its characters, deeds, and nature. Some hearts are transformed into the heart of a pig because of the intensity of their owner's resemblance to it, and some are transformed into the heart of a dog, a donkey, a snake, a scorpion, or others. This is the interpretation of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no creature crawling on the earth, nor a bird flying with its wings, but they are communities like you﴾ [al-An'am: 38].

He said: "Among them are those who have the characters of savage beasts, and among them are those who have the characters of dogs, pigs, and donkeys. Among them are those who strut in their clothing as a peacock struts in its feathers. Among them are those who are foolish like a donkey. Among them are those who prefer others over themselves like the rooster. Among them are those who are sociable and whom people are sociable with, like the dove. Among them is the spiteful one like the camel. Among them is the one who is all good like the sheep. Among them are those like foxes that dodge like their dodging." Allah, may He be exalted, has likened the people of Hellfire and misguidance to donkeys at times, to dogs at times, and to cattle at times. This resemblance grows inwardly until it appears in the outward form, a hidden appearance that the discerning see, and appears in deeds in a manner everyone sees. It keeps growing until the form becomes repulsive, and the form is changed for him by the permission of Allah. This is the complete transformation, so Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, changes the outward form into the form of that animal, as He did to the Jews and their likes, and He does it to a people of this Ummah, transforming them into apes and pigs.

Glory be to Allah! How many a heart is inverted while its owner is unaware? And a heart transformed and a heart swallowed up by it? And how many are infatuated with people's praise of them and deceived by Allah's covering of them, and lured by Allah's blessings upon them? All of these are punishments and humiliations, yet the ignorant one thinks it is an honor.

(Another Section)

Among human souls are those that are like the souls of ordinary animals and others. This is the interpretation of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no creature crawling on the earth, nor a bird flying with its wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾ [al-An'am: 38].

On this resemblance rely the people of ta'bir (dream interpretation) regarding seeing these animals in a dream in a person's presence or in his house, or that they fight him. And they rely on it correctly. Many such events have occurred to us and to others in dreams, and their interpretation corresponded to peoples according to the natures of those animals. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw in the story of Uhud cows being slaughtered, and those among the believers who were struck were struck by the slaughter of the disbelievers. For cattle are the most beneficial of animals to the earth, and by them its welfare and prosperity come, along with the tranquility, benefits, and submissiveness they have, for they are docile, tamed, obedient, and not unruly. Buffaloes are their big ones and their leaders. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab saw in a dream as if a rooster pecked him three times, and it was the stabbing by Abu Lu'lu'ah, and the rooster is a foreign, evil man.

Among people is one whose nature is the nature of a pig, who passes by good things and does not turn to them, and when a person gets up from his excrement, he vomits on it. Likewise, many people hear from you and see far more good things than bad, yet they do not retain them, nor transmit them, nor are they suited to them. But when they see a slip or an obscene word, they find their aim and what suits it, and they make it their fruit and their talk.

Among them is one whose nature is that of a peacock, having nothing but strutting and adorning himself with feathers, and there is nothing beyond that.

Among them is one whose nature is that of the camel, the most spiteful of animals and the coarsest in liver.

Among them is one whose nature is that of the bear, mute and wicked, and whose nature is that of the monkey.

The best of animal natures are those of horses, which are the noblest of animals in souls and most honorable in nature, and likewise sheep. Whoever becomes accustomed to one type of these animals acquires from its nature and character. If he feeds on its meat, the resemblance is stronger, for the one who feeds resembles what he feeds on.

For this reason Allah has forbidden eating the flesh of beasts of prey and birds of prey, because they bequeath to the one who eats them a resemblance of their souls to theirs. And Allah knows best.

The purpose here is that the people of this station have no witnessing beyond the likes of their own souls and their appetites; they know nothing whatsoever of what lies beyond that.
