This is evidence of His oneness and attributes of perfection from the perspective of His creation and decree, and the sending down of the Book in which nothing has been neglected is evidence from the perspective of His command and speech. So this is an argument from His command, and that is an argument from His creation: ﴿Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

This is also corroborated by His saying: ﴿They say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner." Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, recited to them? Indeed, in that is mercy and reminder for a people who believe﴾.

As for the one who supports that the intended meaning of "the Book" is the Preserved Tablet, he may say: When they asked for a sign, Allah informed them that He did not refrain from sending it down because He was unable to do so, for He is able to do so. Rather, He did not send it down because of His wisdom, His mercy toward them, and His kindness to them. Had He sent it down according to their demands, they would have been hastened with punishment if they did not believe. Then He mentioned what indicates His complete power by creating these great communities whose number none but He can count. Whoever is able to create these communities with the difference of their kinds, types, attributes, and forms, how could He be unable to send down a sign? Then He informed about His complete power and knowledge, that these communities He has counted, recorded, and decreed their provisions, their terms, and their conditions in a Book in which nothing has been neglected. Then He causes them to die, then gathers them to Himself. "And those who denied Our signs are deaf and dumb, in darknesses," away from sight and reflection which would lead them to knowledge of His lordship, His oneness, and the truthfulness of His messengers. Then He informed that signs do not by themselves establish guidance, even if He sent them down according to human demands; rather, the whole matter belongs to Him: whoever He wills, He lets go astray, and whoever He wills, He places on a straight path. This second opinion is the more apparent of the two, and Allah knows best.

(Section)

Some of the early generation said: "These hearts are wandering. Some of them roam around the Throne, and some of them roam around the latrine (al-hush)."

The Transformation of the Heart (Maskh al-Qalb)

Among them is the transformation of the heart, so it is transformed as an image is transformed, and the heart becomes like the heart of the animal that resembles it in its characters, deeds, and nature. Some hearts are transformed into the heart of a pig because of the intensity of their owner's resemblance to it, and some are transformed into the heart of a dog, a donkey, a snake, a scorpion, or others. This is the interpretation of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no creature crawling on the earth, nor a bird flying with its wings, but they are communities like you﴾ [al-An'am: 38].

He said: "Among them are those who have the characters of savage beasts, and among them are those who have the characters of dogs, pigs, and donkeys. Among them are those who strut in their clothing as a peacock struts in its feathers. Among them are those who are foolish like a donkey. Among them are those who prefer others over themselves like the rooster. Among them are those who are sociable and whom people are sociable with, like the dove. Among them is the spiteful one like the camel. Among them is the one who is all good like the sheep. Among them are those like foxes that dodge like their dodging." Allah, may He be exalted, has likened the people of Hellfire and misguidance to donkeys at times, to dogs at times, and to cattle at times. This resemblance grows inwardly until it appears in the outward form, a hidden appearance that the discerning see, and appears in deeds in a manner everyone sees. It keeps growing until the form becomes repulsive, and the form is changed for him by the permission of Allah. This is the complete transformation, so Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, changes the outward form into the form of that animal, as He did to the Jews and their likes, and He does it to a people of this Ummah, transforming them into apes and pigs.

Glory be to Allah! How many a heart is inverted while its owner is unaware? And a heart transformed and a heart swallowed up by it? And how many are infatuated with people's praise of them and deceived by Allah's covering of them, and lured by Allah's blessings upon them? All of these are punishments and humiliations, yet the ignorant one thinks it is an honor.

(Another Section)

Among human souls are those that are like the souls of ordinary animals and others. This is the interpretation of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no creature crawling on the earth, nor a bird flying with its wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾ [al-An'am: 38].

On this resemblance rely the people of ta'bir (dream interpretation) regarding seeing these animals in a dream in a person's presence or in his house, or that they fight him. And they rely on it correctly. Many such events have occurred to us and to others in dreams, and their interpretation corresponded to peoples according to the natures of those animals. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw in the story of Uhud cows being slaughtered, and those among the believers who were struck were struck by the slaughter of the disbelievers. For cattle are the most beneficial of animals to the earth, and by them its welfare and prosperity come, along with the tranquility, benefits, and submissiveness they have, for they are docile, tamed, obedient, and not unruly. Buffaloes are their big ones and their leaders. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab saw in a dream as if a rooster pecked him three times, and it was the stabbing by Abu Lu'lu'ah, and the rooster is a foreign, evil man.

Among people is one whose nature is the nature of a pig, who passes by good things and does not turn to them, and when a person gets up from his excrement, he vomits on it. Likewise, many people hear from you and see far more good things than bad, yet they do not retain them, nor transmit them, nor are they suited to them. But when they see a slip or an obscene word, they find their aim and what suits it, and they make it their fruit and their talk.

Among them is one whose nature is that of a peacock, having nothing but strutting and adorning himself with feathers, and there is nothing beyond that.

Among them is one whose nature is that of the camel, the most spiteful of animals and the coarsest in liver.

Among them is one whose nature is that of the bear, mute and wicked, and whose nature is that of the monkey.

The best of animal natures are those of horses, which are the noblest of animals in souls and most honorable in nature, and likewise sheep. Whoever becomes accustomed to one type of these animals acquires from its nature and character. If he feeds on its meat, the resemblance is stronger, for the one who feeds resembles what he feeds on.

For this reason Allah has forbidden eating the flesh of beasts of prey and birds of prey, because they bequeath to the one who eats them a resemblance of their souls to theirs. And Allah knows best.

The purpose here is that the people of this station have no witnessing beyond the likes of their own souls and their appetites; they know nothing whatsoever of what lies beyond that.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 44:

Some of the deluded may rely on what they see of Allah's blessings upon them in this world, and that He does not change what is with them, and they suppose that this is from Allah's love for them, and that He will give them better than that in the Hereafter. This is among the delusions (al-ghurur).

The Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Harmala ibn Imran al-Tujibi, from Uqba ibn Muslim, from Uqba ibn Amir, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "If you see Allah, Mighty and Majestic, giving the servant of the worldly things he loves while he persists in his disobediences, then it is only istidraj (gradual enticement). Then he recited His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of everything until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair﴾."

Some of the early predecessors (al-salaf) said: If you see Allah continuing His blessings upon you while you persist in His disobedience, then beware of Him; for it is only istidraj from Him, by which He draws you on. And the Exalted has said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses and stairways [of silver] upon which they ascend, And doors for their houses and couches [of silver] upon which they recline, And adornments of gold. But all that would be nothing but enjoyment of the worldly life. And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33-35].

Indeed, He, glorified is He, has refuted those who suppose this supposition by His saying: ﴿As for man, when his Lord tries him and honours him and gives him favour, he says, "My Lord has honoured me." But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." No!﴾ [al-Fajr: 15-17].

That is: not everyone whom I bless and whose provision I widen is one whom I have honoured, and not everyone whom I test and whose provision I restrict is one whom I have humiliated. Rather, I test this one with blessings, and I honour that one with trial.

In the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Allah gives the world to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He gives faith only to whomever He loves."

Some of the early predecessors said: How many a one is drawn on by Allah's blessings while he does not know it; how many a one is deceived by Allah's concealing of him while he does not know it; and how many a one is tempted by people's praise of him while he does not know it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 53:

That is, We tested and tried some of them by means of others. Thus He tried the leaders and masters by means of the followers, the clients and the weak. When the leader and the one obeyed looks at the client and the weak one with disdain and arrogance, and is too proud to submit, and says, "This one has been favoured by God with guidance and happiness over me," God the Exalted says: ﴿Is not God most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ Those are the ones who recognise the blessing and its worth, and thank God for it through acknowledgment, humility, submission and servitude. If your hearts were like their hearts, knowing the worth of My blessing, thanking Me for it, remembering Me by it, submitting to Me as they submit, and loving Me as they love, I would have bestowed favour upon you as I bestowed it upon them. But My favour and My blessings are placed in locations that suit them alone and are fitting only with them. For this reason He often pairs specification with knowledge, as in His saying here: ﴿Is not God most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, and His saying: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of God." God knows best where to place His message﴾, and His saying: ﴿And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses. They have no choice. Glory be to God, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him. And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they reveal﴾.

(Section)

God has informed us that all the actions of His servants occur by His decree and destiny. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And thus We tried some of them by means of others, that they might say: "Are these the ones upon whom God has bestowed favour from among us?"﴾

There is no doubt that this is the explanation (ta'lil) for His mentioned act, which is the testing of some of His creation by means of others, just as He tested the masters and nobles by means of the slaves, the weak and the clients. When the noble and the master looks at the slave, the weak one and the poor man who has embraced Islam, he becomes too proud and resentful to embrace it together with him or after him, and says, "This one precedes me to goodness and success, while I am left behind. If this were good and happiness, these would not have preceded us to it." This statement from them is part of the wisdom and the desired end of this test, for this statement indicates haughtiness, arrogance and refusal to submit to the truth after complete knowledge of it. Although this is a cause, it is sought for something else. Final causes are sometimes sought for themselves and sometimes sought for other things, so they become a means to an end that is sought for its own sake. What these people said, and what follows from this saying, entails effects desired by the Agent: the manifestation of His justice, wisdom, might, power and sovereignty; His giving to whom deserves His gift and rightly places it with him; and His withholding from whoever deserves to be withheld from and for whom no one else is fitting. For this reason He said: ﴿Is not God most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, those who recognise the worth of the blessing and thank the ones who bestowed it upon them, among those who were favoured, distinguished from those who do not recognise it and do not thank their Lord for it. The testing of some by means of others was for the occurrence of this distinction, which resulted in the gratitude of these and the disbelief of those.

(Section)

How many wisdoms, praises, commands, prohibitions, decrees and destinies belong to God, the Exalted, in making some of His servants a trial for others, as He said: ﴿And thus We tried some of them by means of others﴾, and He said: ﴿And We made some of you a trial for others. Will you be patient?﴾

He, glory be to Him, made His friends a trial for His enemies, and His enemies a trial for His friends; kings a trial for subjects, and subjects a trial for them; men a trial for women, and women a trial for them; the rich a trial for the poor, and the poor a trial for them. He tested each person with the opposite of what He had made them to be in contrast. The feet of the two parents had not settled upon the earth before their opposite stood opposite them, and the matter continued thus among their offspring until God folds up this world and whoever is upon it. How many wisdoms, perfect blessings, executed judgments, commands, prohibitions and dispositions, indicating His lordship, divinity, dominion and praiseworthiness, does He have in such a trial and testing. Likewise, His testing of His servants with good and evil in this abode is part of the perfection of His wisdom and the requirement of His complete praise.

(Section)

Were it not for this trial and testing, the excellence of patience, contentment, reliance upon God, struggle, chastity, courage, forbearance, pardon and forgiveness would not have become manifest. God, the Exalted, loves to honour His friends with these perfections and loves that they be manifest upon them, so that He and His angels may praise them thereby, and so that they may attain, through being characterised by them, the utmost honour, delight and joy. Although their beginnings are bitter, nothing is sweeter than their outcomes, and the existence of the necessitated thing without its necessity is impossible. God, the Exalted, has set His wisdom such that the perfection of ends follows the strength of their causes, and their deficiency follows the deficiency of their causes. Whoever perfects the causes of bliss and pleasure, their ends are perfected for him; whoever is deprived of them is deprived of their ends; and whoever lacks some of them is lacking in some of their ends. Upon this stands recompense with justice, reward and punishment. This world is sufficient as a witness to this, for the Lord of this world and the Hereafter is one, His wisdom is consistent in both, and to Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and to Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.

[Between Ibn ʿAbbas and the Khawarij]

ʿAbdullah ibn Wahb said, from ʿAmr ibn al-Harith, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ʿAli sent me to the Harouriyya (the Khawarij) to speak with them. When they said, "There is no judgment except that of Allah," I said: "Indeed, you are right. There is no judgment except that of Allah. But Allah has appointed arbitration (ḥukm) concerning a man and his wife, and He appointed arbitration concerning the killing of game. So is the judgment concerning a man and his wife and the game better, or the judgment concerning the Ummah, by which it is restored, its blood is preserved, and its scattered affairs are gathered together?"

ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar narrated to us, Simak al-Hanafi narrated to us, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: ʿAli said, "Do not fight them until they come out, for they will come out." He said: I said, "O Commander of the Faithful, delay the prayer (al-Ibrad bil-Salah), for I want to enter upon them, hear their speech, and speak with them." ʿAli said, "I fear for you from them." He said: I was a man of good character who did not harm anyone. He said: So I put on the finest Yemeni clothing and combed my hair, then I entered upon them while they were at midday rest (qaʾilun). They said to me, "What is this clothing?" So I recited to them the Qur'an: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ [al-Araf: 32].

And I had indeed seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wear the finest Yemeni clothing. They said, "There is no harm in that. So what brought you?" I said: "I have come to you from the presence of my companion, who is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his son-in-law, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are among you with revelation, and the Qur'an was revealed upon them. I convey to you their words and I convey their words to you. So what do you resent?" Some of them said, "Indeed, Quraysh are a contentious people." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Rather, they are a contentious people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 58]. Some of them said, "Speak to him." Two or three of them came toward me and said, "If you wish, you speak, and if you wish, we will speak." I said, "Rather, you speak." They said, "There are three things we resent in him: he made arbitration a matter for men, and Allah says: ﴿The judgment is only for Allah﴾ [al-Anʿam: 57]." I said: "Allah has indeed made arbitration in His affair a matter for men concerning a quarter of a dirham regarding a rabbit, and concerning a woman and her husband: ﴿So send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family﴾ [al-Nisa: 35]. Have I got out of this?" They said, "Yes." They said: "And another: he erased himself from being Commander of the Faithful, so if he is not Commander of the Faithful, then he is Commander of the Disbelievers." I said to them: "What do you think, if I recite to you from the Book of Allah and bring you from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, will you return?" They said, "Yes." I said: "You have heard, or I think it has reached you, that when the day of al-Hudaybiyya came, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAli: 'Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon.' They said: 'If we knew that you are the Messenger of Allah, we would not have fought you.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAli: 'Erase it, O ʿAli.'" Have I got out of this? They said, "Yes." He said: As for your saying, "He killed but did not take captives or booty," will you take captive your mother and consider lawful from her what you consider lawful from others? If you say yes, then you have disbelieved in the Book of Allah and left Islam, and you are between two misguidances. Whenever I brought them something of this sort, I would say, "Have I got out of it?" and they would say, "Yes." He said: So two thousand of them returned, and six thousand remained. This narration has several chains from Ibn ʿAbbas, and this analogy mentioned is among the finest and clearest analogies.

Ibn ʿAbbas also criticized Zayd ibn Thabit for his deviation from analogy in the matter of the grandfather and the brothers. He said: "Does Zayd not fear Allah? He makes the son of the son a son, but does not make the father of the father a father?" And this is pure analogy.

When al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr) gave the inheritance to the mother's mother to the exclusion of the father's mother, one of the Ansar said to him: "You have given inheritance to a woman from a deceased who, if she had been the one who died, he would not have inherited from her, and you have left a woman who, if she had been the one who died, he would have inherited all she left. So he made them share." ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from Yahya ibn Saʿid, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: Two grandmothers came to Abu Bakr, and he gave the inheritance to the mother's mother to the exclusion of the father's mother. A man of the Ansar, from Banu al-Harith, called ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sahl, said to him: "O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah, you have given the inheritance to the one who, if she had died, he would not have inherited from her," so he made the inheritance shared between them.

When Abu Bakrah and his companions testified against al-Mughira ibn Shuʿbah for the hadd punishment but did not complete the required number of witnesses, ʿUmar punished them, by analogy with the slanderer (qadhif), though they were not slanderers but witnesses. ʿUthman said to ʿUmar: "If we follow your opinion, your opinion is the most solid, and if we follow the opinion of those before you, then how excellent was the one of opinion who came before."

ʿAli said: "My opinion and ʿUmar's agreed on not selling the umm al-walad (mothers of children), that they should not be sold, then I saw that they should be sold." His judge ʿUbaydah al-Salmani said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, your opinion together with ʿUmar's in the community is more beloved to us than your opinion alone in division."

When ʿUmar summoned a woman who then miscarried her fetus, he consulted the Companions. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf and ʿUthman said to him: "You are only an educator, and there is nothing upon you." ʿAli said to him: "As for the sin, I hope it is removed from you, but I see that the blood money (diyah) is due from you." ʿUthman and ʿAbd al-Rahman analogized him to the one who disciplines his wife, his slave, and his child, while ʿAli analogized him to the killer by mistake. ʿUmar then followed ʿAli's analogy.

When al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was on his deathbed, he designated the caliphate to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and analogized his authority after him to the fact that he is the one who binds and loosens (ahl al-hall wal-aqd) regarding the governance of the Muslims, since they are the people who bind and loose. This is among the finest analogies.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 76:

His saying: ﴿This is my lord﴾

It has been said: it is on the basis of an interrogative (istifham), meaning: "Is this my lord?" But this is not correct.

It has also been said: it was in the manner of establishing the proof against his people. He imagined himself in the form of one who agrees with them, so that it would be more likely to be accepted. Then he used the form of agreement as a means to inform them that the worshipped one cannot be deficient and setting.

For the true worshipped one: it is not permissible that He should be absent from His worshippers and His creation, and set away from them.

For that contradicts His lordship over them.

Or, he moved through the stages of reasoning about the worshipped one until the evidence led him to the One who originated the heavens and the earth.

So he turned his face toward Him, as a pure monotheist (hanif muwahhid), turning toward Him, turning away from anything other than Him. And Allah is most knowing.

When the leader of the hanifs (ḥunafāʾ, those who turn away from all false worship to pure monotheism) saw that the sun, the moon and the stars were not of this status, he ascended from them to their Originator, Creator and Innovator, and said:

﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as a hanif (ḥanīf), and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ [Al-An'am: 79].

In this is an indication that He, glory be to Him, is the Creator of their places and locations, which they need, and they have no subsistence except through them. So they need a place in which to subsist, and a Creator (Fāṭir) who creates them, governs them and nurtures them.

What is needy, created, nurtured and governed cannot be a god. His people argued with him about Allah, but whoever argues about the worship of Allah, his argument is refuted.

So Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said:

﴿Do you argue with me about Allah when He has guided me?﴾ [Al-An'am: 80].

This is among the finest of speech. That is: do you want to turn me away from affirming my Lord and His oneness, from worshipping Him alone, and cause me to doubt it? He has guided me and made clear to me the truth, until it became manifest to me as if I were seeing it with my own eyes. He made clear to me the falsity of association (shirk) and its evil outcome, and that your gods are not fit for worship, and that worshipping them brings upon their worshippers the utmost harm in this world and the next. So how do you want me to turn away from worshipping Him and His oneness to associating others with Him? When He has guided me to the truth and the path of right guidance?

Argument and dispute have no purpose except seeking a return and a transition from falsehood to truth, from ignorance to knowledge, and from blindness to sight. Your disputing with me about the true God, besides whom every object of worship is false, involves the opposite of this.

Then they frightened him with their gods, that they might afflict him with harm, as the polytheist frightens the monotheist with the god he worships alongside Allah, that it may strike him with evil. So the Friend (al-Khalīl) said:

﴿And I do not fear those you associate with Him.﴾ [Al-An'am: 80].

For your gods are too weak and too contemptible to harm one who disbelieves in them and denies their worship. Then he returned the matter to the will of Allah alone, and that it is He who is feared and hoped in. He said:

﴿Except that my Lord should will something.﴾ [Al-An'am: 80].

This is an exceptive clause that is disjunct (munqaṭiʿ). The meaning is: I do not fear your gods, for they have no will and no power. But if my Lord wills something, it will reach me and strike me, not your gods, which neither will nor know anything. My Lord has the absolute will, and His knowledge encompasses all things. So who is more deserving to be feared and worshipped: He, glory be to Him, or they? Then he said:

﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ [Al-An'am: 80].

That is, you would know what you are upon, of associating with one who has no will and knows nothing, rather than with the One who has perfect will and perfect knowledge.

Then he said:

﴿And how should I fear what you have associated, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority?﴾ [Al-An'am: 81].

This is among the finest reversals of argument, making the argument of the falsifier itself a proof of the corruption of his claim and the falsity of his doctrine.

For they frightened him with their gods, for which Allah had sent down no authority to them to worship. The falsity of their divinity and the harm of worshipping them has been made clear. Yet despite this, do you not fear your associating others with Allah and your worshipping other gods alongside Him?

So which of the two groups is more deserving of security and more fitting not to be touched by fear: the group of monotheists or the group of polytheists? Allah, glory be to Him, judged between the two groups with the most just judgment, than which there is no more correct. He said:

﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing (ẓulm) — that is, with association (shirk) — for them is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾ [Al-An'am: 82].

When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily on the Companions, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us has not wronged himself?"

He said: "It is only association. Have you not heard the saying of the righteous servant: ﴿Indeed, association is a great wrong﴾?" [Luqman: 13].

So Allah, glory be to Him, judged for the monotheists with guidance and security, and for the polytheists with the opposite of that, which is misguidance and fear. Then He said:

﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Ibrahim against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.﴾ [Al-An'am: 83].

Abu Muhammad ibn Ḥazm said: "What the Sabians (al-Ṣābiʾah) adhered to was the oldest of religions over the course of time and the dominant one in the world, until they introduced innovations and altered its laws. So Allah sent to them Ibrahim, His friend, with the religion of Islam, which we follow today, and to correct what they had corrupted, and with the pure (samḥah) ḥanīfiyyah that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), brought to us from Allah, Exalted is He."

In that time and after it, they were called ḥunafāʾ.

I say: They are of two kinds: Sabians who are polytheists, and Sabians who are ḥunafāʾ, and there are debates between them.

Al-Shahrastani has recounted some of their debates in his book.

(Section)

His saying:

﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing (ẓulm) — that is, with association (shirk) — for them is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾ [Al-An'am: 82].

When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily on the Companions, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us has not wronged himself?"

He said: "It is only association. Have you not heard the saying of the righteous servant: ﴿Indeed, association is a great wrong﴾?" [Luqman: 13].

So Allah, glory be to Him, judged for the monotheists with guidance and security, and for the polytheists with the opposite of that, which is misguidance and fear. Then He said:

﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Ibrahim against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.﴾ [Al-An'am: 83].

Abu Muhammad ibn Ḥazm said: "What the Sabians (al-Ṣābiʾah) adhered to was the oldest of religions over the course of time and the dominant one in the world, until they introduced innovations and altered its laws. So Allah sent to them Ibrahim, His friend, with the religion of Islam, which we follow today, and to correct what they had corrupted, and with the pure (samḥah) ḥanīfiyyah that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), brought to us from Allah, Exalted is He."

In that time and after it, they were called ḥunafāʾ.

I say: They are of two kinds: Sabians who are polytheists, and Sabians who are ḥunafāʾ, and there are debates between them.

Al-Shahrastani has recounted some of their debates in his book.

(Section)

His saying:

﴿And how should I fear what you have associated, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority? So which of the two groups is more deserving of security, if you know?﴾

He says to his people: how is it reasonable, to any intellect or to any person of understanding, that I should fear what you have made a partner to Allah in divinity, when it is neither a source of benefit nor of harm, while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah in His divinity things for which no proof has been sent down to you, nor has He legislated them for you? The one who associates with his Creator, Originator and Maker, whom they themselves acknowledge as the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Lord and Sovereign of all things, and the Master of harm and benefit, gods that create nothing, for they are created, and possess nothing for themselves or for their worshippers, neither harm nor benefit, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection; and he made them equals and likenesses to Him in divinity, worshipped, prostrated to, submitted to and drawn near to: such a person is more deserving of fear than the one who has not set up another god alongside Allah, but has made Him alone, singled Him out with divinity, lordship, greatness, sovereignty, love, fear and hope. So which of the two groups is more deserving of security, if you know? Thus Allah, glory be to Him, judged between them with the best judgment, to which hearts submit, natural dispositions affirm, and minds yield. He said:

﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing, for them is security, and they are rightly guided.﴾ [Al-An'am: 82].

Reflect on this speech and its wondrous placement in cutting down opponents, and its encompassing of everything the intellect requires to repel what they called to and wanted to impose. It grasps the argument from all its sides, leaving no critic a point of attack or a question.

Since it has this status, He, glory be to Him, indicated its mention and its greatness by pointing to it and attributing it to Himself, to magnify its matter. He said:

﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Ibrahim against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will.﴾ [Al-An'am: 83].

So the listener, from His attributing it to Himself, knows that it is He who gave His Friend understanding of it and taught it to him, and that the Friend received it from Him, Exalted is He. And it suffices for an argument that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught to His friend and beloved, to be decisive in cutting the roots of obstinacy and crushing the people of polytheism and atheism.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 89:

Al-wikala (agency, entrusting) is used to mean two things. The first is al-tawkil (entrusting someone as an agent), which is appointing a deputy and delegating authority. The second is al-tawakkul (trusting in God), which is the recognition, by way of acting as a deputy for the one who entrusts, that this is so from both sides. God, blessed and exalted, entrusts the servant and establishes him to guard what He has entrusted to him, and the servant entrusts his Lord and relies upon Him.

As for the Lord's entrusting of His servant, it is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But if these disbelieve in them, We have already entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them﴾ [al-An'am: 89].

Qatadah said: "We entrusted them to the eighteen prophets whom We mentioned," meaning before this verse. Abu Raja' al-Utaridi said: "Its meaning: if the people of the earth disbelieve in them, We have entrusted them to the people of the heavens, who are the angels." Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "They are the Ansar, the people of Madinah."

The correct view is that what is meant is those who upheld them (the revelations) through faith, calling (to them), striving (jihad) and support. These are the ones whom God entrusted with them.

If you say: Is it correct to say that someone is "the agent (wakil) of God"?

I say: No. For the wakil is one who acts on behalf of his principal by way of deputyship, and God, mighty and majestic, has no deputy, and no one succeeds Him. Rather, it is He who succeeds His servant, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Successor over the family."

Nevertheless, there is no objection to applying that term on the basis that He is commanded to guard what He has entrusted, to look after it and to attend to it.

As for the servant's entrusting of his Lord, it is his delegating his affairs to Him, withdrawing himself from acting independently, and affirming Him as the one entitled to and in charge of them. For this reason it has been said of tawakkul: it is the self's withdrawal from lordship and its standing in servitude. This is the meaning of the Lord being the wakil of His servant, that is, the one who suffices him and takes charge of his affairs and interests, because He acts as his deputy in managing them. So the Lord's entrusting of His servant is a command, an act of worship, a kindness toward him, and a robe of honour bestowed by Him upon him, not out of any need from Him or dependence upon him, just as His befriending (of His servants) is.

As for the servant's entrusting of his Lord, it is a submission to His lordship and a standing in His servitude.

The connection of creation to His complete power requires that no existing thing escapes His power; His connection to His complete knowledge requires that He encompasses it and precedes it in knowledge; and His connection to His wisdom requires that it occurs in the most perfect and best of ways, and that it includes the praiseworthy end desired by the Lord, exalted is He.

Likewise is the connection of His command to His knowledge, wisdom and might. He is All-Knowing regarding His creation and His command, All-Wise in His creation, and Mighty in His creation and His command. For this reason al-Hakim (the All-Wise) is among His Most Beautiful Names, and wisdom (al-hikmah) is among His Exalted Attributes. The Sharia that proceeds from His command is founded upon wisdom, and the Messenger sent with it was sent with the Book and wisdom. Wisdom is the Sunnah of the Messenger (ﷺ), and it includes knowledge of the truth, acting upon it, reporting about it, and commanding it. All of this is called wisdom. In a report it is said, "Wisdom is the lost property of the believer," and in a hadith: "Indeed, among poetry there is wisdom."

Just as nothing decreed escapes His knowledge, power and will, so likewise nothing escapes His wisdom and praise. He is praised for everything in existence, both good and evil, with a praise that He deserves by His very essence, and from which both His creation and His command proceed. So the source of all of that is wisdom. Denying wisdom is, in reality, a denial of His praiseworthiness, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 103:

So His saying ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ is among the strongest proofs of the abundance of His attributes and qualities. His saying ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾ is among the strongest proofs that He can be seen but cannot be encompassed. His saying ﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then He established Himself upon the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾

is among the strongest proofs of the distinction (mubayanah) of the Lord from His creation. For He did not create them within His essence; rather He created them outside of His essence. Then He became distinct from them by His establishment upon His Throne, while He knows what they are upon, sees them, and His sight encompasses them, and He surrounds them with knowledge, power, will, hearing and sight. This is the meaning of His being with them wherever they are.

Reflect on the excellence of this contrast in wording and meaning, and between His saying ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps [all] vision﴾. For He, in His greatness, is exalted above being grasped by vision or encompassed by it, and in His subtle kindness and expertise, He grasps vision, so nothing is hidden from Him. He is Great in His subtlety and Subtle in His greatness, High in His nearness and Near in His highness, the One whom nothing resembles, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps vision, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾.

(Section)

(The deficiency of the Mu'tazilah in understanding the speech of Allah)

From what has preceded regarding the limited scope of negation in ﴿lan﴾ and its extension in ﴿la﴾, the one granted success understands the deficiency of the Mu'tazilah in grasping the speech of Allah, the Exalted, for they took ﴿lan﴾ to indicate perpetual negation and argued with His saying: ﴿You will not see Me﴾. By this you know that their corrupt innovation stood between them and a proper understanding of the speech of Allah, and likewise every person of innovation you will find veiled from understanding the Qur'an.

Reflect on His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾, how He negated the act of perceiving with ﴿la﴾, which indicates the extension and perpetuity of negation, for He is never grasped, even though the believers will see Him; their sight does not grasp Him, exalted above being encompassed by any creature. And how He negated seeing with ﴿lan﴾, saying: ﴿You will not see Me﴾, because negation with it is not perpetual. Allah has refuted their claim that negation with ﴿lan﴾ is perpetual by His saying: ﴿And they said, "O Malik, let your Lord decree upon us"﴾, which is a wish for death. Had ﴿lan﴾ required perpetual negation, the speech would be self-contradictory, especially since it is paired with perpetuity in His saying: ﴿And they will never wish for it, ever﴾. But that does not contradict their wishing for it in the Fire, because "ever" may be meant as restricted perpetuity or as absolute perpetuity. Restricted perpetuity is limited by a period, such as the lifetime, as in your saying: "By Allah, I will never speak to him," while absolute is like your saying: "By Allah, I will never disbelieve in my Lord, ever." Given this, the verse only required the negation of wishing for death for the duration of the life of this world, and did not address the Hereafter at all, because they, out of love for life and aversion to recompense, do not wish for death; and this is absent in the Hereafter. Thus the speech of Allah should be understood in this way, not as the distorters understand it, removing words from their places.

Abu al-Qasim al-Suhayli said: "Moreover, I say that the Arabs use ﴿lan﴾ only to negate what was possible in the listener's estimation and presumed to be going to happen, so you say to him, 'Lan takuna,' for what he presumed would occur, because ﴿lan﴾ carries the meaning of 'an' (that not), and when the matter is in their view one of doubt rather than assumption, it is as if he is saying: 'Will it be or not?'"

I say: In negation, "lan yakun" is said, and all of this is said because of its composition from "la" and "in," and it becomes clear to you the reason it is specific in the Noble Qur'an to the places where it occurs instead of "la."

(Section)

As for adornment (tazyin), Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Thus We have made attractive to every community its deeds﴾. He also says: ﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good [equal to one guided]? Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. And He says: ﴿And Satan made their deeds attractive to them﴾. So He attributed the adornment to Himself, in terms of creation and will, and at times He omits its agent, and at times He ascribes it to its cause, and to the one through whose hand He causes it to occur. This adornment by Him, glorified is He, is good, for it is a trial and a test, that the obedient among them may be distinguished from the disobedient, and the believer from the disbeliever, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾. But it is ugly when it comes from Satan. Furthermore, His adorning the servant's evil deed for him is a punishment from Him for his turning away from His tawhid and worship, and for preferring evil deeds over good ones. For He must make him know the bad from the good. So when he prefers the ugly, chooses it, loves it and is pleased with it for himself, Allah adorns it for him and blinds him to seeing its ugliness after he had seen it as ugly. Every wrongdoer, sinner and transgressor, Allah must show him his wrongdoing, sinfulness and transgression as ugly. Then, if he persists in it, the sight of its ugliness is lifted from his heart, so he may see it as good, as a punishment for him. For its ugliness is only revealed to him by the light that is in his heart, which is the proof of Allah against him. When he persists in his error and wrongdoing, that light departs, and he does not see its ugliness in the darkness of ignorance, transgression and wrongdoing. Yet, despite this, the proof of Allah stands against him through the message and through the first recognition. So the Lord's adornment (of evil) is justice, and His punishment is wisdom; Satan's adornment is seduction and wrongdoing. The former is the cause external to the servant, and the latter is the cause internal to him: his love, his hatred and his turning away. The Lord, glorified is He, is the Creator of all, and all occurs by His will and power. Had He willed, He would have guided all His creatures. The one protected is he whom Allah protects, and the one forsaken is he whom Allah forsakes. ﴿Surely, to Him belong creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

[Section: The evidences for prohibiting what leads to the forbidden]

The evidence for the prohibition is of several aspects. The first aspect: the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾.

So Allah the Exalted forbade reviling the gods of the polytheists, even though reviling would be an expression of anger, zeal for Allah, and humiliation of their gods, because it is a means (dhari'a, a pathway that leads) to their reviling Allah the Exalted. The benefit of abandoning the reviling of Him, the Exalted, outweighed the benefit of our reviling their gods. This is like an indication, indeed like an explicit statement, of the prohibition of what is permissible, lest it become a cause for doing what is not permissible.

This is a commentary on verse 6:110, in the words of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim).

This is a continuation of His saying: ﴿And that if a sign came to them, they would not believe﴾. That is, We will come between them and faith, even if that sign came to them, and they would still not believe.

Scholars differed over His saying: ﴿as they did not believe in it the first time﴾. Many of the commentators (mufassirun) said: The meaning is that We will come between them and faith if the sign comes to them, just as We came between them and faith the first time. Ibn Abbas, in the narration of Ata' from him, said: "And We turn their hearts and their sights, until they return to what was decreed for them by My knowledge." He said: This is like His saying: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a person and his heart﴾.

Others said: The meaning is: "And We turn their hearts and their sights" as a punishment for their abandoning faith in it the first time, so We punished them by turning their hearts and their sights. This is a good meaning, for the particle of comparison (kaf al-tashbih) carries a kind of causation, as in His saying: ﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾, and His saying: ﴿Just as We sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you Our verses, purifying you, teaching you the Book and wisdom, and teaching you what you did not know. So remember Me, I will remember you﴾.

What makes the combination of causation and comparison good is the informing that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, in good and in evil.

Taqlib (turning) is changing a thing from one aspect to another. The requirement of the revelation of the verse and their reaching it, as they asked, was that they should believe when it came to them, because they saw it with their own eyes, knew its proofs, and confirmed its truth.

So when they did not believe, that was a turning of their hearts and sights away from the state in which they ought to be.

Muslim related in his Sahih, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The hearts of all the children of Adam are between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, like one heart; He turns it however He wills." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, Turner of the hearts, turn our hearts to Your obedience."

Al-Tirmidhi related from the hadith of Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to often say: 'O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have believed in you and in what you brought. Do you fear for us?' He said: 'Indeed, hearts are between two fingers of Allah; He turns them however He wills.'"

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith.

Hammad related from Ayyub, Hisham, and Ya'la ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan, who said: Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "It was a supplication the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) often used to make: 'O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, it is a supplication you often make?' He said: 'There is no servant except that his heart is between two fingers of Allah. If He wills to keep it upright, He keeps it upright, and if He wills to make it deviate, He makes it deviate.'"

As for His saying: ﴿And We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, Ibn Abbas said: "I forsake them and leave them in their misguidance, going on in their excess."

As for the adornment (tazyin) being attributed to Him, the Glorified: it is by His creation and will. Its agent is sometimes omitted, sometimes attributed to its cause, and sometimes to the one through whose hand it occurs.

This adornment from Him, the Glorified, is good, for it is a trial and test for the servant, so that the obedient among them is distinguished from the disobedient, and the believer from the disbeliever, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾. But adornment from Satan is ugly.

Also, His adorning the servant's evil deed is a punishment from Him for his turning away from His Tawhid and His worship, and his preferring bad deeds over good ones. For He, the Glorified, must make the bad distinct from the good for him. So when he prefers and chooses the ugly, loves it, and is pleased with it for himself, He adorns it for him and blinds him from seeing its ugliness after he had seen it as ugly. Every oppressor, sinner, and wrongdoer, Allah the Exalted must show him his oppression, sinfulness, and wickedness as ugly. But if he persists in it, the sight of its ugliness is removed from his heart. Sometimes he sees it as good, as a punishment for him, because the ugliness is only revealed to him by the light within his heart, which is Allah's proof against him. If he persists in his error and oppression, that light departs, and he does not see its ugliness in the darkness of ignorance, sinfulness, and oppression. Yet despite this, Allah's proof stands against him through the message and through the first informing.

So the Lord's adornment, the Exalted, is justice, His punishment is wisdom, and Satan's adornment is seduction and wrongdoing. It is the external cause outside the servant, while the internal cause is his love, his hatred, and his turning away. The Lord, the Glorified, is the Creator of all, and all occurs by His will and power. Had He willed, He would have guided all of His creation. The protected one is the one Allah protects, and the forsaken one is the one Allah forsakes. Verily, to Him belong creation and command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.

(Benefit)

Beware, beware of two matters that have evil consequences:

The first: rejecting the truth because it opposes your desire. For you will be punished by the turning of the heart, and whatever truth comes to you will be rejected outright; you will not accept it unless it appears in the mold of your desire. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾. So He punished them for rejecting the truth the first time by turning their hearts and sights afterwards.

The second: neglecting a command when its time comes. For if you neglect it, Allah will hold you back and keep you from His pleasure and His commands, as a punishment for you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, then say: "You will never go out with me, nor will you fight an enemy with me. You were pleased with sitting [at home] the first time, so sit with those who stay behind."﴾

Whoever is safe from these two great afflictions and calamities, may he rejoice in his safety.

(Section: Sins may forsake their doer at death, so they come between him and a good ending)

Indeed Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, punishes an evil deed with another evil deed, and the punishments for evil deeds multiply one upon another, just as He rewards a good deed with another good deed.

If you look at the condition of many of the dying, you will find that they are prevented from a good ending, as a punishment for their evil deeds.

The hafiz (a title for a master of hadith) Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ishbili, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"Know that the causes of a bad ending, from which Allah protect us, have ways and doors. The greatest of them is being absorbed in this world, turning away from the Hereafter, and boldness and audacity in disobeying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Sometimes a kind of sin, a type of disobedience, a side of aversion, and a share of audacity dominate a person; it takes over his heart, captivates his intellect, extinguishes his light, and lets down its veils upon him, so that no reminder benefits him and no admonition succeeds with him. Death may come upon him in that state; he hears the call from a far place, and the meaning is not clear to him, nor does he know what is intended, even if the caller repeats and repeats."

He said: It is related that a man among the people of al-Nasir (a ruler) was approaching death, and his son kept saying: "Say: there is no god but Allah." He said: "Al-Nasir is my master." He repeated the words to him, and he repeated the same. Then he was overcome by unconsciousness, and when he recovered he said: "Al-Nasir is my master." This was his habit: whenever he was told, "Say: there is no god but Allah," he said: "Al-Nasir is my master." Then he said to his son: "O so-and-so, al-Nasir only knows you by your sword. Killing, killing!" Then he died.

Abd al-Haqq said: It was said to another, whom I knew: "Say: there is no god but Allah." He began saying: "The house of so-and-so, fix this and that in it; the garden of so-and-so, do such-and-such with it."

He said: Among what Abu Tahir al-Salafi permitted me to narrate from him: a man was approaching death, and it was said to him: "Say: there is no god but Allah." He began saying in Persian: "Dah yazdah, dah wazdah," its meaning: "Ten with eleven."

It was said to another: "Say: there is no god but Allah," and he began saying:

Where is the road to the Bath of Minjab?

He said: This speech has a story. A man was standing in front of his house, whose door resembled the door of this bath. A girl with a beautiful appearance passed by him and said: "Where is the road to the Bath of Minjab?" He said: "This is the Bath of Minjab." She entered the house, and he entered behind her. When she found herself in his house and knew that he had deceived her, she showed him joy and delight at being with him, and said to him: "It would be good if there were with us what makes our life pleasant and our eyes content." He said to her: "Right now I will bring you everything you want and desire," and he went out, leaving her in the house without locking it. He took what was suitable and returned, but found that she had gone out and left, and had not betrayed him in anything. The man was bewildered and kept remembering her. He walked through the roads and alleys, saying:

O how many a speaker one day, who was wearied, how is the road to the Bath of Minjab?

One day, while he was saying this, his slave-girl answered him from a window:

Would that you had, when you won her, placed a guard over the house or a lock on the door!

His bewilderment increased and intensified, and he remained in that state until this line was the last of his words from the world.

Sufyan al-Thawri wept one night until morning. When morning came, he was asked: "All this out of fear of sins?" He took a straw from the ground and said: "Sins are easier than this. I weep only from fear of a bad ending."

This is one of the greatest understandings (fiqh): that a man fears his sins will forsake him at death, coming between him and a good ending.

Imam Ahmad mentioned from Abu al-Darda' that when he was dying, he kept fainting and then recovering, reciting: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am: 110].

From this, the early generations (al-salaf) feared sins, lest they become a veil between them and a good ending.

He said: Know that a bad ending, from which Allah the Exalted protect us, does not befall one whose outward is upright and whose inward is sound; this has not been heard of nor known, and praise be to Allah. It only befalls one who has corruption in belief, or persistence in major sins and boldness in grave matters. Often this dominates him until death comes upon him before repentance, seizing him before the setting right of his inner intention, and overwhelming him before turning back to Allah. Then Satan prevails over him at that shock and snatches him at that bewilderment. We seek refuge in Allah.

He said: It is related that there was a man in Egypt who was devoted to a mosque for the call to prayer and the prayer, and upon him was the radiance of obedience and the lights of worship. One day he climbed the minaret as usual for the call to prayer. Beneath the minaret was the house of a Christian, and he looked into it and saw the daughter of the owner of the house, and was tempted by her. He abandoned the call to prayer, came down to her, and entered the house to her. She said to him: "What is your business and what do you want?" He said: "I want you." She said: "For what?" He said: "You have captivated my intellect and taken hold of my heart." She said: "I will never answer you in an illicit matter." He said: "Shall I marry you?" She said: "You are a Muslim and I am a Christian, and my father will not marry me to you." He said: "I will become a Christian." She said: "If you do, I will do it." So the man became a Christian in order to marry her, and he stayed with them in the house. But in the midst of that day, he climbed to a roof that was in the house, fell from it, and died. He did not attain her, and he lost his religion.

He said: It is related that a man fell in love with a person and his passion for him grew intense, and his love settled in his heart, until pain afflicted him and he was confined to bed because of it. That person rejected him and his aversion increased. The go-betweens kept going back and forth between them until he promised to visit him. The people informed him of this, and he rejoiced, his joy intensified, and his grief was lifted. He began waiting for the appointed time that had been set for him. While he was in that state, the messenger between them came to him and said: "He went with me part of the way and then turned back. I begged him and spoke with him, and he said: 'He mentioned me and declared himself, but I will not enter the places of suspicion nor expose myself to the sites of accusation.' I insisted with him, but he refused and left." When the wretched man heard this, he was crushed, and returned to a worse state than before. Signs appeared upon him, and in that condition he began saying:

O Salm, O comfort of the sick, and O healing of the emaciated, wasted one!

Your pleasure is dearer to my heart than the mercy of the Creator, the Majestic.

I said to him: "O so-and-so, fear Allah." He said: "It has already happened." I left him, and I had not yet passed the door of his house when I heard the cry of death. We seek refuge in Allah from a bad outcome and the ill omen of a bad ending.

(Section)

As for the lam in His words, ﴿and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾,

it retains its original function of indicating purpose (ta'lil). If it is taken as giving the reason for the enemies' action, which is the whispering of some of them to others, then the meaning is clear. On this reading it is conjoined to His words, ﴿as deception﴾, for that is a object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), meaning: so that they may deceive them by this inspired speech, and so that the hearts of those to whom it is conveyed may incline to it, approve of it, and act according to its requirements. In this case, the Exalted has informed us of their intended aims in the aforementioned whispering, which are four: the deception of those to whom they whisper, the inclination of their hearts toward them, their love for this, and their being affected by it so as to commit the sin.

If, however, it gives the reason for God, Exalted is He, making every prophet an enemy, then this ruling is among the ends and wisdoms sought by this appointment. It is an end and a wisdom intended for the sake of something else, because it leads to matters that are beloved and desired by the Lord, Exalted is He, and the loss of these would entail the loss of what is even more beloved to Him than their occurrence. On both interpretations, the lam is the lam of causation and wisdom.

**Section: The Wisdom in Treating the Slaughter of a Non-People-of-the-Book Like Carrion**

As for the grouping of the slaughter of a non-scriptuary (*ghayr al-kitabi*) with carrion (*maytah*) in prohibition, and of the game killed by a person in the state of ihram with carrion of game, what difference is there in that? It seems the questioner thought that since the blood was retained in carrion, which made it forbidden, and the blood of what was slaughtered by a person in ihram or by a non-scriptuary unbeliever was not retained, there is no reason to forbid it. This is an error and an ignorance. If the cause of prohibition were confined to the retention of blood, the question would have some basis. But when the causes of prohibition are multiple, the absence of some of them does not necessarily entail the absence of the ruling when another cause takes its place. This is a consistent principle in rational causes and reasons.

So what is objectionable about this in the Sacred Law (*shari'ah*)?

If it is said: Has the Sacred Law not equated the two in being carrion, although they differ in the cause of death? It thus combined things that differ and separated things that are alike, for the slaughter is one in form, in sensory reality and in essence. Some of its forms were made a means of exempting the animal from being carrion, and some of its forms were made to necessitate its being carrion, without any distinction.

It is said: The Sacred Law did not equate the two in the linguistic meaning of the term carrion. It equated them only in the legal term. Thus the term carrion in the Sacred Law is more general than in the language. The Lawgiver (*al-Shari'*) deals with linguistic terms sometimes by transferring their meaning (*naql*), sometimes by generalizing them (*ta'mim*), and sometimes by specifying them (*takhsis*). The people of custom (*ahl al-'urf*) also act in this way. So this is not objectionable in the Sacred Law or in custom.

As for combining the two in prohibition, it is because Allah, glory be to Him, has forbidden us the foul things (*al-khaba'ith*). The foulness that necessitates prohibition may be apparent to us and may be hidden. What was apparent, the Lawgiver did not set up any sign for except its attribute. What was hidden, He set up a sign indicating its foulness. The retention of blood in carrion is an apparent cause. As for the slaughter of a Magian, an apostate, one who omits the invocation of the name of Allah, and one over whose slaughter a name other than Allah was invoked, the very act of slaughter by these people imparted to the slaughtered animal a foulness that necessitated its prohibition. One does not deny that invoking the names of idols, stars and jinn over the slaughtered animal imparts foulness to it, and that invoking the name of Allah alone imparts goodness to it, except for those whose share of the realities of knowledge and faith and of the taste of the Sacred Law is small. Allah, glory be to Him, has made what the name of Allah was not mentioned over among the slaughtered animals a matter of defiance (*fisq*), which is the foul. There is no doubt that invoking the name of Allah over the slaughtered animal makes it good and drives Satan away from the slaughterer and the slaughtered. When the name of Allah is neglected, Satan clings to the slaughterer and the slaughtered, and this has an effect of foulness on the animal. Satan runs through the channels of the blood of the animal, and the blood is his vehicle and carrier, and it is the most foul of foul things. When the slaughterer mentions the name of Allah, Satan leaves with the blood, and the slaughtered animal becomes good. When he does not mention the name of Allah, the foulness does not leave.

As for when he mentions the name of his enemy among the devils and idols, this imparts to the slaughtered animal another kind of foulness.

This is clarified by the fact that slaughter takes the place of worship, which is why Allah, glory be to Him, joins them together, as in His saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ [al-Kawthar: 2], and His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am: 162]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And the camels — We have made them for you among the symbols of Allah; in them is good for you. So mention the name of Allah over them as they stand in lines. And when their sides fall [after slaughter], eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar. Thus We have subjected them to you that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Hajj: 36], ﴿Their meat will not reach Allah, nor their blood, but piety from you will reach Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 37]. He informed that He subjected them only for the one who mentions His name over them, and that piety reaches Him, and piety is drawing near to Him through them and mentioning His name over them. So when the name of Allah is not mentioned over them, the one who does so is forbidden to eat them, and they become hateful to Allah. His hatred of them, since His name was not mentioned over them, or the name of someone else was mentioned over them, imparts to them the attribute of foulness, and so they become in the status of carrion. If this is the case for the one over which the name was not mentioned, and for the one over which the name of other than Allah was mentioned, then what his enemy, the polytheist who associates others with Allah, who is among the most wicked of creatures, slaughters is more deserving of prohibition. For the act, intention and foulness of the slaughterer cannot be denied to affect the slaughtered animal, just as the foulness, character and intention of the husband affect the wife he marries.

These are matters that only one believes in whom the light and radiance of the Sacred Law has shone, whose heart has been touched by the joy of its wisdoms and the benefits it contains for hearts and bodies, who has received them pure from the niche of prophethood, and who has firmly bound them to the Names and Attributes, whose light of realities has not been obscured by the darkness of interpretation and distortion.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 122 (part 1 of 7):

He combined for him light and life, just as He combined for the one who turned away from His Book death and darkness.

Ibn 'Abbas and all the exegetes (mufassirun) said: he was a disbeliever, astray, and We guided him.

His saying ﴿And We made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾ includes several matters:

The first: he walks among the people with the light while they are in darkness. His example and theirs is like a people over whom the night has darkened, so they went astray and did not find the way, while another has with him a light by which he walks along the path, sees it, and sees what he should beware of in it.

The second: he walks among them with his light, and they borrow from it because of their need for light.

The third: he walks with his light on the Day of Resurrection over the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), when the people of polytheism and hypocrisy remain in the darkness of their shirk and hypocrisy.

(Benefit)

His saying, majestic and exalted: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in the darkness, not coming out of it?﴾

He, glorified and exalted, gave him life by His spirit, which is His revelation, and it is the spirit of faith and knowledge. He made for him a light by which he walks among the people of darkness, as a man walks with a shining lamp in the dark. He sees the people of darkness in their darkness while they do not see him, like the seeing one who walks among the blind.

(Section)

On the fact that the life and illumination of the heart are the source of every good in it, and its death and darkness are the source of every evil and temptation in it.

The root of every good and happiness for the servant, indeed for every living rational being, is the perfection of its life and its light. Life and light are the source of all good. God, exalted, said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, not coming out of it?﴾ [al-An'am: 122].

So He combined the two roots: life and light. By life comes his strength, his hearing and sight, his modesty and chastity, his courage and patience, and all his noble character, and his love for what is good and his hatred for what is ugly. Whenever his life grows strong, these qualities grow strong in him, and when his life weakens, these qualities weaken in him. His modesty regarding ugly things is in proportion to his life within himself. So the sound, living heart, when ugly things are presented to it, recoils from them by its nature, hates them, and does not turn toward them. This contrasts with the dead heart, which does not distinguish between good and ugly, as 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Ruined is the one who has no heart by which he recognizes the good and rejects the evil."

Likewise the heart sick with desire: because of its weakness, it inclines toward whatever is presented to it, according to the strength or weakness of the sickness.

Likewise, when its light and illumination strengthen, the forms of known things and their realities are revealed to it as they truly are. So it perceives the beauty of the beautiful by its light, prefers it with its life, and likewise the ugliness of the ugly. God, glorified and exalted, mentioned these two roots in several places in His Book.

He, exalted, said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

So He combined the spirit, by which life is achieved, and the light, by which illumination and radiance are achieved. He informed that His Book, which He sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ), contains both matters. It is a spirit by which hearts live, and a light by which they are illuminated and shine, as He, exalted, said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, not coming out of it?﴾ [al-An'am: 122].

That is: is one who was a disbeliever, dead of heart, submerged in the darkness of ignorance, and We guided him to his right course, granted him faith, and made his heart alive after its death, radiant and illuminated after its darkness? He made the disbeliever, because of his turning away from obedience to Him, his ignorance of knowing Him, His Oneness and the laws of His religion, his abandonment of his share of His pleasure, and his failure to act upon what leads to his salvation and happiness, like the dead person who benefits himself by nothing and repels from himself no harm. We guided him to Islam and revived him through it, so he came to know the harms and benefits of his own self, and works to free himself from the wrath and punishment of Allah, the Exalted. He saw the truth after his blindness to it, recognized it after his ignorance of it, followed it after his turning away from it, and attained a light and radiance by which he is illuminated, and he walks with his light among the people while they are in the gloom of darkness, as it was said:

Your face, Layla, is radiant,
and its darkness walks among the people.

The people are in the shadows of darkness,
while we are in the light of day.

(Section: Remembrance and the reality of the divine light)

Remembrance of God is a light for the one who remembers in this world, a light for him in his grave, and a light for him in his return, running before him on the Sirat. Hearts and graves have never been illuminated by anything like the remembrance of God, exalted. God, exalted, said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, not coming out of it?﴾

The first is the believer, illuminated by faith in God, His love, His knowledge and His remembrance. The other is the one heedless of God, turning away from His remembrance and love. The whole matter, the whole success, lies in the light, and the whole misery lies in its loss.

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) used to exceed in asking his Lord, blessed and exalted, that He place light in his flesh, bones, nerves, hair, skin, hearing and sight, above him and below him, to his right and to his left, behind him and before him, until he would say: "and make me light." So he asked his Lord, blessed and exalted, to place light in his outward and inward particles, to make it encompass him from every direction, and to make his very self and entirety light. The religion of Allah, mighty and majestic, is light; His Book is light; His Messenger is light; His abode which He prepared for His friends is a shining light; He, blessed and exalted, is the light of the heavens and the earth; among His names is al-Nur (the Light); and the darkness was lit up by the light of His Face.

In the Prophet's (ﷺ) supplication on the day of al-Ta'if: "I seek refuge in the light of Your Face, by which the darkness is lit up and by which the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, that Your anger descend upon me or Your wrath come down upon me. To You is the blame until You are pleased, and there is no power nor strength except by You."

And Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "With your Lord there is no night nor day; the light of the heavens is from the light of His Face."

[Section: The reality of life]

The author of al-Manazil (Manazil al-Sa'irin) said:

(Chapter on Life) Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life?﴾ [al-An'am: 122].

His citing this verse in this chapter is very clear, for what is meant by it is one whose heart was dead by the absence of the spirit of knowledge, guidance and faith, and the Lord, exalted, gave him life by another spirit, other than the spirit by which He gave life to his body. That spirit is the spirit of knowing Him, His Oneness, His love, and worshipping Him alone with no partner. For the spirit has no life except by this, and otherwise it is among the dead. For this reason God, exalted, described the one who lacks that as dead, saying: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life?﴾ [al-An'am: 122], and He, exalted, said: ﴿Indeed you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ [al-Naml: 80].

His revelation was called a spirit, because of the life of hearts and spirits that is achieved by it. He, exalted, said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. So He informed that it is a spirit by which life is achieved, and a light by which illumination is achieved. He, exalted, said: ﴿He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that they warn that there is no god but Me, so fear Me﴾ [al-Nahl: 2], and He, exalted, said: ﴿Exalted in degrees, Owner of the Throne, He sends the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, to warn of the Day of Meeting﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. So revelation is the life of the spirit, just as the spirit is the life of the body. For this reason, whoever lacks this spirit has lost beneficial life in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, his life is the life of beasts, and he has a constricted livelihood. As for the Hereafter, he has Hell, where he neither dies nor lives.

God has made the good life for the people of His knowledge, love and worship. He, exalted, said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. The good life has been explained as contentment, satisfaction, good provision, and other things. The correct view is that it is the life of the heart, its bliss, its joy and its happiness through faith, knowledge of God, love of Him, turning to Him in repentance, and reliance upon Him. There is no life better than the life of its possessor, and no bliss above his bliss except the bliss of Paradise. As one of the knowers used to say: "There pass over me moments in which I say: if the people of Paradise are in such a state, then they are indeed in a good life." Another said: "There pass over the heart moments in which it dances with joy."

When the life of the heart is a good life, the life of the limbs follows it, for it governs them. For this reason God made the constricted livelihood the lot of the one who turns away from His remembrance, and it is the opposite of the good life.

This good life exists in the three abodes, that is: the abode of this world, the abode of the barzakh (intermediate state), and the abode of permanence. The constricted livelihood also exists in the three abodes. The righteous are in bliss here and there, and the wicked are in the Blaze here and there.
