God, exalted, said: ﴿For those who do good in this world there is a good reward, and the abode of the Hereafter is better﴾ [al-Nahl: 30], and He, exalted, said: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness of your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy a good provision until an appointed term and will give every person of virtue his virtue﴾ [Hud: 3].

So the remembrance of God, glorified and exalted, His love, His obedience, and turning to Him guarantee the best life in this world and the Hereafter, while turning away from Him, heedlessness, and disobedience to Him entail a troubled life and a constricted livelihood in this world and the Hereafter.

[The life intended here is three things]

[Section: The first life is the life of knowledge from the death of ignorance, and it has ten levels]

The author of al-Manazil said: Life in this chapter is referred to by three things. The first life is the life of knowledge from the death of ignorance, and it has three breaths: the breath of fear, the breath of hope, and the breath of love.

His saying "Life in this chapter" means: the special life which the people (of Sufism) speak about, not the general life shared by all animals, indeed shared by animals and plants. Life has levels, and we point to them.

The first level: the life of the earth through plants. God, exalted, said: ﴿God sent down water from the sky, and by it gave life to the earth after its death. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen﴾ [al-Nahl: 65]. He said about water: ﴿And by it We brought to life a dead land; thus is the emergence﴾ [Qaf: 11]. And He said: ﴿And We sent down from the sky pure water to give life thereby to a dead land﴾ [al-Furqan: 48]. He made this life a sign of life on the Day of Return. This is real life at this level, used in every language, current on the tongues of the elite and the common people. A poet praising 'Abd al-Muttalib said:

By the whiteness of praise, Allah gave life to our land
when we lost the rain, and the rain-clouds passed by.

This is more than can be cited in its examples.

The second level: the life of growth and nourishment. This life is shared by plants and by animals that live by food. God, exalted, said: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30].

The jurists have differed about whether hair (sha'r) is touched by life, on two views. The correct view is that it is touched by the life of growth and nourishment, but not by sensation and movement. For this reason it is not made impure by death, for if the separation from growth and nourishment made it impure, plants and trees would be impure when this life departs from them. For this reason the majority held that hair is not made impure by death.

The third level: the life of animals that feed with an additional measure beyond their growth and nourishment, which is their sensation and movement. For this reason they feel pain when painful conditions come upon them, and when connections are severed, and the like. This life is above the life of plants. This life grows strong and weak in the same animal according to its conditions. Its life after birth is more perfect than when it was a fetus in its mother's womb, and its life when it is healthy and well is more perfect than when it is sick and ill.

The very essence of this life varies greatly among its bearers. The life of a snake is more perfect than the life of a gnat. Whoever says otherwise has contradicted sense and reason.

The fourth level: the life of the living being that does not feed on food and drink, like the life of the angels and the life of spirits after their separation from their bodies. Their life is more perfect than the life of the feeding animal. For this reason no weariness or languor afflicts them, nor sleep or exhaustion. God, exalted, said: ﴿They glorify Him night and day, and they do not tire﴾ [al-Anbiya': 20]. Likewise, when spirits are freed from these bodies and become detached, they have another life, more perfect than this one if they are blessed. If they are wretched, they are laboring and toiling in punishment.

The fifth level: the life to which the author refers, which is the life of knowledge from the death of ignorance. Ignorance is a death for its possessors, as it was said:

Before physical death there is a death for its people in ignorance,
and their bodies are graves before the graves.

And their spirits are in loneliness away from their bodies,
so for them there is no resurrection until the Resurrection.

Indeed, the ignorant person is dead in heart and spirit. Even if his body is alive, his body is a grave walking upon the face of the earth. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people, like one who is in darkness from which he cannot emerge?﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur'an, to warn whoever is alive and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69-70]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ [al-Naml: 80]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, and you cannot make hear those who are in the graves﴾ [Fatir: 22].

He (Allah) likened the people whose hearts are dead to the people of the graves, for their spirits have died and their bodies have become graves for them. Just as the people of the graves cannot hear, so too these people cannot hear. Since life is perception and movement and what necessarily accompanies them, these hearts, because they do not perceive knowledge and faith and do not move toward them, are truly dead. This is not a metaphor likening their death to the death of the body; rather, it is the death of the heart and the spirit.

Imam Ahmad mentioned in the Kitab al-Zuhd (Book of Asceticism) from the words of Luqman that he said to his son: "O my son, sit with the scholars and press close to them with your knees, for Allah gives life to hearts with the light of wisdom, just as He gives life to the earth with heavy rain." Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "Learn knowledge, for learning it is fear of Allah, seeking it is worship, studying it is glorification (of Allah), researching it is struggle (jihad), teaching it to one who does not know it is charity, and giving it to its people is an act of drawing near (to Allah). For it is the markers of the lawful and the unlawful, the beacon of the paths of the people of Paradise. It is the companion in loneliness, the friend in estrangement, the confidant in solitude, the guide in ease and hardship, the weapon against enemies, and the adornment among friends. Through it Allah raises peoples, making them leaders and imams in goodness, whose traces are followed, whose deeds are emulated, and whose opinions are final. The angels desire their companionship and wipe them with their wings. Every moist and dry thing seeks forgiveness for them, including the fish of the sea and its creatures, and the beasts of the land and its livestock. For knowledge is the life of hearts from ignorance and the lamps of sight from darkness. Through knowledge a servant reaches the stations of the righteous and the high ranks in this world and the Hereafter. Reflecting upon it equals fasting, and studying it equals standing in prayer at night. Through it kinship ties are maintained, through it the lawful is known from the unlawful. It is the leader of action, and action follows it; the fortunate are inspired to it, and the wretched are deprived of it." Narrated by al-Tabarani, Ibn Abd al-Barr and others. It has also been reported as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ), but the mawquf (ending with the Companion) is more authentic.

The purpose here is his statement: "For knowledge is the life of hearts from ignorance," so the heart is dead, and its life is through knowledge and faith.

The sixth level: the life of will and resolve.

Weakness of will and seeking is from weakness in the life of the heart. The more complete the life of the heart, the higher its resolve, and the stronger its will and love. For will and love follow awareness of the desired object. The soundness of the heart from the affliction that stands between it and its pursuit and will means that weakness in seeking and lassitude of resolve arises either from a deficiency in awareness and perception, or from the presence of an affliction that weakens life. Thus the strength of awareness and the strength of will are evidence of the strength of life, and their weakness is evidence of its weakness. Just as loftiness of resolve and sincerity of will and seeking are part of the perfection of life, they are also a means to attaining the most perfect and purest life. For a good life is only attained through lofty resolve, sincere love, and pure will. Accordingly, the good life is in proportion to these. The lowest of people in life are the lowest in resolve, the weakest in love and seeking. The life of animals is better than his life. As it has been said:

"Your day, O deceived one, is heedlessness and negligence,
and your night is sleep, and death is inevitably yours.
You toil for what you will later deny its consequence;
thus in this world the animals live."

"You are delighted by what perishes, and rejoice in wishes,
as the dreamer is deceived by pleasures in sleep."

The purpose here is that the life of the heart is through knowledge, will, and resolve. When people witness this in a man, they say: "He is alive of heart." The life of the heart is through constant remembrance and abandoning sins, as Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

"I saw that sins kill hearts,
and persistence in them brings humiliation.
Abandoning sins is the life of hearts,
and for your soul, disobeying them is best.
Did anything corrupt religion but kings,
and evil scholars and monks?
They sold their souls and did not profit,
and their price was not raised in the sale.
So they have grazed upon a carcass,
whose loss is evident to the one of understanding."

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) say: "Whoever persists in saying, 'O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting, there is no god but You,' every day between the Fajr Sunnah and the Fajr prayer, forty times, Allah will give life to his heart through it."

Just as Allah the Glorified made the life of the body depend upon food and drink, so the life of the heart depends upon constant remembrance, turning to Allah, abandoning sins, and freedom from heedlessness that lies heavy upon the heart. Attachment to base vices and desires that quickly cut off weakens this life, and the weakness continues to follow him until he dies. The sign of his death is that he no longer recognizes what is good and does not denounce what is evil. As Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "Do you know who is the dead-hearted one about whom it was said:

'He who dies and rests is not dead;
rather, the dead is the dead among the living.'"
They said: "And who is he?" He said: "The one who does not recognize good, nor denounce evil."

The true man is the one who fears the death of his heart, not the death of his body. Most people fear the death of their bodies, and do not care about the death of their hearts. They recognize from life nothing but natural life, and this is from the death of the heart and spirit. For this natural life is like a fleeting shadow, a plant that quickly dries, or a dream that appears real, but when one awakens, he realizes it was imagination. As Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If the life of this world, from beginning to end, were given to a single man, and then death came to him, he would be like one who sees in his sleep what pleases him, then awakens to find nothing in his hand." It has also been said: "Death is of two kinds: voluntary death and natural death. Whoever causes his self to die a voluntary death, his natural death will be a life for him." The meaning of this is that voluntary death is the suppression of destructive desires, the extinguishing of their burning fires, and the calming of their destructive passions. Then the heart and spirit become free to reflect upon what constitutes the servant's perfection and knowledge of Allah, and to occupy themselves with it. At that point he sees that preferring a fleeting shadow over pleasant, lasting life is the greatest of losses. But when desires come flooding in, pleasures are preferred, habits prevail, and nature rules, the heart then becomes either a humiliated captive, or a defeated one expelled from its homeland and resting place, which has no stability except in it, or a slain corpse, for which there is no pain in its wound. The best of its states is that it is in a battle, in which it sometimes gains and sometimes is overcome. When the servant dies his natural death, after it there is the life of his spirit through those beneficial sciences, righteous deeds, and virtuous states that he attained by causing his self to die. His life here will be according to his voluntary death in this abode.

This is a matter that none understand except the intelligent and wise among people, and none act upon its requirements except the people of lofty resolve and pure, noble souls.

The seventh level of the levels of life:

The life of character and praiseworthy qualities, which is a firmly established life for the one who possesses them. He does not strain to climb the degrees of perfection, nor does it burden him, because his character and qualities require it, such that if they were to leave him, he would be departing from what is part of his nature and disposition. The life of one who is naturally disposed to modesty, chastity, generosity, munificence, manliness, truthfulness, faithfulness and the like is more complete than the life of one who subdues his self and struggles against his nature until he becomes so. For this is like one afflicted by the causes of illness who treats them and overcomes them with their opposites, while the other is like one who has been cured of that.

The more perfect these characters are in their possessor, the stronger and more complete his life. For this reason, the trait of modesty (haya') is derived from life (hayah) both in name and reality. The most perfect of people in life are the most perfect in modesty. The lack of a person's modesty is from the lack of his life, for when the spirit dies, it does not feel the pain of ugly deeds and so does not feel shame from them. But when it is healthy in life, it feels this and becomes ashamed of it. Likewise, all virtuous characters and praiseworthy qualities follow the strength of life, and their opposites follow from its deficiency. For this reason, the life of the brave is more complete than the life of the coward, the life of the generous more complete than the life of the miser, and the life of the sharp and intelligent more complete than the life of the dull and sluggish. Therefore, since the Prophets, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them, were the most complete of people in life, to the extent that the strength of their life prevents the earth from consuming their bodies, they were the most complete of people in these characters, and then the best of their followers in order.

Now consider the life of "a mean oath-swearer, a humiliator, a spreader of slander, a hinderer of good, a transgressor, sinful, brutal and furthermore of illegitimate birth" [al-Qalam: 10-13], and compare it with the life of one who is generous, brave, pious, just, chaste and benevolent. You will find the former dead in comparison with the latter. How well the poet said:

"There is no good for a man in a life
if he is counted among the refuse of goods."

The eighth level of the levels of life: the life of joy and delight, and the coolness of the eye in Allah. This life only comes after attaining the sought object, in which the eye of the seeker finds coolness. There is no beneficial life for him without it. Around this life all people hover, and all of them have missed its path, taking roads that do not lead to it, but rather cut one off from it, except for a very few.

Thus the pursuit of everyone revolves around this life, and most of them are deprived of it.

The cause of their deprivation of it is weakness of intellect, discernment and insight, and weakness of resolve and will. For its raw material is insight and a leading guide, and a discerning resolve. Insight is like sight: it can be blindness, dimness, bleariness, and inflammation, or complete light and radiance. These afflictions may be innate from the start, or they may occur later through acquired causes.

The point is that this level of life is the highest of its levels. But how can one reach it whose intellect is taken captive in the lands of desires, whose hope is fixed on plucking pleasures, whose conduct proceeds on the worst habits, whose religion is consumed by sins and transgressions, whose resolve is stuck with lowly things, and whose creed is not received from the niche of prophethood?!

He is immersed in desires, overturned by doubts, turned away from the advisor, opposed to the guide, asleep to happiness, and his heart wanders in every valley. If he were to strip himself of his self, turn away from sharing in the company of his fellow kind, and come out of the narrowness of ignorance into the expanse of knowledge, out of the prison of desire into the courtyard of guidance, and from the filth of the self into the purity of holiness, he would see the familiarity in which he grew up, increased with its increase, strengthened with its strength, and gained honor in his own eyes and in the eyes of his kind through its attainment, as a speck blocking the eye of his insight, a bone stuck in the throat of his faith, and a disease spreading to his destruction.

If you say: "You have pointed to a life unfamiliar among the dead among the living. Can you describe its path, so that I may reach some of its tastes? For it has become clear to me that what we are in of life is an animal life, in which animals may surpass us through being free from the evils and disturbances and through soundness of outcome?"

"I say: By Allah's life, your longing for this life, and your seeking knowledge of it and recognition of it, is indeed a proof of your life, and that you are not among the dead.

The first step on its path is that you recognize Allah and be guided to Him by a path that connects you to Him, and that burns away the darknesses of natural disposition (ṭabʿ) with the rays of insight (baṣīrah). Thus there stands in his heart a witness of the witnesses of the Hereafter, so he is drawn toward it with his whole being, renounces attachments that perish, and diligently works at correcting repentance, at performing the commanded acts, outward and inward, and at abandoning the forbidden acts, outward and inward. Then he stands as a guard over his heart, not permitting it a passing thought that Allah dislikes, nor a passing thought of idle matters that do not benefit him. Thereby his heart is purified from the talk of the self (ḥadīth al-nafs) and its whisperings, so it is ransomed from its captivity and becomes free. Then his heart becomes alone with the remembrance of his Lord, His love, and turning to Him in repentance, and he emerges from among the houses of his natural disposition and self into the open space of solitude with his Lord and His remembrance, as it has been said:

"I go out from among the houses, perhaps I may
Speak to the self of you, in secret, alone."

Then his heart, his thoughts, and his inner talk become gathered upon the will of his Lord, the seeking of Him, and longing for Him.

If he is sincere in this, he is granted love of the Messenger (ﷺ), and his spiritual nature (rūḥāniyyah) takes control of his heart, so he makes him his imam, teacher, master, shaykh, and exemplar, just as Allah made him His prophet, messenger, and guide to Him. He studies his biography (sīrah) and the beginnings of his mission, and the manner in which revelation came down to him, and he knows his attributes, his character, and his manners in his movements, his stillness, his wakefulness, his sleep, his worship, and his dealings with his family and companions, until it is as if he were with him as one of his companions.

When his heart is firmly established in this, Allah opens up for him the understanding of the revelation sent down to him from his Lord, such that if he recites the surah, his heart witnesses what it was revealed for, what is intended by it, and his share of it specifically, of the blameworthy attributes, characters, and actions, so he strives to be rid of them just as one strives to be cured of a dangerous illness; and he witnesses his share of the praiseworthy attributes and actions, so he strives to perfect and complete them.

When he is able to do this, another eye is opened in his heart, by which he witnesses the attributes of the Lord, glorified is His majesty, until they become for his heart like the seen thing is for the eye. So he witnesses the loftiness of the Lord, glorified is He, above His creation, His istiwāʾ over His throne, the descent of the command from Him in the management of His kingdom, His speaking through revelation, His speaking to His servant Jibrīl with it, His sending it to whomever He wills with what He wills, and the ascent of affairs to Him and their presentation to Him.

So his heart witnesses a Lord who is dominant over His servants, commanding and forbidding, sending forth His messengers, sending down His books, worshipped and obeyed, having no partner, no like, and no equal, with no one having any share of the command along with Him; rather, the entire command belongs to Him. He witnesses his Lord, glorified is He, standing in sovereignty and management, so there is no movement nor stillness, no benefit nor harm, no giving nor withholding, no contracting nor expanding, except by His power and management. He witnesses the subsistence of the whole universe through Him, and His own subsistence through Himself, for He is the Self-Subsisting, who sustains all that is other than Him.

When his heart is firmly established in this, he witnesses the attribute that validates all the attributes of perfection, which is life, whose perfection necessitates the perfection of hearing, sight, power, will, speech, and all the other attributes of perfection, and the attribute of true self-subsistence (qayyūmiyyah), which validates all actions. So the Living, the Self-Subsisting, is the one who possesses every attribute of perfection, and He is the Doer of what He wills.

When his heart is firmly established in this, He opens for him the witnessing of nearness and companionship (maʿiyyah), so he witnesses Him, glorified is He, with him, not absent from him, near and not distant, while being above His heavens on His throne, separate from His creation, standing in creating, managing, and commanding. Thus there is attained for him, along with veneration and reverence, intimacy with this attribute. He becomes intimate with Him after having been lonely, strengthened by Him after having been weak, joyful with Him after having been sorrowful, and finds Him after having been lost. Then he tastes the flavour of the saying: "My servant does not cease to draw near to Me through supererogatory acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. Were he to ask Me, I would surely give him, and were he to seek refuge in Me, I would surely protect him."

So the best of life in absolute terms is the life of this servant, for he is a lover who is beloved, one who draws near to his Lord, and his Lord is near to him. His Beloved has become, due to the intensity of His dominion over his heart, his constant mention of Him, and his aspiration being devoted to His good pleasure, like his hearing, sight, hand, and foot, and these are the instruments of his perception, his action, and his striving. So if he hears, he hears by his Beloved; if he sees, he sees by Him; if he strikes, he strikes by Him; if he walks, he walks by Him.

If the meaning of this is difficult for you to grasp, and that the perfectly loving lover hears, sees, strikes, and walks by his beloved while his own self is absent from him, then turn away from it and leave this matter to its people:

"Leave passion to people known for it,
Who have endured love until its hardest part became easy."

The seeker to his Lord, his aspiration never ceases to be devoted to two matters: exhausting the heart in sincere love, and exerting effort in complying with the command. He continues thus until the signs of his knowledge of Him and the traces of His attributes and names appear upon his secret, but that is sometimes concealed from him and sometimes appears. It appears by the bounty of the Source, and it is concealed by the judgment of the lull (fatrah), and lulls are a necessary matter for the servant, for every doer has a surge of vigour (shirrah), and for every surge there is a lull. The highest of them is the lull of revelation, which belongs to the prophets; the lull of a special state belongs to the knowers (ʿārifīn); the lull of aspiration belongs to the seekers (murīdīn); and the lull of action belongs to the worshippers. In these lulls there are kinds of wisdom and mercy, divine self-disclosures, the making known of the worth of blessing, the renewal of longing for it, pure yearning for it, and other things.

Those witnesses continue to recur and increase until they settle, and his heart becomes dyed with them, and the lull no longer cuts him off; rather it becomes a blessing for him, a rest for him, a refreshment and a relief for him.

So the aspiration of the lover, when his spirit is attached to his Beloved, is devoted to increasing his love and the causes of its strength. He acts upon this, then he ascends from it to seeking his Beloved's love for him, and works to attain that. He does not lose the first seeking, nor ever leaves it; rather he enters into this second seeking, so his aspiration is attached to both matters together. For the station of "I was his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees" is only attained for him through this second matter, which is his being beloved to his Beloved, as He said in the hadith: "When I love him, I am his hearing and his sight," and so on. So he draws near to his Lord, preserving His love for him and seeking the love of his Lord for him.

Then he tightens the waistband of striving in seeking his Beloved's love for him through all kinds of drawing near to Him: his heart, for love, turning in repentance, trust, fear, and hope; his tongue, for remembrance and recitation of his Beloved's speech; and his limbs, for acts of obedience. So he does not cease to draw near to his Beloved.

This is the journey that leads to this goal, which cannot be attained except through it, and one cannot arrive at it except by this gate and this path. Then all the scattered elements of the spiritual path, of presence, awe, watchfulness, negation of thoughts, and emptying of the inner self, are gathered for him in his journey.

For the lover first begins with drawing near through outward acts, which is the outward aspect of drawing near; then he ascends from that to the state of drawing near, which is being drawn wholly to his Beloved with his spirit, heart, intellect, and body; then he ascends from that to the state of ihsan, so he worships Allah as if he sees Him. Then he draws near to Him from within through acts of the heart: love, turning in repentance, veneration, reverence, and awe. Then there arises from within him generosity in giving up the spirit, and generosity in loving his Beloved without strain, so he gives of his spirit, self, breaths, will, and actions to his Beloved as a state, not as an effort. When the lover finds this, he has attained the state of drawing near, its secret and its inner reality. If he does not find it, then he draws near only with his tongue, body, and outward self, so let him persist in that and force himself to draw near through remembrance and actions constantly, for perhaps he will be granted the state of nearness.

Beyond this inner nearness there is yet another matter, something that cannot be expressed better than in the words of the nearest of creation to Allah (ﷺ) concerning this meaning, where he relates from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He: "Whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; whoever draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running." This lover finds in his inner self a taste of the meaning of this hadith, a truly real taste.

He mentioned three degrees of nearness, and by them he alerted to what is below them and what is above them. He mentioned the servant's drawing near to Him by righteousness, and His drawing near to the servant a cubit; when the servant truly tastes this drawing near, he moves from it to the drawing near of the cubit, so he finds the taste of his Lord's drawing near to him a fathom.

When he tastes the sweetness of this second nearness, he then quickens his pace toward his Lord, so he tastes the sweetness of His coming to him running. Here is the end of the hadith, alerting that when His servant runs toward Him, the nearness of His beloved to him is beyond the servant's running toward Him. Either He has withheld the explanation of that because of the greatness of the witness of the reward, or because he enters into a reward that no ear has heard and no human heart has conceived; or it is a referral to the earlier degrees, as if it were said to him: "Measure by this." So in proportion to what you give of yourself drawing near to your Lord, He draws near to you with more than that. On this basis, the necessary consequence of this mentioned drawing near in its degrees is: whoever draws near to his Beloved with his spirit, all his faculties, his will, his words, and his actions, his Lord, glorified is He, draws near to him in Himself in return for his servant's drawing near to Him.

Nearness in all these degrees is not nearness of sensory distance nor of physical contact; rather it is a real nearness, while the Lord, exalted is He, is above His heavens on His throne, and the servant is on the earth.

This point is the secret of the path, the reality of servanthood, and it is the meaning of arrival (wuṣūl) around which the people revolve.

The foundation of this matter is the intention of drawing near first, then drawing near second, then the state of nearness third, which is being wholly propelled toward the Beloved.

The reality of this propulsion is: that you pass away in His purpose from your own desire, and in what comes from Him from your own portion; rather, that becomes the whole of your portion and your purpose. You know that whoever draws near to his Beloved with anything of things is rewarded with a nearness that is many times more. And you know that the highest kind of drawing near is the servant's drawing near with his whole self, outwardly and inwardly, and with his existence, to his Beloved. Whoever does that has drawn near with his whole being, and no remnant of him is left for anyone other than his Beloved, as it has been said:

"May there never be in him for other than You a remnant
By which the blamers find a way to him."

If the one drawn near to with deeds gives many times over what he is drawn near with, then what is thought of one who is given the state of nearness, its taste, and its ecstasy? What is thought of one who draws near to Him with his spirit, all his will, his aspiration, his words, and his actions?

On this basis, just as he gave himself to his Beloved, He is worthy of being given to in return, so that His glorified Lord becomes his portion and share, in place of everything, as a fitting recompense, for reward is of the same kind as the deed. There are many proofs of this.

Among them is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 2]. So He distinguished between the two rewards, as you see, and made the reward of the one who relies upon Him that He, glorified is He, is his sufficiency and protector."

**Among its benefits:** When the martyr gives up his life for Allah, Allah, glorified is He, grants him in return a life that is more complete, in His presence, in the place of His nearness and honour.

**Among its benefits:** Whoever gives something up for Allah, Allah gives him something better in return.

**Among its benefits:** His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you. Be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152].

**Among its benefits:** His saying in the divine hadith (al-Hadith al-Qudsi): "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it."

**Among its benefits:** His saying: "Whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit," and the rest of the hadith.

So the servant is always gaining from his Lord more than what he has offered Him. This one who draws near to Him with his heart, his spirit and his deeds, his Lord opens to him a life unlike the kinds of life that people have. Rather, the life of one who is not like this, compared to his life, is like the life of the foetus in its mother's womb compared to the life of the people of this world and their pleasure in it, and even greater than that.

This is the model of one who has surpassed the nobility and excellence of this life. Even if the knowledge of this brings its possessor a good life, how much more so if the heart is steeped in it and it becomes a state constantly joined to his essence! So Allah is the one sought for help.

This life is, in reality, the life of this world and its bliss. Whoever loses it, his losing his natural life is even more fitting for him. (Verse)

*This is the life of the young man; if it is lost,*
*his losing life is more fitting for him.*

So there is no life except the life of the lovers, those whose eyes are comforted by their Beloved, whose souls are at rest in Him, whose hearts are reassured by Him, who find intimacy in His nearness, and who delight in His love. In the heart there is a poverty that nothing fills except the love of Allah, turning towards Him and returning to Him, and its scattered state is gathered by nothing else at all. Whoever does not attain this has a life that is entirely worries and griefs, pains and regrets. If he has a lofty aspiration, his soul is torn apart by regret over the world, for his aspiration does not accept what is base in it. And if he is humble and lowly, his life is like the life of the most debased animals. So the eyes are comforted only by love of the First Beloved.

*Shift your heart wherever you wish among desires;*
*love is only for the First Beloved.*

*How many a dwelling on earth the young man has grown fond of,*
*yet his longing is always for the first dwelling.*

The ninth stage of the stages of life is the life of the spirits after their separation from the bodies and their release from this prison and its narrowness. For behind it there is spaciousness, rest, fragrance and comfort. The relation of this abode to it is like the relation of the mother's womb to this abode, or even closer than that. Some of the gnostics (al-ʿĀrifūn) said: "Let your haste to leave this world be like your haste to leave a narrow prison for your loved ones, and to gather with them in the gleaming gardens." Allah, exalted is He, said about this life: ﴿But if he is one of those brought near, then rest and provision and a Garden of bliss﴾ [al-Waqiʿah: 88].

What suffices for the goodness of this life is accompanying the Highest Companion, and being separated from the harmful companion who spoils life, whose sight and presence make life bitter, let alone associating with and living among him. (Accompanying) the Highest Companions, upon whom Allah has bestowed His favour: of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous, and how excellent those companions are, in the neighbourhood of the Lord, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

*I have said, when they praised life and went to excess,*
*that in death there are a thousand unknown virtues:*
*among them is the security of meeting Him in His meeting,*
*and the separation from every companion who is not fair.*

Even if death had no good in it except that it is the gate to entering this life and a bridge crossed to it, it would suffice as a gift for the believer.

*May Allah reward death on our behalf with good, for it*
*is kinder to us than every kindness and gentler.*
*It hastens the release of souls from harm*
*and brings them near to the abode that is more noble.*

So striving in this short life, in this brief span, with effort and toil, bearing burdens, weariness and hardship, is only for this life. Knowledge and deeds are a means to it. This is wakefulness, while what precedes it of life is sleep; this is (true) sight, while what precedes it is a trace. It is a life combining the absence of what is disliked and the attainment of what is loved, in a station of intimacy and the presence of holiness, where no sought thing is out of reach and no beloved is lost; where there is tranquillity and rest, joy and happiness; where the servant has no means of describing the reality of its essence, because it is in a land we have no acquaintance with, and there is no familiarity between us and its inhabitant. So the soul, through its familiarity with this narrow, wretched prison for a long time, dislikes moving from it to that land, and feels estranged when it senses separation from it.

The knowledge of this life has reached us only through a divine report, by the hand of the most perfect of creation, the most knowing of them and the most sincere, (ﷺ). Its evidences stood firm in the hearts of the people of faith, until they became for them like direct sight. So their souls fled from this fleeting shade, this vanishing phantom, and this transient life mixed with disturbance and all kinds of distress: desiring to turn away from this life, longing for that kingdom (al-Malakūt), ecstasy at this joy, rapture to this degree, and yearning for this breeze blowing from the place of lasting bliss.

By Allah's life, whoever travels to a land of justice, fertility, security and joy endures on his way every hardship, scarcity and drought. He leaves behind those who stay back, at the time he most needs them. He answers the caller when he calls, "Come to success." He spends himself in reaching it, giving himself out of love, with willingness and generosity. He persists in the journey morning and evening. So at arrival he praises his night journey, for the traveller only praises the night journey at dawn.

*At dawn people praise the night journey,*
*and at death people praise the meeting.*

By Allah, this is not difficult or hard, given this short life, which compared to that abode is like an hour of a day: ﴿As if they, on the day they see what they were promised, had not remained but an hour of a day﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 35]. ﴿And the day He gathers them, as if they had not remained but an hour of the day, recognising one another﴾ [Yūnus: 45]. ﴿As if they, on the day they see it, had not remained but an evening or a morning of it﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 46]. ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they remained but an hour﴾ [al-Rūm: 55]. ﴿He said, "How long did you remain on earth, counting years?" They said, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count." He said, "You remained but a little, if only you had known"﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 112–114]. So if one of us were dragged on his face, protecting himself with it from thorns and stones, to this life, that would not be much, nor a loss compared to what he is being spared.

Alas for the insight that has witnessed these two lives as they really are, and for the aspiration that prefers the lower over the higher! This is nothing but by the success of Him in whose hand are the reins of all affairs, from whom every thing begins and to whom it returns. He made the souls of those overcome by wretchedness sit down, unable to travel to this abode, and drew the hearts of those for whom the best (reward) had preceded from Him, and kept them on the path and made it easy for them to ride the dangers. So those wasted the stages of their lives with those who stayed behind, and these crossed the stages of their lives with the travellers. The dust settled and the dust cloud rose, and both the travellers and those who stayed behind disappeared from sight.

It will soon be revealed, and then the doers will triumph and the falsifiers will lose.

Among the sweetness and pleasure of this life: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No soul dies that has with Allah something good which would make it glad to return to the world and to have the world and all that is in it, except the martyr, for he wishes to return to the world because of the honour he sees from Allah for him," meaning that he may be killed in it once more.

One of the gnostics heard a reciter reciting:

*Life is only in the animal enjoyment of pleasure,*
*which is what the philosopher says.*
*The judgement of the cup of death is that in its drinking*
*the dull and the sharp are equal.*
*The fool ends up under the dust of the earth*
*just as the clever one ends up beneath it.*
*So ask the earth about them both, if the clear question*
*removes doubt and suspicion.*

He said: "May Allah fight him! How intensely he opposes religion and reason! This is the very enemy of the natural disposition (fiṭrah), the Law, reason, faith and wisdom. O poor man! Is it because death makes the righteous and the wicked, the knowing and the ignorant equal, and they all end up under the layers of the earth, that they must be equal in their final outcome? Do not people who travel from one land to another, when they reach their destination, each descend into a place prepared for him, and each is received in a manner different from his companion on the road? Does not every people have an abode, so that each one of them is seated where he is fitting? And is one thing met with something, and this with its opposite? Did not one who came to the king with what pleases him get honoured by him, and one who came with what angers him get punished by him? Did not a caravan arrive at the city, so some of them descended into its palaces, gardens and noble places, while others settled on the roadside among the dogs? Did not two come from the same mother's womb, one of them rising to kingship and the other to captivity and hardship?"

As for your saying, "Ask the earth about them both": we have indeed asked it, and it told us that it has gathered their bodies, their corpses and their limbs, not their disbelief and their faith, nor their lineages and their noble qualities, nor their forbearance and their foolishness, nor their obedience and their disobedience, nor their certainty and their doubt, nor their monotheism and their polytheism, nor their injustice and their justice, nor their knowledge and their ignorance. It told us about these decayed corpses, these dissolved bodies and these torn limbs, and said, "This is the news of what is with me."

As for the news of those spirits and what they have come to, ask about it the Books of the Lord of the worlds, His truthful messengers, and their successors who inherit (from them). Ask the Qur'an, for with it is the certain news. Ask the one who brought it, for he is the most knowing of the knowers about it. Ask knowledge and faith, for they are the two accepted witnesses. Ask the intellects and the natural dispositions, for with them is the reality of the news: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? How badly they judge﴾ [al-Jāthiyah: 21]. Exalted is Allah, the Wisest of judges, above this assumption and supposition, which is fitting only for the most ignorant of the ignorant.

Then he said: "The one who looks into this matter is of two kinds. One looks at things, and the other looks into things. The first is bewildered by them, for their forms, shapes and outlines empty his mind and senses, and scatter his thought and heart. So his looking at them is with the eye of the senses; he gains from them neither the fruit of consideration nor the cream of testing, because when he lacks consideration at the beginning, he also lacks choice afterwards.

As for the one who looks into things: his looking moves him to pass through their forms to their realities and what is intended by them, and what the existence of these things required of perfect wisdom and complete knowledge. This looking gives him the ability to distinguish their ranks, to know what is beneficial in them from what is harmful, the sound from the sick, the lasting from the transient, the husk from the kernel. He distinguishes between the means and the end, and between the means to a thing and the means to its opposite. Then he knows that this world is the husk and the Hereafter is the kernel, that this world is the place of sowing and the Hereafter the time of harvest, and that this world is a crossing and a passage, while the Hereafter is the abode of permanence."

وإذا عرف أنّ الدنيا طريقٌ ومَمَرٌّ، كان حَرِيًّا بتهيئة الزاد لقراره، ويعلم حينئذٍ أنه لم ينشأ في هذه الدار للاستيطان والخلود، ولكن للجَواز إلى مكان آخر، هو المنزل والمُتَبوَّأ. وأن الإنسان دُعِي إلى ذلك بكل شريعة، وعلى لسان كل نبيّ، وبكل إشارة ودليل، ونُصب له على ذلك علم، وضُرب لأجله كل مثل، ونُبِّه عليه بنشأته الأولى ومبادئه، وسائر أحواله، وأحوال طعامه وشرابه، وأرضه وسمائه، بحيث أُزيلت عنه الشبهة، وأُوضحت له المحجّة، وأُقيمت عليه الحجة، وأُعذر إليه غاية الإعذار، وأُمهل أتمّ الإمهال، فاستبان لذي العقل الصحيح والفطرة السليمة أن الظعن عن هذا المكان ضروريٌّ، والانتقال عنه حقٌّ لا مِرْيَة فيه، وأن له محلًّا آخر له قد أُنشئ، ولأجله قد خُلق، وله هُيِّئ، فمصيرُه إليه وقدومُه بلا ريب عليه، وأن داره هذه منزل عبور، لا منزل قرار.

وبالجملة: مَن نظر في الموجودات، ولم يقنع بمجرد النظر إليها وحدها، وجدها دالّةً على أن وراء هذه الحياة حياةً أخرى أكملَ منها، وأن هذه الحياة بالنسبة إليها كالمنام بالنسبة إلى اليقظة، وكالظلّ بالنسبة إلى الشخص، وسمعها كلها تنادي بما نادى به ربّها وخالقها وفاطرها: ﴿يا أيها الناس إن وعد الله حقٌّ، فلا تغرنّكم الحياة الدنيا، ولا يغرنّكم بالله الغرور﴾ [فاطر: 5]، وتنادي بلسان الحال بما نادى به ربّها بصريح المقال: ﴿واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماءٍ أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيمًا تذروه الرياح، وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرًا﴾ [الكهف: 45]. وقال تعالى: ﴿إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماءٍ أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام، حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازّيّنت وظنّ أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها، أتاها أمرنا ليلًا أو نهارًا، فجعلناها حصيدًا كأن لم تغنَ بالأمس، كذلك نفصّل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون﴾ [يونس: 24]. وقال تعالى: ﴿اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعبٌ ولهوٌ وزينةٌ وتفاخرٌ بينكم وتكاثرٌ في الأموال والأولاد، كمثل غيثٍ أعجب الكفارَ نباتُه ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرًّا ثم يكون حطامًا، وفي الآخرة عذابٌ شديد ومغفرةٌ من الله ورضوان، وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور﴾ [الحديد: 20]. ثم ندبهم إلى المسابقة إلى الدار الآخرة الباقية التي لا زوال لها، فقال: ﴿سابقوا إلى مغفرةٍ من ربكم وجنةٍ عرضها كعرض السماء والأرض، أُعدّت للذين آمنوا بالله ورسله، ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء، والله ذو الفضل العظيم﴾ [الحديد: 21].

وسمع بعض العارفين مُنشدًا يُنشد عن بعض الزنادقة عند موته، وهو محمد بن زكريا المُتطبِّب (الطبيب):
لَعَمْرِي ما أدري وقد أذِنَ البِلى ∗∗∗ بعاجل تِرحالي إلى أين تِرحالي
وأين محلّ الروح بعد خروجه ∗∗∗ عن الهيكل المُنحلّ والجسد البالي
فقال: وما علينا من جهله، إذا لم يدرِ أين ترحاله؟ ولكنّا ندري إلى أين ترحالنا وترحاله. أما ترحاله فإلى دار الأشقياء، ومحلِّ المنكرين لقدرة الله وحكمته، والمكذّبين بما اتفقت عليه كلمةُ المرسلين عن ربّهم: ﴿أولئك الذين كفروا بربهم، وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم، وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون﴾ - ﴿وقالوا أئذا ضللنا في الأرض أئنا لفي خلقٍ جديد؟ بل هم بلقاء ربهم كافرون﴾ - ﴿قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وُكِّل بكم، ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون﴾ - ﴿ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم، ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحًا إنا موقنون﴾ [السجدة: 5-12].

وأما ترحالنا أيها المسلمون المصدّقون بلقاء ربهم وكتبه ورسله، فإلى نعيمٍ دائم، وخلودٍ متصل، ومقامٍ كريم، وجنةٍ عرضها السماوات والأرض، في جوار ربّ العالمين، وأرحم الراحمين، وأقدر القادرين، وأحكم الحاكمين، الذي له الخلق والأمر، وبيده النفع والضر، الأول بالحق، الموجودُ بالضرورة، المعروفُ بالفطرة، الذي أقرّت به العقول، ودلّت عليه الموجودات، وشهدت بوحدانيته وربوبيته جميعُ المخلوقات، وأقرّت بها الفطر، المشهودُ وجودُه وقيوميتُه بكل حركةٍ وسكون، وبكل ما كان وما هو كائن وما سيكون، الذي خلق السماوات والأرض، وأنزل من السماء ماءً فأنبتنا به حدائقَ ذات بهجةٍ من أنواع النباتات، وبثّ به في الأرض جميعَ الحيوانات: ﴿أمّن جعل الأرض قرارًا وجعل خلالها أنهارًا وجعل لها رواسيَ وجعل بين البحرين حاجزًا﴾ [النمل: 61]، الذي يجيب المضطرّ إذا دعاه، ويغيث الملهوف إذا ناداه، ويكشف السوء ويفرّج الكربات، ويُقيل العثرات، الذي يهدي خلقه في ظلمات البرّ والبحر، ويرسل الرياح بشرًا بين يدي رحمته، فيُحيي الأرضَ بوابل القطر، الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده، ويرزق من في السماوات والأرض من خلقه وعبيده، الذي يملك السمع والأبصار والأفئدة، ويُخرج الحيَّ من الميت، ويُخرج الميتَ من الحي، ويدبّر الأمر: ﴿قل من بيده ملكوت كل شيءٍ وهو يُجير ولا يُجار عليه؟﴾ - ﴿الذي له ملكُ السماوات والأرض، ولم يتخذ ولدًا، ولم يكن له شريكٌ في الملك، وخلق كل شيءٍ فقدّره تقديرًا﴾ [الفرقان: 88-2]، المستعان به على كل نائبةٍ وفادحة، والمعهودُ منه كلُّ برٍّ وكرامة، الذي عنت له الوجوه، وخشعت له الأصوات، وسبّحت بحمده الأرضُ والسماوات وجميعُ الموجودات، الذي لا تسكن الأرواح إلا بحبّه، ولا تطمئن القلوب إلا بذكره، ولا تزكو العقول إلا بمعرفته، ولا يُدرك النجاح إلا بتوفيقه، ولا تحيا القلوب إلا بنسيم لطفه وقربه، ولا يقع أمرٌ إلا بإذنه، ولا يهتدي ضالٌّ إلا بهدايته، ولا يستقيم ذو أوَد إلا بتقويمه، ولا يفهم أحدٌ إلا بتفهيمه، ولا يُتخلّص من مكروهٍ إلا برحمته، ولا يُحفظ شيءٌ إلا بكلاءته، ولا يُفتتح أمرٌ إلا باسمه، ولا يتمّ إلا بحمده، ولا يُدرك مأمولٌ إلا بتيسيره، ولا تُنال سعادةٌ إلا بطاعته، ولا حياةٌ إلا بذكره ومحبّته ومعرفته، ولا طابت الجنة إلا بسماع خطابه ورؤيته، الذي وسع كل شيءٍ رحمةً وعلمًا، وأوسع كل مخلوقٍ فضلًا وبرًّا.

فهو الإله الحق، والرب الحق، والملك الحق، والمنفرد بالكمال المطلق من كل الوجوه، المبرَّأ عن النقائص والعيوب من كل الوجوه، لا يبلغ المثنون وإن استوعبوا جميع الأوقات بكل أنواع الثناء ثناءً عليه، بل ثناؤه أعظم من ذلك، فهو كما أثنى على نفسه، هذا الجار.

وأما الدار: فلا تعلم نفسٌ حسنَها وبهاءَها، وسعتَها ونعيمَها، وبهجتَها وروحَها وراحتَها، فيها ما لا عينٌ رأت، ولا أذنٌ سمعت، ولا خطر على قلب بشر، فيها ما تشتهي الأنفس، وتلذّ الأعين، فهي الجامعة لجميع أنواع الأفراح والمسرّات، الخالية من جميع المنكِّدات والمنغِّصات، ريحانةٌ تهتزّ، وقصرٌ مُشيَّد، وزوجةٌ حسناء، وفاكهةٌ نضيجة.

فترحالنا أيها الصادقون المصدِّقون إلى هذه الدار بإذن ربنا وتوفيقه وإحسانه.

وترحالُ الكاذبين المكذّبين إلى الدار التي أُعدّت لمن كفر بالله ولقائه، وكتبه ورسله.

ولن يجمع الله بين الموحِّدين له، الطالبين لمرضاته، الساعين في طاعته، الدائبين في خدمته، المجاهدين في سبيله، وبين الملحدين - الساعين في مساخطه، الدائبين في معصيته، المستفرغين جهدهم في أهوائهم وشهواتهم - في دارٍ واحدة، إلا على سبيل الجواز والعبور، كما جمع بينهما في هذه الدنيا، ويجمع بينهم في موقف القيامة، فحاشاه من هذا الظن السيّئ الذي لا يليق بكماله وحكمته.

(فصل)
وفي هذه المرتبة تُعلم حياة الشهداء، وأنهم عند ربهم يُرزقون، وأنها أكمل من حياتهم في هذه الدنيا، وأتمّ وأطيب، وإن كانت أجسادهم متلاشيةً، ولحومهم متمزقةً، وأوصالهم متفرقةً، وعظامهم نخِرة، فليس العمل على الطَّلَل، إنما الشأن في الساكن. قال الله تعالى: ﴿ولا تحسبنّ الذين قُتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتًا، بل أحياءٌ عند ربهم يُرزقون﴾ [آل عمران: 169]، وقال تعالى: ﴿ولا تقولوا لمن يُقتل في سبيل الله أمواتٌ، بل أحياءٌ ولكن لا تشعرون﴾ [البقرة: 154]. وإذا كان الشهداء إنما نالوا هذه الحياة بمتابعة الرسل وعلى أيديهم، فما الظن بحياة الرسل في البرزخ (الحياة الوسطى بين الموت والبعث)؟ ولقد أحسن القائل:
فالعيش نومٌ والمنيّة يقظةٌ ∗∗∗ والمرء بينهما خيالٌ سارِ
فللرسل والشهداء والصديقين من هذه الحياة، التي هي يقظةٌ من نوم الدنيا، أكملُها وأتمُّها، وعلى قدر حياة العبد في هذا العالم يكون شوقُه إلى هذه الحياة، وسعيُه وحرصُه على الظفر بها، والله المستعان.

المرتبة العاشرة من مراتب الحياة: الحياة الدائمة الباقية بعد طيّ هذا العالم، وذهاب الدنيا وأهلها، في دار الحيوان (الدار الآخرة بوصفها دار الحياة الحقيقية)، وهي الحياة التي شمّر إليها المشمّرون، وسابق إليها المتسابقون، ونافس فيها المتنافسون، وهي التي أجرينا الكلام إليها، ونادت الكتب السماوية ورسل الله جميعُهم عليها، وهي التي يقول من فاته الاستعداد لها: ﴿إذا دُكّت الأرض دكًّا دكًّا - وجاء ربُّك والملَكُ صفًّا صفًّا - وجيء يومئذٍ بجهنم، يومئذٍ يتذكر الإنسان وأنّى له الذكرى - يقول يا ليتني قدّمت لحياتي - فيومئذٍ لا يعذّب عذابَه أحد - ولا يوثق وثاقَه أحد﴾ [الفجر: 21-26]، وهي التي قال الله عزّ وجلّ فيها: ﴿وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهوٌ ولعب، وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان، لو كانوا يعلمون﴾ [العنكبوت: 64].

والحياة المتقدّمة كالنوم بالنسبة إليها، وكلُّ ما تقدّم من وصف السير ومنازله، وأحوال السائرين، وعبوديتهم الظاهرة والباطنة، فوسيلةٌ إلى هذه الحياة، وإنما الحياة الدنيا بالنسبة إليها، كما قال النبي ﷺ: «ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كما يُدخل أحدُكم إصبعَه في اليمّ (البحر)، فلينظر بم ترجع؟».

وكما قيل: تنفّست الآخرةُ فكانت الدنيا نَفَسًا من أنفاسها، فأصاب أهلُ السعادة نَفَسَ نعيمها، فهم على هذا النَّفَس يعملون، وأصاب أهلُ الشقاوة نَفَسَ عذابها، فهم على ذلك النَّفَس يعملون.

وإذا كانت حياةُ أهل الإيمان والعمل الصالح في هذه الدار حياةً طيبة، فما الظن بحياتهم في البرزخ، وقد تخلّصوا من سجن الدنيا وضيقها؟ فما الظن بحياتهم في دار النعيم المقيم الذي لا يزول، وهم يرَوْن وجهَ ربّهم تبارك وتعالى بكرةً وعشيًّا، ويسمعون خطابه؟

فإن قلت: ما سبب تخلُّف النفس عن طلب هذه الحياة التي لا خطر لها، وما الذي زهّدها فيها؟ وما سبب رغبتها في الحياة الفانية المضمحلّة، التي هي كالخيال والمنام؟ أفسادٌ في تصوّرها وشعورها؟ أم تكذيبٌ بتلك الحياة؟ أم لآفةٍ في العقل، وعَمًى هناك؟ أم إيثارٌ للحاضر المشهود بالعيان على الغائب المعلوم بالإيمان؟

قيل: بل ذلك لمجموع أمورٍ مركّبةٍ من ذلك كلّه.

And the strongest of the causes behind this is weakness of faith (īmān). Faith is the spirit of deeds. It is what moves a person to them, what commands him to the best of them, and what forbids him from the worst of them. In proportion to the strength of faith is the force of its command and prohibition over its possessor, and the possessor's compliance and restraint. God Most High said: ﴿Say: Evil is what your faith commands you, if you are believers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 93].

In summary: when faith grows strong, longing for this life grows strong, and its possessor's pursuit of it intensifies.

The second cause is the weight of heedlessness (ghaflah) upon the heart. Heedlessness is the sleep of the heart. For this reason you find many who are awake in the senses yet asleep in reality. You take them to be awake while they are sleeping. This is the opposite of the state of one whose heart is awake while his body sleeps. When life is strong in the heart, it does not sleep when the body sleeps. The perfection of this life belonged to our Prophet (ﷺ), and to whomever God has given life to his heart through love of Him and following His message, with insight into that according to his share of both.

Heedlessness and wakefulness occur in the senses, the intellect and the heart. So the heart that is awake and the heart that is heedless are like the awake body and the sleeping body. Just as the wakefulness of the senses is of two kinds, so too is the wakefulness of the heart of two kinds.

The first kind of sensory wakefulness is that its possessor penetrates sensory matters and goes deep into them through his earning, his shrewdness, his cunning and his skilful handling.

The second kind is that one turns toward his self, his heart and his essence, and takes care to attain its perfection. He observes both the lofty and the base affairs, prefers the higher over the lower, sacrifices the lesser of two goods to secure the greater, and commits the lighter of two evils out of fear of the greater one occurring. He adorns himself with noble character and lofty qualities, so that his outward appearance is beautiful and his inward state is more beautiful than his outward, and his secret is better than his public face. He competes with the people of lofty aims for these qualities, as the people of gold and silver compete for those metals. Through this wakefulness he prepares himself for the other two kinds.

One of them is a wakefulness that moves him to acquire the lasting, enduring life, which has no worth compared with this transient, perishing life that has no value.

If you say: Give me an example of how the everlasting life is acquired from the perishing life, and how this works, for I do not understand it.

I say: This too is from the sleep of the heart, or even its death. Is the everlasting life acquired except from this passing life? You may light your lamp from another lamp that is nearly extinguished. The second then catches fire and gives its brightest light, its light connects, and the first goes out. The one who acquires his everlasting life from his severed life only moves from a severed abode to an enduring abode, and death lies between the two abodes. It is a bridge that none crosses to that abode except over it, and a gate that none enters through except by it. So they are two lives in two abodes with death between them. Just as the light of that abode is acquired from the light of this abode, so its life is likewise acquired from its life. In proportion to the light of faith in this abode is the servant's light in that abode, and in proportion to his life in this abode will be his life there.

Yes, this light and life from which that light and life is acquired does not cease. Rather it shines for the servant in the barzakh (intermediate state), at the Standing on the Day of Resurrection, and upon the Sirat (bridge). It does not leave him when he goes to the abode of the living. The light of the sun is extinguished, but this light is not extinguished. Sensory life is annulled, but this life is not annulled. This is one of the two kinds of wakefulness of the heart.

The second kind is a wakefulness that gives rise to a life which expression cannot grasp, imagination cannot reach, and in which the word does not correspond to its meaning at all. What is pointed to by it is the life of the lover with his beloved, on whom the heart, spirit and life of the lover depend, and without whom he has no sufficiency even for the blink of an eye. There is no coolness for his eye, no tranquillity for his heart, and no rest for his spirit except through Him. He needs Him more than he needs his hearing, his sight or his strength, indeed more than his life. For his life without Him is torment, pains, anxieties and sorrows. His life is contingent upon nearness to Him, love for Him and companionship with Him. The torment of being veiled from Him is greater than the other torment. Just as the bliss of the heart and spirit through the removal of that veil is greater than the bliss of eating, drinking and enjoying the maidens with lustrous eyes, so the torment of the veil is greater than the torment of the Blazing Fire. For this reason God, glorified is He, combined for His friends both kinds of bliss in His saying: ﴿For those who have done good is the best [reward], and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. The "best" is Paradise, and the "more" is the sight of His noble Face in the Gardens of Eden. And for His enemies He combined both torments in His saying: ﴿No! Indeed they, that Day, from their Lord will be veiled. Then indeed they will be burning in Hellfire﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15-16].

The aim is this: heedlessness is the sleep of the heart from seeking this life, and it is a veil over it. If this veil is uncovered by remembrance (dhikr), well and good; otherwise it thickens until it becomes a veil of idleness, play and preoccupation with what is of no benefit. If one hastens to uncover it, well and good; otherwise it thickens until it becomes a veil of disobedience and minor sins that distance him from God. If he hastens to uncover it, well and good; otherwise it thickens until it becomes a veil of major sins that bring about the Lord's hatred, wrath and curse. If he hastens to uncover it, well and good; otherwise it thickens until it becomes a veil of practical innovations (bid'ah 'amaliyyah), through which the doer torments himself and gains nothing. If he hastens to uncover it, well and good; otherwise it thickens until it becomes a veil of verbal innovations in belief, which include lying against God and His Messenger and denying the truth that the Messenger brought. If he hastens to uncover it, well and good; otherwise it thickens until it becomes a veil of doubt and denial, which undermines the five foundations of faith: belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers and the meeting with Him. Because of the coarseness, density, darkness and blackness of this veil, he does not see the realities of faith, and Satan gains power over him, promising and deluding him, while the commanding self (al-nafs al-ammarah bi'l-su') desires and craves. The sovereignty of nature (sultan al-tab') has overcome the sovereignty of faith, so it has captured and imprisoned it, if it has not destroyed it. It takes charge of the kingdom, employs the armies of desires, assigns to them the customs upon which practice has run, closes the gate of wakefulness, and posts over it the gatekeeper of heedlessness. It says: Beware lest we be attacked from your side. It appoints a chamberlain from among the passions and says: Beware lest you allow anyone to enter upon me except with you. So the affair of this kingdom has come to you and to the gatekeeper. O gatekeeper of heedlessness, and O chamberlain of passion, let each of you hold his frontier. If you both leave it, the affairs of our kingdom will be corrupted, the rule will return to others, and the sultan of faith will inflict upon us the worst of disgrace and humiliation, and we will never again rejoice in this city.

So there is no god but God! When these armies gather upon the heart, with the faintness of faith, the scarcity of helpers, turning away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, joining the line of the sons of the age, and long hope which corrupts the human being, he prefers the immediate present over the absent promised thing that is to come after these worlds are folded up. God is the One sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

This is a brief and beneficial section on the mention of life and its kinds, and on arousing longing for its most noble and pure kind. Whoever finds life in his heart benefits from it. Otherwise it is like a shy bride led to a blind, crippled man.

Let us return to explaining the words of the author of Manazil al-Sa'irin (the Shaykh):

He said: "It has three breaths: the breath of fear, the breath of hope and the breath of love."

Since every living creature has breath, and breath necessitates life and is its sign, the breaths of the life referred to here are three: the breath of fear, whose source is contemplating the threat and what God has prepared for whoever prefers this world over the Hereafter, the created over the Creator, desire over guidance, and error over right direction.

The breath of hope, whose source is contemplating the promise, good opinion of the Lord Most High, and what God has prepared for whoever prefers God, His Messenger and the Last Abode, and makes guidance the judge over desire, revelation the judge over opinions, and the Sunnah the judge over innovation, and what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions were upon, over the customs of the creation.

The breath of love, whose source is contemplating the Names and Attributes, and witnessing blessings and favours.

So when he remembers his sins, he breathes with fear. When he remembers his Lord's mercy, the vastness of His forgiveness and His pardon, he breathes with hope. When he remembers His beauty, majesty, perfection, kindness and bounty, he breathes with love.

So let the servant weigh his faith by these three breaths, that he may know how much faith he has. For hearts are created inclined to love beauty and perfection, and God, glorified is He, is beautiful. Rather, to Him belongs complete and perfect beauty from every aspect: the beauty of His essence, the beauty of His Attributes, the beauty of His acts and the beauty of His Names. If all the beauty of all creatures were gathered upon one person, and all of them were upon the beauty of that person, and then this beauty were compared to the beauty of the Lord, blessed and exalted, it would be less than the ratio of a weak lamp to the sun itself.

So the breath that comes from this observation and contemplation is the noblest of the servant's breaths absolutely. Where is the breath of the longing, sincere lover compared with the breath of the fearful, hopeful one? But he cannot attain this breath except by attaining those two breaths, for one of them is the fruit of abandoning transgressions and the other is the fruit of performing acts of obedience. Through these two breaths he reaches the third breath.

[Section: The second life is the life of unification after the death of dispersion]

He said: "The second life is the life of unification (jam') after the death of dispersal (tafriqah), and it has three breaths: the breath of compulsion (idtirar), the breath of need (iftiqar) and the breath of pride (iftikhar)."

By "unification" in this stage, if God wills, he means: gathering the heart upon God and gathering the thoughts and resolutions in turning toward Him, glorified is He, not the unification which is the presence of existence (hadrat al-wujud), because he has mentioned the life of that unification in the third stage and called it the life of existence.

The gathering of the heart upon God and the thoughts upon journeying toward Him is a true life, because the heart has no happiness, no salvation, no bliss, no success, no delight and no coolness of eye except by having God alone as the ultimate goal of its seeking, the final end of its intention, and its highest face is its entire aim. So dispersal, which includes turning away from turning toward Him, and the gathering of the heart upon Him, is its sickness, unless it dies from it.

He said: "This life has three breaths: the breath of compulsion, which arises from the severing of one's hope from all besides God, so that he is then compelled in heart, spirit, soul and body toward his Lord with complete necessity, such that in every root of his hair he finds complete need of his Lord and his Worshipped One. This breath is a breath compelled toward what he cannot do without even for the blink of an eye. His need of Him is from the standpoint that He is his Lord, Creator, Originator, Helper, Guardian, Aider, Provider, Guide, Healer, and the One who manages all his interests; and from the standpoint that He is his Worshipped One, his God, and his Beloved, without whom his life cannot be complete or beneficial, and that He alone be the most beloved thing to him and the most longed-for thing. This compulsion is the compulsion of ﴿You alone we worship﴾, and the first compulsion is the compulsion of ﴿You alone we ask for help﴾."

By God's life, the breath of need is this breath, or of its kind. But the Shaykh made them two breaths: he made the breath of compulsion the beginning, the breath of need the middle, and the breath of pride the end. It seems that the breath of compulsion cuts the creation off from his heart, and the breath of need hangs his heart upon his Lord.

The verification is that it is one extended breath, whose beginning is severance and whose end is connection.

Ibn al-Qayyim's Tafsir (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 6, verse 122 (part 7 of 7):

As for the breath of pride (nafs al-iftikhar), it is the result of these two breaths. When they are sound for the servant, he attains nearness to his Lord, intimacy with Him, and joy in Him, and in the robes of honour (khila') which his Lord has bestowed upon his heart and spirit, which all the kingdoms of this world in their entirety could not match even a part of. Then he breathes another breath, finding in it a relief, ease, comfort, and expansion, which in some respects resembles the breath of one who has a rope placed around his neck to strangle him until he dies, then it is removed from him after his breath had been cut off, so he breathes the breath of one whose life has been restored and who has escaped the causes of death.

If you say: What has the servant to do with pride? And where is servanthood (ubudiyya) from the breath of pride?

I say: He does not mean by this that the servant takes pride in it and swaggers over his fellow creatures. Rather, it is a joy and delight that cannot be repelled from himself, due to what his Lord has opened up for him, granted him, and singled him out with. The most fitting thing for the servant to rejoice in is the bounty of his Lord upon him, for He, exalted is He, loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant, and loves that he rejoice in it, because that is part of gratitude. Whoever does not rejoice in the blessing of the Benefactor is not considered grateful. So this is pride in what is purely the grace and blessing of God upon His servant, not pride in what the servant has bestowed. This is what contradicts servanthood, not that.

Here is a subtle secret: this breath takes pride over its other breaths which are not like it, just as life takes pride over death, knowledge over ignorance, hearing over deafness, and sight over blindness. So the pride is of one breath over another breath, not of the one who breathes over people. And God knows best.

[Chapter: The Third Life, the Life of Existence (hayat al-wujud)]

He said: The third life is the life of existence (hayat al-wujud). It is a life by the Truth, and it has three breaths: the breath of awe (nafs al-haybah), which kills moderation (al-i'tidal); the breath of existence (nafs al-wujud), which prevents separation (al-infisal); and the breath of solitude (nafs al-infirad), which produces union (al-ittisal). Beyond this there is no vantage point for observers, and no capacity for allusion.

This level of life is the life of the one who has found (al-wajid), and it is more complete than the two types preceding it. The servant's existence in his Lord is what He indicated in the divine hadith with His saying: "When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks; by Me he hears, by Me he sees, by Me he strikes, and by Me he walks." And what is alluded to in His saying: "O son of Adam, seek Me and you will find Me; for if you find Me, you will find everything, and if you miss Me, you will miss everything."

More on this will come in the chapter on existence, God willing.

The life of existence is the most complete life because of its nobility and its perfection through its Originator (mujid), who is the Truth, glorified and exalted. Whoever is granted His existence has attained the highest kind of life.

If you say: It is difficult for me to understand the meaning of life through His existence.

I say: This is because of the veil that has been placed between you and this life. So understand life through the existence of annihilation (fana'), and through the existence of the Owner, the Capable, when He is with you and your helper, not merely His existence, nor any knowledge between you and Him whatsoever. The reality of life is life through the Lord, exalted is He, not the life of breath, annihilation, and the means of living.

The "life of existence" may also be interpreted as witnessing the Self-Subsisting (shuhud al-qayyumiyya), whereby one sees nothing among things except that it is by God, and it is He who has established it. In the state of this witnessing, the heart does not turn toward anything other than God, does not fear or hope in anything else, but has restricted its fear, hope, reliance, and turning to the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Sustainer of existence, its Establisher and Maintainer, alone. Whenever this witnessing and this state are attained, the life of existence has been attained.

Sometimes he breathes through awe, which is the overpowering radiance of the attributes, and this occurs at the first shining of the light of existence. The heart falls into an awe that overwhelms its perception so that it does not turn to anything of the worlds of the breath. That is the infirmity (al-i'tilal) which the second breath kills, namely his saying: "and a breath that kills infirmity." Thus there die from it the ailments of his deeds, the traces of his appetites, and the witnessing of his selfhood.

His saying "and the breath of existence" means by it: the servant's existence through his Lord. He breathes by this existence just as he hears by it, sees by it, strikes by it, and walks by it.

Do not listen to anything other than this, lest a foot slip after it was firm.

(Section)

As for the constriction of the breast and making it tight and narrow so that it cannot accept faith, the Exalted said: ﴿Whomever Allah wishes to guide, He expands his breast for Islam; and whomever He wishes to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as though he were climbing up into the sky﴾

Ḥaraj (narrow, constricted) is, in the words of all the linguists, the one whose breast is extremely tight. It is said: a man is ḥaraj and ḥarij, meaning his breast is constricted.

The poet said:

"Neither constricted of breast nor harsh."

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: Ibn ʿAbbas recited this verse and said: "Is there anyone here from the Banu Bakr?" A man said: "Yes." He said: "What is the ḥarjah among you?" They said: "A valley with many trees in which there is no path." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Likewise is the heart of the disbeliever."

ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭab recited the verse and said: "Bring me a man from Kinanah and make him a shepherd." They brought him to him, and ʿUmar said: "O young man, what is the ḥarjah among you?" He said: "A tree surrounded by many trees, so that no shepherd nor wild animal can reach it." ʿUmar said: "Likewise is the heart of the disbeliever; no good reaches it."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He makes his breast tight and constricted; when he hears the remembrance of Allah, his heart recoils, and if something of the worship of idols is mentioned, he is relieved and at ease with it."

Since the heart is the place of knowledge, cognizance, love and turning back (to Allah), and these things only enter the heart when it is spacious for them, when Allah wills the guidance of a servant He expands his breast and opens it, so these things enter it and dwell in it; and when He wills his misguidance, He constricts his breast and makes it narrow, so he finds no place for them to enter, so he turns away from them and does not dwell with them. Every empty vessel, when something is put into it, is constricted by it, and whenever you pour something into it, it becomes tight, except the soft heart: whenever faith and knowledge are poured into it, it expands and widens.

This is among the signs of the power of the Lord, the Exalted. In al-Tirmidhi and others, it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "When light enters the heart, it expands and opens." They said: "What is the sign of that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Turning back to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before it descends."

Thus the expansion of the breast is among the greatest causes of guidance, and its constriction is among the causes of misguidance, just as its expansion is among the greatest blessings and its constriction among the greatest afflictions. The believer has an expanded, widened breast in this world despite what he encounters of its hardships; and when faith is strong and its delight mixes with hearts, he is more expansive of breast in its hardships than in its desires and loves. When he departs from it, the expansion of his soul and the expansion obtained by leaving it are far greater, like one who leaves a narrow prison for a wide open space suited to him, for this world is the prison of the believer. When Allah resurrects him on the Day of Resurrection, he will see from the expansion and vastness of his breast what has no comparison to what came before.

So the expansion of the breast, just as it is the cause of guidance, is the root of every blessing and the foundation of every good. Moses ibn ʿImran, the interlocutor of the Merciful, asked his Lord to expand his breast for him, knowing that he could not fulfill his message and bear its burdens except if his breast was expanded. He (the Exalted) enumerated among His blessings upon the seal of His prophets and messengers the expansion of his breast, and reported about his followers that He expanded their breasts for Islam.

If you say: What are the means that expand the breasts and those that constrict them? I say: The means that expands the breast is the light that Allah casts into it. When that light enters it, it expands according to the strength and weakness of the light; and when that light is lost, it darkens and becomes constricted.

If you say: Is it possible to acquire this light, or is it bestowed?

I say: It is bestowed, and its acquisition is also a mere gift from Allah, the Exalted. The whole matter belongs to Allah, all praise is His, all good is in His hands, and the servant has nothing of himself at all. Rather, Allah is the Giver of the means and their effects, the One who makes them means, and who grants them to whom He wills and withholds them from whom He wills. If He wills good for His servant, He enables him to exhaust his effort and spend his utmost in desire and fear toward Him, for these two are the sources of success; by the measure of desire and fear in the heart, success is attained.

If you say: Are desire and fear in His hand, not in the servant's hand?

I say: Yes, by Allah, and they are merely His grace and favor; He places them in the place that befits them and withholds them from one who is not fit for them.

If you say: What is the sin of one who is not fit?

I say: Most of his sin is that he is not fit, because his fitness depends on what he chose for himself, preferred and loved of error and misguidance, with clear knowledge of his own affair. He preferred his desire over the right of his Lord and His pleasure, and chose blindness over guidance. The disbelief of one who was blessed with the kinds of blessings, the denial of his Benefactor's favor, association with Him, and striving toward what angers Him was more beloved to him than gratitude to Him, His tawhid, and striving for His pleasure. This is from his unfitness to receive the success of his Creator and Owner. And what sin is greater than this? When the Just Judge withholds His success from one of such a condition, He has been just with him, and the doors of guidance and the paths of right direction are closed to him, and his heart is darkened, so it is constricted from entering Islam and faith. Even if every sign came to him, it would only increase him in misguidance and disbelief.

When one who has had Allah expand his breast for Islam and faith reflects on this verse and what it contains of the secrets of tawhid, the excuse, justice, and the greatness of the matter of lordship, his heart gains another servitude and a special knowledge.
