He knows that he is a servant in every respect and in every consideration, and that the Lord, the Exalted, is the Lord of everything and its Sovereign, of substances, attributes and actions, that the whole matter is in His hand, all praise is His, the reins of affairs are in His hand, and all their return is to Him. This verse has a status above our minds, greater than our understandings, and more significant than what the theologians said about it, those who wronged its meaning: ﴿and they wronged themselves﴾. By Allah, their veil has grown thick over it, their understandings have been stopped by it, and their foundations which they established and their principles which they founded have prevented them from reaching its intended meaning. For it contains the affirmation of tawhid and the justice with which Allah sent His messengers and revealed His books, and the justice which the deniers of attributes and the deniers of divine decree claim.

It also contains the affirmation of wisdom, power, legislation and decree, cause and judgment, sin and punishment. It opened to the sound heart a wide door of knowledge of the Lord, the Exalted, through His names, attributes of perfection, and descriptions of majesty, and His wisdom in His legislation and decree, and His justice in His punishment, and His grace in His reward. It contains the perfection of His tawhid, lordship, self-subsistence and divinity, and that the sources of all matters come from the pure essence of His will and return to the perfection of His wisdom; that the guided one is the one whom Allah specifically granted His guidance and expanded his breast for His religion and His law; and that the misguided one is the one who made his breast tight and constricted from knowing and loving Him, as though he were climbing into the sky, and that is not within his power. It is also justice in His punishment toward one who did not measure Him with His due measure, denied the perfection of His lordship, disbelieved His blessing, and preferred the worship of Satan over His servitude. So the door of His success and guidance was closed to him, and the doors of his error and misguidance were opened to him; his breast became constricted, his heart hardened, his limbs were idle from the worship of their Lord, and his inner parts were filled with darkness. The fault is his, since he turned away from faith and substituted for it disbelief, transgression and disobedience, and was content with allying with Satan, and the enmity of the Merciful became light to him. He does not speak to himself about returning to his Master, nor does he resolve one day to give up his desire. He has opposed Allah in His command by loving what He hates and hating what He loves, allying with the one who is hostile to Him and being hostile to the one who allies with Him; he becomes angry when the Lord is pleased, and is pleased when He is angry. Yet he turns in His favor, dwells in His house, feeds on His provision, and strengthens himself in His disobedience with His blessings. Who is more just than Him, the Exalted, above what the ignorant and the wrongdoers describe Him with, when He places the revelation upon such as these who do not believe?

Regarding the naming of Paradise as "the Abode of Peace" (Dar al-Salam), there is difference of opinion. It has been said: al-Salam is Allah, and Paradise is His abode.

It has also been said: al-Salam is safety (al-salamah), and Paradise is the abode of safety from every calamity, defect and deficiency.

It has also been said: it was named the Abode of Peace because their greeting therein is "Salam" (peace).

There is no contradiction between all these meanings.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 128:**

That is, you have greatly increased in misleading them and leading them astray.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and others said: "You misled many of them." Then Allah, glory be to Him, is answered by their allies among mankind, who say:

﴿Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others﴾ [al-An'am: 128].

They mean that each kind has enjoyed the other kind. The jinn's enjoyment of mankind is that mankind obeys them in what they command: disbelief, wickedness and disobedience. This is the greatest aim of the jinn regarding mankind. When people obey them in this, they have given the jinn their desire.

Mankind's enjoyment of the jinn is that they help them in disobeying Allah, the Exalted, and in associating partners with Him, by every means they can: beautifying and adorning (evil), invocation, fulfilling many of their needs, and employing them through sorcery, incantations and other things. Mankind obeys them in what pleases them: association with Allah, obscenities and immorality. The jinn obey mankind in what pleases them: influencing them and informing them of some unseen matters.

So each of the two groups has enjoyed the other.

This verse applies to those people of satanic states who have satanic unveilings and satanic influence. The ignorant one thinks them to be friends of the Most Merciful, when in fact they are friends of Satan. They obeyed him in associating partners with Allah, in disobeying Allah, and in departing from what His messengers were sent with and what His books were revealed with. He obeyed them by serving them with his information of many unseen matters and influences. Whoever has little share of knowledge and faith is deceived by them, so he takes as allies the enemies of Allah, treats His allies as enemies, thinks well of those who have departed from His path and Sunnah, and thinks ill of those who follow the Sunnah of the Messenger and what he brought, and does not leave it for the statements of those who differ, the opinions of the bewildered, the extravagances of the renegades, and the nonsense of the Sufis.

The discerning person whom Allah has illuminated with the light of faith and knowledge, when he recognises the reality of what most of this creation is upon, and is a skilled critic on whom adulterated metal cannot pass as genuine, it becomes clear to him that they fall under the ruling of this verse, and that it applies to them.

So the wicked person enjoys Satan, by Satan's help to him in the causes of his wickedness, and Satan enjoys him in his acceptance and obedience to him, so that this pleases and delights Satan.

The polytheist is enjoyed by Satan through his associating partners with Allah and worshipping Satan, and he enjoys Satan in the fulfilment of his needs and Satan's help to him.

Whoever does not comprehend this has not known the reality of faith and polytheism, nor the wisdom of the Lord, glory be to Him, in testing each of the two species (humans and jinn) through the other.

Then they said: ﴿and we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾ [al-An'am: 128].

This encompasses the term of death and the term of resurrection. Both are terms that Allah, the Exalted, set for His servants, and they are the two terms about which Allah said: ﴿Then He decreed a term, and a specified term is with Him﴾ [al-An'am: 2].

It seems that this, and Allah knows best, is an indication from them of a kind of entreaty and repentance. As if they were saying: this matter had a set time and it ended when its term ended. It did not continue or last, so the matter reached the term appointed for it and came to its end. Everything has an end. Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide forever﴾ [al-An'am: 128].

Even though the period of enjoyment ended and its term expired, the period of punishment remains. So let no one imagine that when the time of disbelief and polytheism has passed, and some of you have enjoyed others, its corruption has vanished with its vanishing and ended with its ending.

The point is that Satan toyed with the polytheists until they worshipped him, and took him and his offspring as allies besides Allah.

(Section)

No son of Adam has worshipped anyone other than Allah, whoever he may be, except that his worship fell to Satan. The worshipper enjoys the object of worship in attaining his aim, and the object of worship enjoys the worshipper in his exalting it and associating it with Allah, which is the utmost of Satan's satisfaction. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all, [He will say]: "O assembly of jinn, you have greatly increased in [misleading] mankind"﴾, that is, in their seduction and misguidance, ﴿and their allies among mankind will say: "Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us." He will say: "The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide forever, except as Allah wills. Indeed your Lord is Wise and All-Knowing"﴾.

This is a subtle indication of the secret for which polytheism is the greatest of the major sins in the sight of Allah, that He does not forgive it without repentance from it, that it necessitates eternal abiding in punishment, and that its prohibition and ugliness are not merely due to the bare prohibition against it. Rather, it is impossible for Allah, glory be to Him, to legislate for His servants the worship of a god other than Him, just as it is impossible for Him to have what contradicts the attributes of His perfection and the descriptions of His majesty. How could one suppose that He who is alone in lordship, divinity, greatness and glorification would permit anyone to share with Him in that, or be pleased with it? Exalted is Allah above that, a great exaltation.

Ibn al-Qayyim's Commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 131:

It has been said: He did not destroy them for their wrongdoing and their polytheism while they were heedless, not having been warned, and no messenger had come to them.

And it has been said: He did not destroy them before the reminder through the sending of a messenger, for then He would have wronged them. Indeed, He, glorified is He, does not seize anyone or punish him except for his sin, and a person is only sinful if he opposes His command and prohibition, and that is only known through the messengers.

When the servant witnesses the decree (al-qadar) preceding the sin, he knows that God, glorified is He, has decreed it as a cause that necessitates its effect of punishment, just as He decreed obedience as a cause that necessitates reward. Likewise is the decree of all the other causes of good and evil: such as making poison a cause of death, fire a cause of burning, and water a cause of drowning.

So when the servant proceeds toward a cause of destruction, while knowing that it is a cause of destruction, and is destroyed, the proof is established against him, and the accountability is binding upon him, like the one who burns, for example: sin is like the fire, and his approaching it is like his delivering himself into the fire. And observing the (divine) judgment (al-hukm) in what does not benefit him in anything is not the case. Rather, what he witnesses when the proof is established against him is the observation of the command (al-amr), not the observation of the decree (al-qadar).

So the claim of the author of al-Manazil (Sahib al-Manazil) that this subtle point is part of the observation of the offence and the decree is not clear; rather, it is part of the observation of the offence and the command. But his intent is that the secret of the decree is that He has known that this servant is fit only for the fuel, like the thorn that is fit only for the fire, and the tree contains both fruit and thorns. So His justice, glorified is He, requires that He drive this servant toward what he is fit for only, and that He establish against him the proof of His justice. So if He decrees sin upon him and he commits it, he deserves what he was created for. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an, to warn whoever is alive and that the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69-70].

[Section: The wisdom in differentiating between some zakat rates]

As for his saying: "He obligated zakat on gold, silver and trade goods at one-fortieth (rub' al-'ushr), on crops and fruits at one-half of a tenth or a tenth, and on mineral deposits (ma'din) at one-fifth," this too is from the perfection of the Shari'ah and its regard for the public interests (maslahah). The Lawgiver (al-Shari') obligated zakat as consolation for the poor (muwasah lil-fuqara'), as a purification of wealth (tuhrah lil-mal), as worship of the Lord ('ubudiyyah lil-Rabb), and as a means of drawing near to Him by giving away what the servant loves and by preferring His pleasure.

Then He prescribed it in the most complete manner and in the manner most beneficial to the needy and most gentle toward the owners of wealth. He did not prescribe it on every kind of property, but prescribed it on the kinds of wealth that can bear consolation and in which profit, yield and increase abound. He did not prescribe it on what a servant needs from his property and cannot do without, such as his slaves, his female slaves, his mount, his house, his clothing and his weapons. Rather, He prescribed it on four categories of wealth: livestock (al-mawashi), crops and fruits (al-zuru' wal-thimar), gold and silver, and trade goods ('urud al-tijarah). These are the most common kinds of people's wealth circulating among them, and the bulk of their dealings are in them, and they are the kinds that can bear consolation, unlike those for which zakat was waived.

Then He divided each of these categories according to its condition and its readiness for growth into that in which there is zakat and that in which there is no zakat. He divided livestock into two parts: grazing animals (sa'imah), which graze without expense, hardship or loss, so that the blessing in them is complete, the favour in them is abundant, the cost of them is small and the increase in them is great; He singled out this type for zakat. And into fodder-fed animals (ma'lufah) which are bought with money, or which work in the interests of their owners, in their irrigation work, their plowing and carrying their goods; He did not place zakat on these, because of the expense of fodder and the owners' need for working animals. They are like their clothing, their slaves, their female slaves and their goods.

Then He divided crops and fruits into two parts: one part that runs in the manner of grazing livestock in that its irrigation comes from rainwater without expense or hardship, and for this He obligated one-tenth ('ushr); and another part that is irrigated with expense and hardship, but whose expense is far less than the expense of fodder-fed animals, since those require fodder every day. So it occupied a rank between the rank of grazing animals and fodder-fed animals. He did not obligate zakat on what it drinks by itself, nor did He waive its zakat altogether, so He obligated one-half of a tenth on it.

Then He divided gold and silver into two parts: one that is prepared for use as currency and for trading and earning by it, in which there is zakat, such as the two monies (naqdayn), bullion and the like; and that which is prepared for personal use without profit or trade, such as women's jewelry and weapons whose like may be used, and in which there is no zakat.

Then He divided trade goods into two parts: a part prepared for trade, in which there is zakat; and a part prepared for keeping and use, which is diverted away from the source of increase, so there is no zakat on it.

Then, since achieving increase and profit through trade is among the hardest things and involves the most toil and work, He lightened it by making the obligation one-fortieth. Since profit and increase from crops and fruits that are irrigated with expense are less costly and the work easier, and it does not occur the whole year, He made it double that, which is one-half of a tenth. And since toil and labour for what drinks by itself is less and the cost lighter, He made it double that, which is one-tenth, and was satisfied in it with a general, specific zakat. So if after that a number of years pass during which it remains with him for purposes other than trade, there is no zakat on it, because its growth and increase has ceased; this is unlike livestock, and unlike the case where it is prepared for trade, for then it is open to growth. Then, since buried treasure (rikaz) is wealth already gathered and obtained, and the cost of obtaining it is less than other kinds, and it needs no more than extraction, the obligation on it was double that, which is one-fifth.

Consider, then, the harmony of this perfect Shari'ah, whose goodness and perfection dazzle the intellects, whose wisdom the natural dispositions (fitar) bear witness to, and that the world has never been visited by a Shari'ah better than it.

And if the minds of the intelligent and the natural dispositions of the wise were gathered together and proposed something that would be the best of proposals, their proposal would not reach what this Shari'ah has brought.

And since not every kind of wealth can bear consolation, the Lawgiver specified for what can bear consolation fixed thresholds (nusub muqaddarah) below which zakat is not due. Then, since these thresholds are divided into those whose consolation does not overburden a portion of them, He obligated zakat from them; and those whose consolation does overburden a portion of them, so He made the obligation from them other than that, such as what is less than twenty-five camels. Then, since consolation cannot be borne every day or every month, for that would burden the owners of wealth, He made it once every year, just as He made fasting like that. And since performing prayer does not burden doing it every day, He assigned it every day and night. And since Hajj is burdensome if its obligation recurs every year, He made it a duty of a lifetime.

When a sensible person reflects on the measure the Lawgiver obligated in zakat, he finds it is something whose loss does not harm the giver, and whose taking benefits the poor. He sees that it has regarded the condition and the side of the owner of wealth with the utmost regard, and benefited the one who takes it, and aimed at each kind of wealth and obligated zakat on its best and most noble part: so He obligated zakat in kind on gold and silver rather than iron, lead, copper and the like; He obligated zakat on grazing livestock among camels, cattle and sheep, rather than horses, mules and donkeys, and rather than what is rarely kept, such as game animals of various kinds, and all birds; and He obligated zakat on what comes out of the earth in its noblest form, which is grains and fruits, rather than herbs, fresh fruits, vegetables, melons and flowers.

It is no secret how distinct what He obligated zakat on is from what He did not obligate it on, in its kind, its quality, its benefit, the intensity of need for it and the abundance of its existence, and that it runs in the manner of wealth in relation to the other kinds of wealth, such that were it to be lost, its loss would harm people and many of their interests would be disrupted; unlike what zakat was not obligated on, which runs in the manner of surpluses and supplements, whose loss would not greatly harm anyone. Likewise, He regarded two important matters concerning those entitled to it:

First: the need of the recipient.

Second: its benefit (to the community).

So He made the entitled recipients of two kinds: one kind that takes out of its need, and one kind that takes for its benefit; and He forbade it to anyone other than these two.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on surah 6, verse 145:

And Allah did not set a prescribed punishment (hadd) for eating carrion, relying instead on the deterrent that Allah placed in human nature: the aversion to it, the revulsion from it, and the keeping away from it. This is unlike wine.

Swine is more strictly forbidden than carrion. For this reason Allah singled out its ruling, declaring it to be impure (rijs) in His saying: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it, except that it be carrion, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine—for indeed it is impure (rijs) or an abomination (fisq)﴾ [al-An'am: 145]. Although the pronoun in His saying "fa-innahu" (for indeed it) refers to the three things mentioned, by way of the word "muharram" (forbidden), the flesh of swine is preferred as its referent for three reasons. The first: its proximity to it. The second: its being masculine in form, unlike His saying "fa-innaha rijs" (for indeed it is impure), which would be feminine. The third: that He used "fa" (for) and "inna" (indeed), drawing attention to the cause of the prohibition so that souls would be restrained from it. This cause is countered by what is in the nature of some people, namely their finding it delicious and savoring it. So He negated that and informed that it is impure (rijs). This is not needed for carrion and blood, because their being impure is an established matter known to them. There are parallels to this in the Qur'an, so reflect upon them.

Then He mentioned afterward the prohibition of selling idols, which is greater in prohibition and sin, and more contrary to Islam, than the selling of wine, carrion, and swine.

Ibn al-Qayyim, *al-Tafsir al-Qayyim*, commentary on Surah 6, verse 148 (Part 1 of 2)

Allah, glory be to Him, rebuked those who used His will (mashi'ah) as proof of His approval in three places of His Book: in Surah al-An'am, in Surah al-Nahl, and in Surah al-Zukhruf. He said, Exalted is He:

﴿The idolaters will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything." Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow only conjecture, and you are only guessing."﴾

He related the same of them in Surah al-Nahl, then said:

﴿Likewise did those before them act. Then, is there upon the Messengers anything but clear conveyance?﴾

And He said in Surah al-Zukhruf:

﴿And they say: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they are only guessing.﴾

They argued for His love of their shirk and His pleasure with it by the fact that He permitted it, and that if He did not love it and was not pleased with it, He would not have willed it from them. They thereby set up their argument against His command and prohibition and against the call of the Messengers. They said: "How can He command a thing when He has willed the opposite of it from us? And how can He hate something from us when He has willed its occurrence? If He hated it, He would not have enabled us to do it, and He would have prevented us from it." So Allah, glory be to Him, denied them in this, and informed that this was a denial of His Messengers, and that His Messengers agree that He, glory be to Him, hates their shirk, detests it, and abhors it, and that were it not for His hatred and aversion to it, He would not have made the idolaters taste His punishment, for He does not punish His servant for what He loves. Then He demanded of them knowledge to support their doctrine, that Allah had permitted it and that He loves it and is pleased with it. Merely His permitting it as a decree does not indicate this to anyone of sound intellect; otherwise, injustice, indecency, spreading corruption in the land, and oppression would be beloved and pleasing to Him. Then He informed that their basis for this was only conjecture, and conjecture is the most false of speech, and that for this reason they were people of guessing and lying.

Then He informed, glory be to Him, that the proof is His against them from two directions. The first is what He placed in them of intellects by which they distinguish between good and evil, truth and falsehood, and the hearing and sight, which are the instruments for perceiving the truth and by which it is distinguished from falsehood. The second is the sending of His Messengers, the sending down of His Books, and His enabling them to believe and submit. He did not hold them accountable for only one of these two matters, but for both together, out of the perfection of His justice and to cut off every excuse from them in every respect. For this reason He called His proof against them "conclusive" (balighah), meaning that it has reached the utmost limit of clarity and its furthest extent, such that no speech remains for any speaker and no excuse for any one making excuses. Whoever offers Him a valid excuse, He accepts it.

Then He concluded the verse with His saying:

﴿Then if He had willed, He would have guided you all.﴾

And that nothing occurs except by His will. This is part of the completeness of His conclusive proof, for when a thing is withheld because He did not will it, it follows that it exists when He wills it. What He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. This is among the greatest proofs of monotheism (tawhid) and among the clearest proofs of the invalidity of what you are upon of shirk and the taking of rivals besides Him. So what you argue by will in support of your shirk is actually one of the most manifest proofs of its invalidity and corruption. Had they mentioned the decree and the will as a declaration of His oneness (tawhid), as a sign of their poverty before Him, of their seeking refuge in Him, of their disavowal of any power or strength except through Him, and of their desire that He relieve them of what, if He had willed it not to occur from them, would not have occurred, that would have benefited them, and He would have opened for them the door of guidance. But they mentioned it as opposing His command and as nullifying the call of the Messengers, so it increased them only in misguidance.

The point is that He, glory be to Him, distinguished between His proof and His will. Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari (ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Ashʿarī, the founder of the Ash'ari school) reported in his *Maqalat* the consensus of the People of the Sunnah and Hadith on this. What Ibn Furak reported from him in his abridgment of his *Maqalat* is that he distinguished between these matters. He said: "He did not distinguish between love (wudd), affection (hubb), will (iradah), volition (mashi'ah), and pleasure (rida), and he did not say that any of them is specific to certain things rather than others. Rather, he said that each of them carries the meaning of its companion in the sense of a qualification that removes ambiguity: the believer is loved by Allah to be a believer from the people of good, as He knows; and the disbeliever is also willed to be a disbeliever as He knows, from the people of evil, and He loves that to be so as He knows." He used to say the same regarding pleasure, election, and choice, and he would qualify the wording with this so that error is not imagined in it.

End of quotation. What the people of Hadith and Sunnah, all of them, the jurists entirely, the majority of the theologians (mutakallimun), and the Sufis hold is that Allah, glory be to Him, hates some substances, actions, and attributes even though they occur by His will. He detests them and abhors them, just as He detests the essence of Iblis and the essences of his armies, and detests their deeds, and does not love that, even though it exists by His will. Allah, Exalted, said:

﴿And Allah does not love corruption.﴾

And He said:

﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.﴾

And He said:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful.﴾

And He said:

﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged.﴾

And He said:

﴿And do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors.﴾

And He said:

﴿If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is free from need of you; and He does not approve for His servants disbelief.﴾

So this is a report of His not loving these matters and His not being pleased with them after they occur. This is explicit in refuting the view of those who interpret the texts to mean that He does not love them from those who did not commit them, but loves them when they occur, so that He loves them from the one who committed them and does not love them from the one who did not. This is among the greatest falsehood and lies against Allah. Rather, He, glory be to Him, hates them and detests them before their occurrence, at the time of their occurrence, and after their occurrence, for they are ugly and vile things, and Allah is exalted above loving the ugly and the vile. Indeed, He is the most hateful thing to Him. Allah, Exalted, said:

﴿All of that — its evil is hateful in the sight of your Lord.﴾

He, glory be to Him, has also informed that He hates the acts of obedience of the hypocrites, and for this reason He discourages them from them. So how could He love their hypocrisy and be pleased with it, and that its people would be beloved to Him, chosen by Him, and pleasing to Him? From this false principle arose their doctrine that actions are equal in relation to the Lord, glory be to Him, and that they are not divided in themselves into good and evil. Thus there is no difference in relation to Him, glory be to Him, between gratitude and disbelief. For this reason they said that thanking Him for His blessings is not obligatory by reason. On this principle they said that His will is identical with His love, that whatever He wills is beloved to Him, pleasing to Him, chosen and preferred by Him. After establishing this principle, they could not say that He hates the substances and actions that He created and loves some of them. Rather, whatever He does and creates is beloved to Him, and what is hated and detested is what He does not will and does not create. They founded this principle only out of concern to protect the decree (qadar). They made it the basis for the Sharia and the decree, and they bound themselves to its implications, by which they cast doubt upon the decree and wisdom, and by which they defied clear reason. They equated the most ugly of ugly things with the most beautiful of good deeds in reality, and said: "They are equal; there is no difference between them except by mere command and prohibition." So lying, oppression, transgression, and aggression are, in their view, equal in reality to truthfulness, justice, and beneficence. In this there is nothing that requires the goodness of the one or the badness of the other. They made this doctrine a slogan of the People of the Sunnah, and held that the opposite view is the view of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah), such as the Mu'tazilah and others. By the life of Allah, it is among the most false of doctrines, and the most contrary to reason, to the Sharia, and to the natural disposition (fitrah) with which Allah created His creatures. We have shown its falsehood in more than fifty ways in the book *al-Miftah* (Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah).

The point is that when this doctrine was combined with the claim that He, glory be to Him, does not love some things and hate others, but that every existing thing is beloved to Him and every non-existent thing is hated by Him, and when to these two was added the denial of wisdom and of the purposes sought in His acts, glory be to Him, and that He does nothing for any reason whatsoever, and to that was added the denial of causes, that He does nothing through anything, and the denial of natural powers, natural dispositions, and instincts, and that they can be causes or have any effect, the door of correctness in matters of the decree was closed to them. They bound themselves to these false principles with implications that are even more evidently false and corrupt. These implications are, from the outset, evidence of the corruption and falsehood of these principles, for the corruption of a implication is from the corruption of what implies it.

[Section: Encouraging treatment and linking causes to their effects]

Muslim reported in his *Sahih*, from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "For every disease there is a cure. When the cure of the disease is applied, it is healed by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

In the *Two Sahihs* (Bukhari and Muslim), from ʿAta', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has not sent down any disease except that He has sent down for it a cure."

In the *Musnad* of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of Ziyad ibn ʿIlaqah, from Usamah ibn Sharik, who said: "I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) when the Bedouins came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall we seek treatment?' He said: 'Yes, O servants of Allah, seek treatment, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not placed any disease except that He has placed for it a cure, except one disease.' They said: 'What is it?' He said: 'Old age (al-haram).'"

In another wording: "Indeed Allah has not sent down any disease except that He has sent down for it a cure; whoever knows it knows it, and whoever is ignorant of it is ignorant of it."

In the *Musnad*, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not sent down any disease except that He has sent down for it a cure; whoever knows it knows it, and whoever is ignorant of it is ignorant of it."

In the *Musnad* and the *Sunan*, from Abu Khuzamah, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of the incantations (ruqa) we seek as remedy, the medicines we use for treatment, and the precautions we take to guard against harm: do they turn back anything of the decree of Allah?' He said: 'They are part of the decree of Allah.'"

These hadiths include the affirmation of causes and their effects, and the nullification of the view of whoever denies them. It is possible that his saying, "For every disease there is a cure," is general in its meaning, so that it includes fatal diseases and diseases which no physician can cure. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made for them remedies that cure them, but He concealed their knowledge from mankind and did not make a way to it for them, for there is no knowledge for creatures except what Allah has taught them. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) tied healing to the coincidence of the medicine with the disease, for nothing among created things lacks an opposite, and every disease has an opposite medicine by which it is treated. So the Prophet (ﷺ) tied recovery to the agreement of the disease with the medicine, and this is an additional matter beyond the mere existence of the medicine. For when the medicine exceeds the degree of the disease in quality, or increases beyond what is appropriate in quantity, it transfers it to another disease; and when it falls short of it, it does not suffice to resist it, and the treatment remains deficient. When the one treating does not hit upon the medicine, or the medicine does not hit upon the disease, healing does not occur. When the time is not suitable for that medicine, it does not benefit. When the body is not receptive to it, or the strength is incapable of bearing it, or there is an obstacle preventing its effect, healing does not occur because of the failure of coincidence. When the coincidence is complete, healing occurs by the permission of Allah without fail. This is the better of the two interpretations of the hadith.

The second: that it is of the general meaning intended to be specific, especially since what is included in the wording is many times what is excluded from it. This is used in every language, and the intended meaning is that Allah has not placed any disease that accepts a remedy except that He has placed for it a remedy. Thus the diseases that do not accept a remedy are not included in this. This is like His saying, Exalted, about the wind which He sent upon the people of ʿAd:

﴿It destroys everything by the command of its Lord﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 25]

That is, everything that accepts destruction; it is in the nature of the wind to destroy it. Its parallels are many.

Whoever reflects on the creation of opposites in this world, and on the resistance of some of them to others, the repelling of some by others, and the empowering of some over others, will see the perfection of the power of the Lord, Exalted, His wisdom, His perfect craftsmanship in what He made, His singularity in lordship, oneness, and dominion, and that everything other than Him has what opposes and restrains it, just as He is self-sufficient in His essence while everything other than Him is needy in its essence.

In the authentic hadiths there is the command to seek treatment, and that it does not contradict reliance upon Allah (tawakkul), just as it does not contradict warding off the affliction of hunger, thirst, heat, and cold with their opposites. Indeed, the reality of tawhid is not complete except by engaging in the causes which Allah has set as necessary means to their effects, both by decree and by Sharia. Neglecting them harms the very essence of tawakkul, just as it harms the command and wisdom, and weakens it in a way that the one who neglects them imagines that abandoning them is stronger in tawakkul. For abandoning them out of incapacity contradicts tawakkul, whose reality is the heart's reliance upon Allah for obtaining what benefits the servant in his religion and his worldly life, and for warding off what harms him in his religion and his worldly life. With this reliance there must necessarily be engagement in the causes, or else one would be neglecting wisdom and the Sharia. So the servant should not make his incapacity into tawakkul, nor his tawakkul into incapacity.

In these hadiths there is also a refutation of whoever denies treatment and says: "If healing has been decreed, treatment is of no benefit; and if it has not been decreed, it is likewise." Furthermore, the illness occurred by the decree of Allah, and the decree of Allah cannot be repelled or turned back. This is the question which the Bedouins raised to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). As for the most eminent Companions, they were more knowledgeable about Allah, His wisdom, and His attributes than to raise such a question. The Prophet (ﷺ) answered them with what healed and sufficed: "These remedies, incantations, and precautions are part of the decree of Allah. Nothing comes out of His decree. Rather, His decree is repelled by His decree." This repelling is itself part of His decree. So there is no way to escape His decree in any respect. This is like repelling the decree of hunger, thirst, heat, and cold with their opposites, and like repelling the decree of the enemy by jihad. Each of these is part of the decree of Allah: the repeller, the repelled, and the repelling.

And it is said to the one who raises this question: "This obliges you not to engage in any of the causes by which you bring benefit or ward off harm. For if benefit and harm have been decreed, they must occur; and if they have not been decreed, there is no way for them to occur." In that lies the ruin of religion and worldly life and the corruption of the world. This is said only by one who rejects the truth and opposes it, who mentions the decree in order to repel the proof of the one who is right against him, like the idolaters who said: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers" [al-An'am: 148], and "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped besides Him anything, neither we nor our fathers" [al-Nahl: 35]. They said this to repel Allah's proof against them through the Messengers.

The answer to this questioner is to say: there remains a third category you have not mentioned. It is that God has decreed such-and-such by this cause. If you bring the cause, the effect occurs; otherwise it does not. If he says: "If God has decreed the cause for me, I will do it, and if He has not decreed it for me, I will not be able to do it,"

it is said: Would you accept this argument from your servant, your child, or your employee, if he used it against you concerning what you commanded him and forbade him, and then disobeyed you? If you accept it, then do not blame the one who disobeys you, takes your wealth, slanders your honour, and neglects your rights. And if you do not accept it, how could it be accepted from you as a defence against your obligations to God?

It has been related in an Israelite narration (isra'iliyyat, narrations traced to Israelite sources) that Ibrahim al-Khalil said: "My Lord, from whom is the disease?" He said: "From Me." He said: "Then from whom is the cure?" He said: "From Me." He said: "Then what of the physician?" He said: "A man through whose hands I send the cure."

In the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "For every disease there is a cure" is a strengthening of the soul of the patient and of the physician, and an incitement to seek that cure and to search for it. For when the soul of the patient perceives that his disease has a cure that will remove it, his heart clings to the spirit of hope, the heat of despair cools within him, and the door of hope opens for him. When his soul grows strong, his innate heat (al-hararah al-ghariziyyah, the natural inborn warmth) is stirred, and this becomes a cause for the strength of the vital spirits (al-arwah al-hayawaniyyah), the psychic spirits (al-arwah al-nafsaniyyah), and the natural spirits (al-arwah al-tabi'iyyah). When these spirits grow strong, the faculties that carry them grow strong, and they overcome the disease and drive it away.

Likewise, when the physician knows that this disease has a cure, he is able to seek it and search for it. The diseases of bodies are in the same measure as the diseases of hearts, and God has not placed a sickness in the heart without placing for it a cure through its opposite. If the owner of the disease knows it and applies it, and it meets the disease of his heart, it heals him by God's permission, may He be exalted.

Then He informed that He has the conclusive proof (al-hujjah al-baligha), which reaches the core of the heart, mixes with the intellect and becomes united with it, so the intellect cannot repel it or deny it. Then He informed that He, glorified is He, is able to guide all of His creation, and if He willed that, He would do it, owing to the perfection of His power and the pervasiveness of His will. But His wisdom refuses that, and His justice refuses to punish anyone and seize him without proof. So He established the proof, varied the signs (al-ayat), struck the parables (al-amthal), and diversified the evidences (al-adillah). Had all creation been upon one single way of guidance, these matters would not have come about, nor would these evidences and parables have been diversified, nor would the might of He, glorified is He, have appeared in His vengeance upon His enemies and His victory of His friends over them, nor would His proofs which He established for the truthfulness of His prophets and messengers have appeared, and there would not have been a sign for people in the two groups that met: a group fighting in the way of Allah, and another group of disbelievers whom they saw as twice their number with their own eyes. Nor would there have been for creation a lasting sign as long as the world endures, concerning the matter of Musa and his people, Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his people, and the splitting of the sea for them, their all entering it together, then the rescue of Musa and his people, none of whom drowned, while Fir'awn and his people were drowned, none of whom was saved. So this making Himself known to His servants, these signs, and this might and wisdom have no way to be nullified at all, and they do not exist without their necessary consequences.

The way of God and His straight path is that which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions followed, as shown by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the Wise Qur'an, indeed you are among the messengers, on a straight path﴾ [Ya-Sin: 1-4]. And He said: ﴿And indeed you are upon a straight guidance﴾ [al-Hajj: 67], and He said: ﴿Indeed you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. Whoever follows the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in his words and deeds is upon the straight path of God, and he is among those whom God loves and whose sins He forgives. Whoever opposes him in his words or deeds is an innovator (mubtadi', one who introduces innovation in religion) following the way of Satan, and is not among those whom God has promised Paradise, forgiveness and excellence.

(Benefit)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, lest they separate you from His way﴾.

Here He gathered the paths of falsehood in the plural and made His way, the truth, singular. This is not contradicted by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By it God guides whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 16].

For those are the paths of His pleasure, which are gathered under His one way and His straight path. All the paths of His pleasure return to one path and one way, and it is His way, to which there is no access except through them. It is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he drew a straight line and said: "This is the way of God." Then he drew lines to its right and to its left and said: "These are paths, over each of which is a devil calling to it." Then he recited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, lest they separate you from His way. That He has instructed you with, that you may become righteous﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

This is because the route that connects to God is one. It is what He sent His messengers with and what He revealed in His books. No one reaches Him except by this route, even if people come from every direction and seek entry from every door. For them the roads are blocked and the doors are closed, except this one route, for it is connected to God and leads to God.

If it is said: God, exalted is He, has said: ﴿There has come to you from God a light and a clear Book, by which God guides whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace﴾?

It is said: These are ways that are gathered into one way, and they are like the branches and roads on the main highway. These are the branches of faith (shu'ab al-iman), which faith gathers together, and faith is one branch, just as the trunk of a tree gathers its boughs and branches. These ways are answering the summons of the One who summons to God, by affirming His report and obeying His command. The way to Paradise is nothing but answering the one who calls to it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 6, verse 154:

His saying: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete, upon the one who did good﴾. He included in "tamam" (completion) the meaning of "in'am" (bestowing favor), and so he made it transitive with "ala" (upon), meaning: a favor from Us upon the one who did good. This is a recompense for acts of obedience with acts of obedience.

**(Benefit)**

God the Exalted says: ﴿Then he shall have ten times as much﴾. He made the number of the multiples feminine because it refers to good deeds (ḥasanāt).

Similar to this is Abu al-'Aliya's reading: ﴿its faith will not benefit a soul﴾, with the feminine verb referring to faith (īmān). Yet faith here means obedience and reward in meaning.

**[Chapter: The Degrees of Contentment (ridā)]**

**[The First Degree: The Contentment of the General Public]**

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree is the contentment of the general public: being content with God as Lord, and abhorring the worship of anything other than Him. This is the pivot of the millstone of Islam (quṭb raḥā al-Islām), and it purifies one from major shirk (al-shirk al-akbar).

Being content with God as Lord means that one does not take as lord anyone other than God Exalted, one does not rest on the management of another, and one does not bring one's needs to another. God Exalted said: ﴿Say: Shall I seek a lord other than God, when He is the Lord of all things?﴾ [Al-An'am: 164]. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: "Master and deity." That is, how could I seek a lord other than Him when He is the Lord of all things? He also said at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Say: Shall I take as a protector (walī) other than God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?﴾ [Al-An'am: 14], meaning worshipped one, helper, aider, and refuge. This belongs to the kind of allegiance (muwālāh) that includes love and obedience. He also said in its middle: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, detailed?﴾ [Al-An'am: 114], that is: shall I seek other than God someone to judge between me and you, so that we may go to him for judgment regarding what we differ about? This is His Book, the chief of judges. How, then, would we go to judgment other than His Book, when He has sent it down detailed, clear, sufficient, and healing?

When you deeply reflect on these three verses, you will see that they are the very essence of being content with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (ﷺ) as messenger. You will also see that the hadith expresses this and is derived from it. Many people are content with God as Lord and do not seek any lord besides Him, yet they are not content with Him alone as protector and helper. Rather, they take other protectors besides Him, thinking that these bring them closer to God, and that their allegiance is like the allegiance of the king's close courtiers. This is the very essence of shirk. True monotheism (al-tawḥīd) is that one does not take protectors besides Him.

The Qur'an is full of describing the polytheists as having taken protectors besides Him.

This is different from the allegiance to His prophets, messengers, and the believing servants among them, for that belongs to the completeness of faith and to the completeness of allegiance to Him. The allegiance to His friends (awliyā') is one kind, and taking a protector besides Him is another kind. Whoever does not understand the distinction between the two should seek monotheism from its foundation, for this issue is the root and basis of monotheism.

Many people seek other than Him as a judge, to whom they resort, whom they dispute before, and whose judgment they accept. These three stations are the pillars of monotheism: not taking anyone other than Him as lord, nor as deity, nor seeking any judge other than Him.

The explanation of being content with God as Lord is that one abhors the worship of anything besides Him. This is being content with God as Lord, and it is part of the completeness of being content with God as Lord. Whoever is given to be content with Him as Lord in its full right will abhor the worship of anything besides Him, certainly. This is because contentment with the singularity of His lordship necessarily entails the singularity of His worship, just as knowledge of the oneness of lordship (tawḥīd al-rubūbiyyah) necessarily entails knowledge of the oneness of divinity (tawḥīd al-ulūhiyyah).

As for his saying "it is the pivot of the millstone of Islam," he means that the axis of the millstone of Islam rests on the servant being content to worship his Lord alone, and abhorring the worship of other than Him. It has already been mentioned that worship ('ibādah) is love together with submission. So whoever you humble yourself to, obey, and love besides God, you are worshipping him.

As for his saying "it purifies from major shirk," he means that shirk is of two kinds: major and minor. This contentment purifies its possessor from the major kind. As for the minor kind, it is purified by his standing at ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [Al-Fatiha: 5].

**[Chapter]**

He said: It is valid with three conditions: that God, Mighty and Majestic, be the most beloved of things to the servant, the most deserving of things of glorification, and the most worthy of things of obedience.

That is, this kind of contentment is also valid only with three things.

The first of them: that God, Mighty and Majestic, be the most beloved thing to the servant. This is also known by three things:

The first: that His love precedes every love in the heart, so that His love comes before all loves.

The second: that His love overpowers every love, so that His love in the heart is prior and dominant, while the love of others is subordinate, overpowered, defeated, and folded into His love.

The third: that the love of others is subordinate to His love. He is then the beloved in essence and in the primary intention, and others are beloved only as a consequence of loving Him, just as they are obeyed only as a consequence of obeying Him. He is, in reality, the one obeyed and the one beloved.

These three also apply to His being the most deserving of glorification and obedience.

The summary: God alone should be the beloved, the glorified, and the obeyed. Whoever does not love Him, obey Him, or glorify Him is arrogant toward Him. Whenever one loves, glorifies, or obeys anything alongside Him, that one is a polytheist. Whenever one singles Him out alone with love, glorification, and obedience, that one is a monotheist servant. God, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

**[Chapter: The Second Degree: Contentment with God]**

He said: The second degree is contentment with God (al-riḍā 'an Allāh). The verses of revelation speak of this. It is being content with Him in all that He decrees and destines. This is among the first paths of the elite (ahl al-khuṣūṣ).

In the authentic divine hadith: "God, Mighty and Majestic, says: My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than performing what I have made obligatory upon him." This shows that drawing near to Him, Glorified, through performing His obligations is better and higher than drawing near to Him through supererogatory acts.

Also: being content with Him as Lord entails and necessitates being content with Him. Contentment with His lordship is the servant's contentment with what He commands him, forbids him, allots him, destines for him, gives him, and withholds from him. Whoever is not content with all of that has not been content with Him as Lord in every respect, even if he is content with Him as Lord in some respects. Being content with Him as Lord in every respect necessarily entails being content with Him, and includes it without doubt.

Also: being content with Him as Lord relates to His essence, His attributes, His names, and His lordship in general and in particular. It is being content with Him as Creator and Manager, as Commander and Forbidder, as King, Giver and Withholder, as Judge, Guardian and Protector, as Helper and Aider, as Sufficient, Reckoner and Watchful, as Tester and Pardoner, as Restrainer and Expander, and according to the rest of the attributes of His lordship.

As for being content with Him in the sense of contentment with Him (riḍā 'an-hu), it is the servant's contentment with what He does to him and gives him. For this reason, it is only mentioned in connection with reward and recompense, as in His saying, Exalted: ﴿O soul at rest, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [Al-Fajr: 27]. This is with her contentment with Him because of the honor that she attained from Him. Likewise His saying: ﴿Abiding therein forever. God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾ [Al-Bayyina: 8].

Being content with Him (al-riḍā bihi) is the root of being content with Him in the other sense (al-riḍā 'anhu), and being content with Him in that sense is the fruit of being content with Him as Lord.

The secret of the matter is that being content with Him relates to His names and attributes, while being content with Him in the other sense relates to His reward and recompense.

Also: the Prophet (ﷺ) linked tasting the sweetness of faith to whoever is content with God as Lord, and he did not link it to whoever is content with Him in the other sense. As he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is content with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (ﷺ) as messenger has tasted the sweetness of faith." He thus made being content with Him accompany being content with His religion and His Prophet. These three are the foundations of Islam, on which it stands and by which it stands.

Also: being content with Him as Lord includes affirming His oneness and worshipping Him, turning to Him in repentance, relying upon Him, fearing Him, hoping in Him, loving Him, and being patient for Him and through Him. Gratitude for His blessings involves seeing everything from Him as a blessing and a kindness, even if His servant is harmed. So being content with Him includes the testimony that there is no deity but God. Being content with Muhammad as messenger includes the testimony that Muhammad is the messenger of God. Being content with Islam as religion includes committing to its servitude to Him and obeying Him and His messenger. These three together encompass the whole religion.
